title: Content Marketing Virtual Assistant
description: Ultimate Stadium Sak® is a growing U.S.-based e-commerce brand behind a patented wearable sleeping bag designed for sports spectators and outdoor families. We're looking for a creative, organized, and reliable Content Marketing Virtual Assistant to help execute our weekly social media, Pinterest, and blog content. We need someone with a strong eye for design who knows how to execute polished, on-brand content across Instagram, Facebook, and Pinterest. This is a content creation and execution role — not a marketing strategy or copywriting role. How the Role Works We provide you with everything you need to create great content: Weekly content strategy and calendar Post topics and concepts Most captions/copy Blog copy Photos and video footage Brand guidelines Product information Pinterest direction Your job is to take that direction and turn it into beautiful, polished, on-brand content — and make sure it's published correctly. You should be someone who can take an idea and run with it without needing detailed instructions for every design decision. Weekly Social Media Responsibilities Create approximately 3 feed posts per week, including: 3 short-form Reels 3 static graphics or carousels Reel covers when needed Daily Instagram/Facebook Story content, generally 3–5 frames You will: Edit provided video footage into engaging Reels Add appropriate text, music, transitions, and captions Design clean, elevated graphics and carousels Repurpose existing content when appropriate Create Story graphics from weekly content Maintain consistent branding Prepare and schedule approved content Pinterest + Blog Responsibilities Each week: Format and publish approximately 1 provided blog post Create 1 Pinterest Pin connected to the weekly blog Create approximately 2 additional static Pinterest Pins Add appropriate Pinterest titles, descriptions, links, and boards Make sure all Pins link to the correct destination Pinterest experience is important. We're looking for someone who understands that Pinterest is a visual search platform, not simply another social media feed. Content Scheduling We use Metricool to organize and schedule content. You'll be responsible for: Loading approved content Scheduling Instagram, Facebook, and Pinterest content Checking captions, links, graphics, and formatting Confirming scheduled content publishes correctly Keeping the content calendar current Experience with Metricool is helpful but not required if you're comfortable learning new software. Content Organization You'll also help maintain an organized content library including: Raw video Product photography Customer content/UGC Archived footage Finished Reels Graphics Pinterest designs Blog images Previously published content Organization and attention to detail are extremely important for this role. Required Skills You should be highly comfortable with: Canva Short-form video editing Instagram Reels Instagram and Facebook content Pinterest Graphic design Social media scheduling Google Drive Basic website/blog formatting Following an established brand style Experience with Shopify blogs and Metricool is strongly preferred. You should also have excellent written English and be able to communicate clearly with a U.S.-based business. Design Style Our visual style is: Clean Modern Elevated Warm Lifestyle-focused Sporty without looking juvenile We are not looking for overly busy graphics, clip-art-style sports designs, or content that looks obviously AI-generated. A strong visual eye is very important for this position. Compensation The starting rate for this position is $2.35/hour. Please only apply if you are comfortable with this rate.

title: Amazon Catalog Specialist
description: Amazon Catalog & PPC Specialist Listings, FBA Logistics, PPC Employment Type: Remote, Full-Time | Reports To: Ecommerce Operations Manager About the Role We're a growing multi-marketplace ecommerce business (Amazon, Etsy, Walmart, eBay) selling novelty apparel, drinkware, custom gift sets, and seasonal/occasion-driven products. We're looking for a hands-on Amazon specialist who can independently manage listing optimization, FBA inventory planning, and PPC campaigns — someone who understands the mechanics behind the numbers, not just how to follow a checklist. This is not an entry-level data-entry role. You'll be trusted with live pricing, inventory decisions with real financial consequences, and campaign budgets. Accuracy and accountability matter more than speed. Core Responsibilities Listing Creation & SEO Optimization • Create new Amazon listings from scratch and optimize existing ones (titles, bullets, backend search terms) following A9 algorithm best practices • Conduct keyword research using tools like Helium 10 (Cerebro, Magnet) and prioritize by conversion signal, not just raw search volume • Maintain listing compliance with Amazon content policies, character limits, and trademark restrictions • Optimize existing listings based on performance data and seasonal relevance • Add and manage listing videos and enhanced content to improve conversion • Communicate clearly and proactively — flag issues, scope changes, and confirm before acting on anything with broad or irreversible impact FBA Inventory & Shipment Management • Project FBA order quantities based on sales velocity, sell-through rate, and upcoming seasonal demand • Build and upload FBA shipment plans, including flat file creation and upload • Monitor inventory health metrics (IPI score, days of supply, excess/aged inventory) and take corrective action before problems compound • Understand and correctly manage the distinction between FBA and FBM (merchant-fulfilled) listings — including the operational and financial implications of converting between the two • Flag stockout or overstock risk ahead of key seasonal windows Flat File & Catalog Management • Confidently build, edit, and upload Amazon flat files (Price & Quantity, Inventory, Listings templates) without introducing catalog-wide errors • Understand the difference between List Price and Sale Price fields, including Sale Start/End Date behavior, before making bulk pricing changes • Double-check bulk changes against a defined SKU list before uploading — no catalog-wide edits without explicit scope confirmation • Troubleshoot and resolve flat file upload errors PPC Campaign Management • Create and optimize Sponsored Products campaigns (auto/manual, exact/phrase/broad match structures) • Analyze PPC reports to identify underperforming keywords, budget drains, and scaling opportunities • Manage bids with attention to ACOS, CTR, and conversion efficiency — not spend alone • Tie PPC strategy to seasonal demand windows and product launch timing Required Qualifications • Demonstrated hands-on experience managing Amazon Seller Central (not just Vendor Central or general "Amazon experience") • Proven experience with Amazon flat file editing and bulk uploads • Working knowledge of FBA logistics: shipment creation, inventory planning, IPI score factors • Clear understanding of FBA vs. FBM operational differences and when/how to convert between them • Experience running and optimizing Amazon PPC campaigns with real budget accountability • Familiarity with keyword research tools (Helium 10, Jungle Scout, or similar) • High attention to detail — this role directly affects live pricing and inventory with real financial impact • Comfortable asking clarifying questions before making bulk or irreversible changes, rather than guessing • Strong written communicator — able to clearly explain issues, scope, and status without back-and-forth Preferred Qualifications • Experience across multiple marketplaces (Etsy, Walmart, eBay) • Experience with novelty, gift, or seasonal/occasion-driven product categories • Familiarity with Amazon compliance issues (trademark, IP, safety violations) and how to resolve them Put ORANGE on the "SUBJECT TITLE" for keywords What Success Looks Like in This Role • Bulk pricing or catalog changes are scoped, confirmed, and verified before and after upload — no unintended catalog-wide impact • FBA shipments are timed and sized correctly against seasonal demand, with no avoidable stockouts or excess inventory • PPC spend is monitored proactively, with issues (like bid-floor errors or underperformers) caught early, not after significant spend • Listings are optimized based on real keyword and conversion data, not guesswork

title: AI Video Producer & Editor - UGC, VSL & Animation Ads
job_title: AI Video Producer & Editor - UGC, VSL & Animation Ads
description: AI VIDEO PRODUCER & EDITOR - UGC, VSL & ANIMATION ADS Remote | Project based, paid per batch | Start: ASAP | $40 - $110 per batch READ THIS FIRST This job post is long. That is on purpose. I am hiring ONE person. I would rather get 5 serious applications than 200 lazy ones. If you send the same message to 40 job posts a day, close this now - you will not get through. But please do not be scared off either. You will not be inventing anything. You get the script, the reference ad, the format specs and every tool paid for. What you need is to already be good at this, and to deliver on time. If that sounds like you, keep reading. ABOUT US We run five direct-response e-commerce brands on Shopify. We sell physical products to customers in the United States, and we advertise on Facebook and Instagram at a four-figure daily budget. Every single ad we run is produced with AI. No film crew, no studio, no actors. That is the whole model. THE BIG IDEA - WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL EDITING JOB Right now our creative output is the bottleneck. Not the budget, not the products, not the audience - the number of finished ads we can put in front of people. That is a strange and very specific problem to have: we can fund more ad spend than we can produce ads for. Every week we do not ship enough new creatives is a week we leave money on the table, because in paid advertising creatives burn out. An ad that prints money today is tired in three weeks, and if there is nothing new to replace it, the whole account cools down. So the number of ads you deliver is not a production statistic. It is the ceiling on how big this business can get. That is the job. Concretely: we want to go from a handful of finished ads per week to 15-20 finished ads per week within your first 60 days, without the quality dropping. This is a doer role, not a manager role. You produce. Nobody reports to you and you do not build a team. If that changes later, it changes because you made it obvious that it should. WHAT YOU WILL PRODUCE You must be able to produce all of these yourself: - AI UGC ads - a generated person on camera showing and talking about a product - VSL edits - longer sales videos cut to a script we give you - AI voiceover - written, generated and timed to the cut - Cartoon and claymation ads - stylized animation, not photoreal - 1:1 ad iterations - this one matters most, see below - The cut itself - captions burned in, clean sans-serif, inside the safe zone, hook in the first two seconds, no dead air, exported to spec Strongly preferred on top of that: Suno-style music ads where a song carries the ad, talking-head avatar ads, and Disney-style animation. About the 1:1 iterations, because this is the majority of the work and it is where people drop out: we hand you an ad that already works and you rebuild it exactly, changing one variable. Same structure, same pacing, same feel, different hook or different actor. If the reference has a cut on beat four, your version has a cut on beat four. "Close enough" is not a delivery. If you need creative freedom to stay motivated, you will not enjoy this role - and we would both rather find that out now. WHAT A BATCH IS We work in batches, not in hours. BATCH A - Cut only. Ten finished ads from clips and product footage we send you. 15-30 seconds, vertical 9:16. BATCH B - Full production. Three to five finished ads, generated and cut by you from a script. Usually one concept with hook variations. Right now we run 3-4 batches per week. That number grows as we scale, and we want the person who grows with it. Turnaround: a batch is delivered within 48 hours of receiving the brief and the assets. STOP. READ THIS PART CAREFULLY. Put the word ORANGE in your subject line, exactly like this: ORANGE - Your Full Name Send it to ---------- - not through the OnlineJobs.ph message system. If ORANGE is not in your subject line we will never see your message, no matter how good your portfolio is. This is not a joke and there is no exception. Most applicants will fail this, and that is fine. ACCOUNTABILITY AND COMMUNICATION This is the part we care about most, so we are going to be very clear. We are not looking for someone who never has a problem. Everybody gets sick. Power goes out. Family emergencies happen. Typhoons happen. We have zero problem with any of that. What we have a problem with is silence. If you are ill, if your internet dies, if a render fails and the batch will be late - send us one message. Before the deadline, not after it. That is all we ask, and if you do it, we will always find a solution together. Going quiet on a batch is the one thing that ends this immediately. Not because we are strict, but because we plan ad launches around your delivery date and we cannot plan around someone we have to chase. Beyond that, we expect three things: - You can already do this. We give you the tools, the budget, the script and the specs. We do not teach you the craft. If you are hoping to learn AI video generation on this job, this is the wrong job and we will both waste our time. - You ask before you produce. When a brief is unclear you ask first, instead of delivering five wrong ads and then explaining them. - You flag what will not work. If a script cannot be built visually, tell us before you start, not after the render. THE TOP THREE SKILLS WE ARE HIRING FOR 1. AI video generation - you already produce photoreal or stylized AI footage today, in production, not as an experiment 2. Short-form direct-response editing - you understand pacing, hooks, and why an ad dies in second three 3. Speed with consistency - you deliver on schedule, and batch number twelve looks like batch number one WHAT YOU MUST BRING (hard requirements) 1. 2+ years producing or editing short-form video, at least the last year with AI-generated footage. 2. You have shipped AI video in production - for clients, for a brand, or for your own offers. Not tutorials, not test renders. We want to see the actual ads. 3. CapCut or Premiere Pro for the cut, your pick, as long as the output is consistent. 4. Hands-on with at least one serious AI generation stack, and the judgment to know when a generation is unusable and needs to be redone instead of shipped. 5. You work in OUR generation stack, and that stack is built on Polaris. Read the tools section below before you apply - this is the one thing about our setup that is not up for discussion, and we would rather you know it now than on day one. 6. Conversational English, spoken and written. 7. Reliable internet, a machine that can handle the work, and the ability to hit a 48-hour turnaround. 8. Willing to sign a freelance contract and a short NDA before you get access to our assets. BONUS (not required, but it moves you to the top of the list) - You have already worked in Polaris, or in a comparable AI ad studio, and can tell us what it is good at and where it falls apart - You have produced paid ads before, not just organic content - After Effects - ElevenLabs or comparable voice tools - You have built your own generation workflow and can explain why it is faster than the obvious one - Music-driven ads, avatar ads, Disney-style animation THE TOOLS WE USE We pay for everything, including every single generation. You never pay for a credit or a subscription. POLARIS IS THE CORE OF OUR STACK, AND WORKING IN IT IS PART OF THE JOB. Polaris ( ---------- ) is an AI ad studio built specifically for e-commerce: you give it a product URL or a product image and it produces UGC-style video and image ads. It generates the footage, it generates the AI actors, it writes the captions, and its ad cloner rebuilds an existing winning ad with one variable changed. That last part is exactly the 1:1 iteration work described above, which is the majority of what you will do here - which is why we picked it. We have tested the alternatives. Polaris is faster and cheaper per finished ad than anything else we ran, and that difference is the whole reason this role exists at the volume it does. So this is not a preference we will negotiate away: if you come on board, you produce in Polaris. You do NOT need previous Polaris experience. We do not expect anyone to have used it for years - it is new. We pay for the account, and if you already know your way around any modern AI generation tool, you will be productive in it within a day or two. What we do need is that you are genuinely willing to move into our stack instead of insisting on the workflow you already have. If that is a dealbreaker for you, this is the wrong role and we would both rather find out before the call. Around Polaris we also work with Magnific and Higgsfield for generation, ElevenLabs for voice, and CapCut for the cut. Those we are flexible on: if you have a faster way to get to the same output, bring it and we will look at it together on the call. Polaris is the fixed point, the rest is open. Communication runs on Telegram and email. Files live in a shared asset library with a fixed folder structure and naming convention. WHAT WE PROVIDE - Every tool account and every generation, fully paid - Polaris included. You never spend your own money on this job. - The script for every ad - you never write copy - Format specs and reference ads, so "done" is never a guess - A proper shared asset library. You will not be hunting for files. - One revision round per batch, with specific feedback, not vague feedback - Direct access to the person making the decisions. No account manager, no layers. WORKING STYLE AND WHERE THIS ROLE IS GOING - Fully remote. We do not care where you sit. - The work itself is asynchronous. No shift, no fixed working hours, no being on call. You get a brief, you deliver a batch within 48 hours, and how you organize your day is your business. - No overlap with our time zone required for the work. We are in Europe and Asia; you will not be asked to work nights. - One fixed 30-minute call per week, camera on. We agree on the day and time together once you start, and then it stays there. That is where we go through what landed and what did not, where the revisions keep coming from, what you need from us, and what we want produced next. You get direct feedback and we expect you to use it. We also expect you to tell us when a brief is bad or a spec makes no sense - that call goes both ways. - This is high tempo. We are a small operation scaling paid ads aggressively, priorities move, and a batch that was due Friday is due Friday. If you need a slow, predictable environment, this is not it. - Where this is going: volume grows as we scale. More batches per week, higher rates, and first pick of the work. Long-term is the point - we are not looking for a one-off gig, we want one person who gets faster every month. HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED Five numbers, nothing else: 1. Batches delivered per week 2. Turnaround time per batch - target: under 48 hours 3. Revision rounds per batch - target: one or fewer 4. Spec compliance - correct format, safe zone, naming, folder 5. Iteration accuracy - does your 1:1 rebuild actually match the reference We do not measure hours. We do not measure how hard something was. COMPENSATION (all amounts in USD) You are paid per delivered batch. Not per hour, not per month. We start low and we go up fast, and we are honest about that instead of promising you a number we do not know you are worth yet. STARTING RATE - your first batches: Batch A (10 finished cuts): $40 Batch B (3-5 full productions): $70 AFTER 4 ACCEPTED BATCHES, delivered on time and to spec: Batch A: $60 Batch B: $110 We review again after that. If you are fast and consistent, the rate keeps moving up. This is not a carrot we dangle - it is how we pay everyone who works with us long-term. At 3-4 batches per week that is roughly $1,400 to $1,800 per month once you are past the starting rate, and the volume is growing. Also included: - Paid on delivery of each accepted batch, every time, no delays. Wise or PayPal, your choice. - Every tool, every subscription and every generation credit paid by us - Bonuses when the business does well - when we grow, you grow - No equity and no revenue share. This is paid work with a clear rate. Why we start low: we have been burned by portfolios that did not match the actual output. Four batches is enough for both of us to know whether this works. If you are as good as your portfolio says, you are at the higher rate within two weeks. ENGLISH Your portfolio tells us nothing about your English - the voice on those ads was generated. So we ask separately. Two steps, and we are open about both. First, the short recording you send with your application: that is how we hear you before anyone spends time on a call. Then a video call in English, camera on, before we hire anyone. You need to be able to hold a normal working conversation - understand a brief, ask a question back, say when something will not work. Written English alone is not enough. We have been burned by exactly this before and we are not doing it again. HOW TO APPLY Send your application to ---------- with ORANGE in the subject line. Keep it short. We are not asking you to do unpaid work to apply - nothing below takes more than ten minutes, and nothing below is work you have to invent for us. Be specific: vague answers are the fastest way to get rejected. 1. YOUR WORK. Links to 2-3 AI videos or ads YOU made. Own work only - no agency reels, no team projects, no "I was part of the team that". For each one, tell us which tools you used and what your part was. 2. YOUR SETUP AND YOUR SPEED. Which tools do you work in, and roughly how many finished 15-second ads can you produce in a working day? A real number, not "many". 3. POLARIS. One or two sentences, nothing more. Have you used Polaris ( ---------- ) before - yes or no? Either answer is fine, we are not filtering on it. What we want to know is whether you are willing to produce in it as your main tool, because that is how this role works. If you have used it, tell us what you built with it. 4. WHAT YOU WANT TO EARN per batch, for Batch A and for Batch B. 5. A 60-SECOND RECORDING OF YOURSELF SPEAKING ENGLISH. Loom, a voice message, an unlisted YouTube link, whatever is easiest. Introduce yourself and walk us through one of the videos you linked above: what you made, which tools, what was hard about it. No production, no script, no editing - phone camera or just audio is completely fine, and we mean that. This is the one thing you send us that is not supposed to look produced. We are not judging your setup or your confidence on camera. We want to hear how you speak English, because that d ---------- whether this works. Send it as a separate link from your portfolio links so we do not mix them up. That is it. No cover letter, no essay, no test task. If your work looks right and we can understand each other, we talk. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT 1. We look at your work and listen to your recording 2. Short video call in English, camera on 3. After the call: a small PAID test batch on a real brief, produced in Polaris. We set up your account and walk you through it first - the test measures whether you can hit a spec, not whether you can guess your way around a new interface. 4. Hire, starting rate, then the rate review after 4 accepted batches The test comes after we have spoken, not before. You get paid for it whether or not we hire you. We keep the number of tests small on purpose, so if you get there you are already a serious candidate. Applications that do not start correctly, or that skip any of the 5 points, will not be reviewed. We are strict about this on purpose: following a brief exactly is the single most important part of this job. We reply to every application that follows the instructions, and we reply fast. If this sounds like you, apply today. We are hiring one person and we are hiring quickly. Send to: ---------- - subject line: ORANGE - Your Full Name

title: Sales Development Representative – B2B Software
description: Sales Development Representative – B2B Software Remote | 20 Hours/Week | 10am-2pm EST About the Role We are looking for an experienced SDR to help our Canadian technology company who provides specialized point-of-sale and operational software to senior living and healthcare organizations across North America. Our platform helps organizations manage dining operations, resident billing, payments, ordering, reservations, reporting, and other important workflows. We are hiring an experienced Sales Development Representative to identify prospective customers, conduct outbound outreach, qualify opportunities, and book product demonstrations for our sales team. This is not a basic scripted call centre role. title: Customer Support VA - Shopify E-Commerce, AI-Assisted
job_title: Customer Support VA - Shopify E-Commerce, AI-Assisted
description: US MARKET EMAIL SUPPORT VA - SHOPIFY E-COMMERCE, AI-ASSISTED Remote | Part-time, about 2-3 hours per day (growing) | Start: ASAP | $2.50 - $4 per hour READ THIS FIRST This job post is long. That is on purpose. I am hiring ONE person. I would rather get 5 serious applications than 200 lazy ones. If you send the same message to 40 job posts a day, close this now - you will not get through. But please do not be scared off either. You will not be thrown into deep water alone. We have written SOPs for every situation, training videos of real past cases, I will train you, and we have a 1-on-1 call every single week. You do not need to invent anything. You need to be reliable, careful, and willing to learn our system. If that sounds like you, keep reading. ABOUT US We run five direct-response e-commerce brands on Shopify. We sell physical products to customers in the United States, and we advertise on Facebook and Instagram at a four-figure daily budget. Growth means more orders, and more orders mean more customer emails. That inbox is what we are hiring for. THE BIG IDEA - WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL SUPPORT JOB Acquiring a customer through paid ads is expensive. We pay for every single one before we ever make a cent. Now think about what happens when one of them writes to us and gets no answer for four days. They do not politely ask again. They open a PayPal dispute or they call their bank and do a chargeback. And that does not just cost us the order - it costs us the dispute fee, it costs us the product that is already on a plane, and if enough of them pile up it costs us the payment processor itself. A store that loses its payment provider is a store that is dead, no matter how good the ads are. That is the real math of this job. Every email you answer fast and properly is a dispute that never happens. You are not "answering tickets" - you are protecting the money at the exact point where it leaks out. A business is also like a house. Most people only build the front: the ads, the product page, the pretty pictures. Then the first storm comes and it falls over, because there is no foundation. The foundation is the backend. That is what you are. THE ROLE IN ONE SENTENCE You own the customer inbox across all five brands and you keep it at zero. This is not a typing job. You do not write every reply from scratch. We use AI to draft, and your job is to judge the draft, fix what reads robotic, check the facts in Shopify, and send. Editor and decision-maker, not typist. The number we hold you to: every customer email gets an answer within 24 hours. That is the whole scoreboard. Within 90 days we want you handling 80 percent of the inbox without asking us anything. This is a doer role. Nobody reports to you and you do not build a team. HOW THE DAY WORKS One focused block per day. You come in, you clear the inbox across all brands, you handle what you can handle, you flag what needs us, you send a short end-of-day note. Then you are done. Our customers are in the United States, so the inbox fills up overnight your time. You work your block in the morning, Philippine time, and everything that came in during the US evening is handled before it gets old. We are looking for one person long-term. Someone who gets faster and more independent every month, not someone who needs the same question answered twice. WHAT YOU WILL DO 1. CUSTOMER EMAILS (your main job) We currently handle around [MAIL-VOLUMEN] customer emails per week across all five brands. - Sweep the support inboxes across all five brands and clear them, every working day - Answer tracking questions ("where is my order") using our tracking tools and the order data in Shopify - Answer product and usage questions from our templates - Process returns, cancellations and address changes along our decision tree - Keep the inbox at zero. No email older than 24 hours. 2. CASES AND DISPUTES - Spot disputes early - PayPal cases, Klarna claims, chargebacks - and log every single one in our tracker with its deadline - Respond to the case: upload the tracking, assemble the evidence, write the response - Never let a deadline pass. A dispute we lose by default is money we simply hand over. 3. ADDRESS PROBLEMS - When an address is wrong, incomplete or undeliverable, you take it from there: you email the customer, you get the correct address, you update it in Shopify, and you confirm it back to our supplier. - We should not have to sit in the middle of that. You are the link. 4. PUSHING PROBLEMS BACK TO THE SOURCE (this one matters to us) You do not just fix problems for the customer. You push them back up the chain so they stop happening. If ten customers this week asked the same question, that is not ten tickets. That is one broken product page, and we want to know about it. If three packages arrived damaged, we do not want you to quietly send three replacements and move on - we want the order numbers, the photos, and the question of why it keeps happening. So you document it: what went wrong, how often, which orders. Then you bring it to the weekly call and we fix the cause instead of the symptom. Tell us when one of our templates, our processes or our product pages is bad. We built them and we will change them. Nobody here is attached to being right. To be clear about what this job is NOT: you do not order stock, you do not manage inventory, you do not do purchasing, you do not write marketing copy, and you never talk to a customer on the phone. Everything is written and asynchronous. STOP. READ THIS PART CAREFULLY. Start your message with the word TAMARIND, exactly like this: TAMARIND - Your Full Name Apply right here through OnlineJobs.ph. Do not email us - we read everything in this system and nowhere else. If TAMARIND is not the first thing in your message we will never see it, no matter how good your experience is. This is not a joke and there is no exception. Most applicants will fail this, and that is fine. ACCOUNTABILITY AND COMMUNICATION This is the part we care about most, so we are going to be very clear. We are not looking for someone who never has a problem. Everybody gets sick. Power goes out. Family emergencies happen. Typhoons happen. We have zero problem with any of that. What we have a problem with is silence. If you are ill, if your internet dies, if something happens in your family, if you simply cannot work today - send us one message. Before, not after. That is all we ask, and if you do it, we will always find a solution together. Disappearing without a word is the one thing that ends this immediately. Not because we are strict about hours, but because we cannot run a business on someone we have to chase. Beyond that, we expect three things: - You work independently. You do not need to be reminded or micromanaged. - You own the outcome. An escalation comes to us with your recommendation attached, not as a forwarded email that says "what should I do". - You are honest when you do not know. A wrong answer sent confidently to a customer costs us a dispute. "I need to check this" costs us nothing. THE TOP THREE SKILLS WE ARE HIRING FOR 1. Shopify Admin, hands-on - orders, customers, fulfillments, refunds, every day 2. Native-level written English - our customers are American, and a reply that sounds translated costs us the sale 3. Judgment on AI drafts - you know when a draft is confidently wrong, and you check before you send WHAT YOU MUST BRING (hard requirements) 1. Hands-on Shopify Admin experience: orders, customers, fulfillments, refunds. Not "I have seen Shopify" - you have worked in it daily and you can tell us exactly what you did in there. 2. Written English that reads like a native-level support agent wrote it. Our customers are American and they notice. 3. A paid ChatGPT Plus or Claude Pro subscription, and you already use it daily. Not the free tier. This role runs on AI drafting and the free versions are too slow and too limited for a daily inbox block. If you do not have one yet but you are otherwise a fit, say so - we will cover it from day one. What we cannot work with is someone who has never used these tools seriously. 4. You know where AI gets things wrong. You can tell when a draft is confidently wrong and you check the facts in Shopify before you send. 5. Parcel tracking tools (17track or similar) and the patience to read what a scan history actually means. 6. Google Sheets for the dispute tracker. 7. Reliable daily availability, a stable internet connection, a working computer, and you are reachable on Telegram during your working block. 8. At least 1 year in customer support, e-commerce preferred. 9. Willing to sign a freelance contract and a short NDA before you get access to our systems. BONUS (not required, but it moves you to the top of the list) - You have handled PayPal or Klarna disputes before and can describe a real case - Previous direct-response or dropshipping support - Experience with high-volume US customers specifically - Helpdesk tools - tell us which ones you have actually used: Gorgias, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Re:amaze, Commslayer, anything. It means you start faster. - Any tool that makes you faster: text expanders, AI tools, order lookup tools. Tell us your setup. - Any experience with Meta Ads Manager THE TOOLS WE USE Shopify Admin, Gmail, 17track, Google Sheets, PayPal and Klarna resolution centers, Telegram for internal communication, and an AI assistant for drafting. Every account you need is paid by us. WHAT WE PROVIDE - Full written playbooks: response templates per brand, refund decision tree, dispute workflow, carrier patterns, escalation rules - Training videos walking you through real past cases, start to finish - Delegated inbox access - you never handle our passwords - Every tool account and software licence you need, paid by us - Direct feedback, and a standing invitation to tell us when something we built is bad WORKING HOURS AND WHERE THIS ROLE IS GOING - 100% remote, from anywhere in the Philippines - Right now: about 2 hours per day, sometimes up to 3 when volume is high. Roughly 10 to 15 hours per week. - The hours depend on how much comes in. Quiet days you are done in an hour. After a big ad push it takes longer. You are paid per hour, so this works both ways - we are not going to pretend it is a fixed 40-hour job today. - You choose when you work. The only rule: every customer email answered within 24 hours, and your block lands in your morning so the overnight US inbox is cleared before it gets old. - Day-to-day communication is asynchronous on Telegram. No ---------- , no "quick calls", no being on call. - One fixed 30-minute call per week, camera on. We agree on the day and time together once you start, and then it stays there. We go through the numbers, the problems that keep coming back, what you need from us, and what we think you should do differently. You get direct feedback and we expect you to use it. We also expect you to tell us when you think we are wrong - that call goes both ways. This is a team, not a hierarchy. - We use time tracking. We say this openly because we would rather lose an applicant now than have a surprise later. - Where this is going: we are scaling, and we are moving our ad launches onto software. Once you are solid on support, this role can grow into launching ad campaigns from creatives and briefs we prepare - execution inside a tool, not strategy, not creative decisions. More hours, more responsibility, more pay. If that sounds like something you want, say so in your application. HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED Five numbers, nothing else: 1. First response time - under 24 hours, always 2. Inbox at zero at the end of every block 3. Disputes logged with their deadline, none missed, none lost by default 4. Escalation quality - is your recommendation usable as it is 5. Independence over time - fewer questions to us every month We do not measure how many words you wrote. COMPENSATION (all amounts in USD) You are paid per hour, for the hours you actually work. We start low and we move you up fast. We are honest about that instead of promising you a number we do not know you are worth yet. STEP 1 - PAID TRIAL: $2.50 per hour. Real tickets, real customers, from day one. You are paid for every hour of it whether or not we hire you. Short, and we d ---------- quickly. STEP 2 - APPROVED: $3.00 per hour. The position is yours. STEP 3 - PROVEN AND LONG-TERM: $3.50 per hour. STEP 4 - FULLY OPERATING, running the whole inbox on your own: $4.00 per hour. At roughly 10 to 15 hours per week that is about $110 to $260 per month today - and both the hours and the rate grow as we scale. We move people up this ladder fast when they earn it. We have never lost a great person over money and we do not plan to start. Also included: - Paid monthly, on time, every month, no exceptions, via Wise or PayPal - A 13th month bonus after one full year - Bonuses when the business does well - when we grow, you grow - All tools and software licences paid by us, including your AI subscription if you do not have one - Paid Philippine public holidays - Freelance contract and NDA - Long-term position - we want someone who grows with the brands The steps above are not promises we forget about. They are tied to the five numbers under HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED, and we review on schedule. One honest note: at today's hours this is a part-time income. If you currently work with another client, that is completely fine with us, as long as our emails are always answered within 24 hours. As we scale, this role is meant to become your main one. Why we start at $2.50: we have hired for this role before and it did not work out, and it cost us months. The trial is where both of us find out. If you are good you are past it quickly - we have no interest in underpaying someone we want to keep. ENGLISH Our customers are American. A reply that reads translated costs us the sale, and a support agent we cannot have a normal conversation with costs us far more than that. So there are two steps, and we are open about both. First, the short recording you send with your application - that is how we hear you before anyone spends time on a call. Then a video call in English, camera on, before we hire anyone. You need to be able to hold a normal working conversation: understand what we are asking, ask a question back, tell us when something is unclear. Written English alone is not enough. We have been burned by exactly this before and we are not doing it again. HOW TO APPLY Apply through OnlineJobs.ph and start your message with TAMARIND - Your Full Name. Keep it short. We are not asking you to do unpaid work to apply - nothing below takes more than ten minutes, and nothing below is work you have to invent for us. Be specific: vague answers are the fastest way to get rejected. 1. WHERE YOU DID SUPPORT BEFORE. Which companies or stores, for how long, and in which tool (Gorgias, Zendesk, Gmail, whatever it was). Numbers, not adjectives. 2. HOW MANY EMAILS PER DAY you handled there, and what your average first response time was. 3. YOUR SHOPIFY EXPERIENCE. What did you actually do in the admin? "Refunds, address edits, fulfillments, daily" tells us more than "I know Shopify". 4. YOUR AI SETUP. Which subscription do you have (ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro, other) and what do you use it for day to day? 5. YOUR TIME ZONE and the daily block you would work in. 6. ONE PIECE OF PROOF from your past support work. Your pick, and any of these is fine: a screenshot of your ticket stats, an SOP you followed or wrote, a few of the templates you worked with, or a reference we may contact. Black out or remove anything confidential - customer names, order data, anything your agreement with a past employer covers. We do not want you to break that agreement to apply here, and a redacted screenshot tells us everything we need. If you genuinely cannot share anything, write us a short SOP instead: "A customer writes that the package never arrived. Step by step, what do you do?" A few lines is enough. 7. A 60-SECOND RECORDING OF YOURSELF SPEAKING ENGLISH. Loom, a voice message, an unlisted YouTube link, whatever is easiest. Introduce yourself, tell us what you did in your last support role, and say why this one interests you. No production, no script, no editing - phone camera or just audio is completely fine. We are not judging your setup or your confidence on camera. We want to hear how you speak English, because that d ---------- whether this works. That is it. No cover letter, no essay, no test task. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT 1. We read your answers and listen to your recording 2. Short video call in English, camera on 3. After the call: a small PAID trial on real cases from our inbox 4. Hire, starting rate, then the first review The trial comes after we have spoken, not before. You get paid for it whether or not we hire you. We keep the number of trials small on purpose, so if you get there you are already a serious candidate. Applications that do not start correctly, or that skip any of the 7 points, will not be reviewed. We are strict about this on purpose: following instructions exactly is the single most important part of this job. We reply to every application that follows the instructions, and we reply fast. If this sounds like you, apply today. We are hiring one person and we are hiring quickly. Apply here on OnlineJobs.ph - start your message with: TAMARIND - Your Full Name

description: We are Goodcommerce, a German consumer-products company. Your work goes live and directly moves our sales. Nobody will hand you a template to fill in. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR We are being specific on purpose. We would rather get twenty good applications than two hundred generic ones. You design for the customer, not for other designers. Our images are judged at thumbnail size on a phone, in a search result, next to fifteen competitors. Beautiful but unreadable is a fail for us. If you have ever argued with someone about where the eye goes first in an image, we will get along. You can follow a brand guideline exactly. We have a written guideline per brand — exact hex codes, exact fonts, defined image world. Exact means exact. We recently had a designer recolour one of our logos because he thought it looked better that way. That is the single fastest way to not get this job. You work independently. We give you the guideline, logo vectors, product photos and a brief. We do not want to explain the basics every week. You tell us early. REQUIRED - 3+ years professional graphic design, with real e-commerce or marketplace work — Amazon strongly preferred - Advanced Photoshop and Illustrator - Video editing at listing-video level: Premiere or After Effects - Written English good enough for detailed briefs and feedback - Reliable internet, your own computer, and a quiet place to work NICE TO HAVE — tell us if you have it, but it is not required - Print-ready packaging: dielines, CMYK, bleed, prepress - Amazon Seller Central experience - Jewellery or kids' product categories WHAT WE OFFER - $1,000 - $1,300 per month, depending on what you can show us. We are building a team, not filling a gap - 13th month pay - 15 days paid leave per year plus Philippine holidays - No night shifts. We only need you online between 2 PM and 6 PM Manila time. The rest of your day is yours to organise - A salary review after 6 months, and again after 12 - Real ownership of the work, and honest feedback instead of silence HOW TO APPLY Copy the template below into your message and fill it in. Applications that do not use it will not be read — not because we are strict for the sake of it, but because it is the only way we can compare people fairly and answer everyone quickly. Please write your answers yourself. We are not against AI, we use it daily — but we can tell, and a generic answer tells us nothing about you. ------- COPY FROM HERE ------- MONTOI 1. PORTFOLIO LINK: (required — Behance, Dribbble, Google Drive, personal site, anything we can open without a login) 2. THREE AMAZON IMAGES YOU DESIGNED YOURSELF: (links or attachments. Gallery images, infographics or A+ modules. If you worked in a team on any of them, say exactly what your part was.) 3. ONE OF THOSE THREE, RESIZED TO 300 PIXELS WIDE: (attach it. Yes, really — this is how our customers see it first.) 4. ONE PRODUCT VIDEO YOU EDITED: (link. 15-60 seconds is perfect.) 5. TAKE THE IMAGE FROM POINT 3. In your own words: What does the customer need to understand in the first two seconds, and what exactly in your design makes that happen? (3-5 sentences.) 6. title: VA - Guest Communication & Operations @ Restay Homes
job_title: VA - Guest Communication & Operations @ Restay Homes
description: Hi! My name is Nikita, I'm the founder of Restay Vacation Homes Rental - a short-term rental management company based in Dubai. We manage 35+ furnished apartments in Dubai under sublease and property management, from studios to 3-bedrooms. We've held Airbnb Superhost status for the past year with a 4.8-4.9 rating across the whole portfolio, and we're adding units every month. We're looking for one more VA to join our operations team. WHAT THE JOB ACTUALLY IS Communication is most of it. You'll be in our CRM, in Slack and on WhatsApp all day - talking to guests, cleaners, maintenance, contractors, suppliers and owners, and keeping our internal team informed. The rest is paperwork: passport and registration documents, DTCM, records, reports. Getting it right, and getting it finished. Guest relations: - Manage guest communication, inbound and outbound - Coordinate check-in and check-out - Handle issues during a stay and follow them through to a result, not just a reply - Coordinate cleaners and suppliers via WhatsApp and Slack Maintenance coordination: - Log every reported issue and keep it visible until it's actually fixed - Dispatch technicians, including after hours, and confirm the job was done - Chase contractors and suppliers who go quiet - Spot problems that keep coming back and say so New unit launches: - Coordinate a new apartment from handover to first booking - furniture delivery, installation, deep clean, photos, keys and access - Handle the paperwork: DTCM registration, documents, listing setup across platforms - Keep the owner and the internal team updated on where each unit stands Operations and admin: - Collect and process guest documents for registration - on time, every time - Keep our CRM accurate: bookings, unit status, guest records - Prepare and check reports and documents - Escalate the right things to the senior team, and only the right things Systems, as you grow into it: - Write and maintain SOPs - Improve how the team works, not just do the tasks - Build simple automations between our tools TWO THINGS MATTER MORE TO US THAN ANYTHING ELSE You chase things until they're done. Most of this job is waiting on other people - a guest who hasn't sent a document, a contractor who read your message and didn't answer, an owner sitting on an approval. Asking once is not doing the task. We need someone who tracks every open thread, notices who has gone quiet, and pushes again - politely, on a schedule, switching channel and escalating when it isn't working. Silence from the other side is not a finished task. You check before you answer. When a source contradicts what we've written, or something doesn't add up, stop and find out which is true rather than passing on the first answer you found. Being right matters more here than being fast, and one good question beats a confident wrong answer. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - You follow up. You have a real system for tracking what you're waiting on - You verify. You notice when two sources disagree and you resolve it - Fluent English, written and spoken - natural and clear, not translated-sounding - You own tasks. You d ---------- what you can d ---------- and escalate what you can't - Structured. You follow SOPs, and you write them when they're missing - Accurate with detail - numbers, dates, documents - Comfortable with CRMs, Google Sheets, Slack, WhatsApp PREFERRED EXPERIENCE - 6+ months in Airbnb operations or another short-term rental company - 6+ months in a small team or startup - Experience helping a company scale from 10 to 50+ units is a big plus - Familiarity with guest communication, pricing tools, turnover coordination - Experience writing SOPs or building team processes WHAT WE OFFER - $4-6/hour depending on experience - Flexible workload, 40-60 hrs/week, 5-6 days - you tell us what suits you - Direct work with the founder, fast decisions, no bureaucracy - Opportunity to grow into Team Lead as we scale HOW TO APPLY We don't accept direct messages. Applications without a completed form are ignored. The application has two parts: Part 1 - a short form about you and your experience (about 10 minutes) Part 2 - five real situations from our operations. You'll get the link right after you submit Part 1. You have 60 minutes from that moment, and we record how long it takes. Part 2 has no trick questions and no perfect answers. We want to see how you think and how fast you get to a result. Form: ---------- Looking forward to hearing from you! Nikita

title: SEO content and topical authority assistant
job_title: SEO content and topical authority assistant
description: We are looking for a reliable SEO content specialist to support a growing portfolio of UK businesses across several different industries. This is not a role for someone who simply generates articles using ChatGPT and sends them over. We already use AI extensively. What we need is someone who can think. You should understand why a page exists, what somebody is searching for, how that page fits into the wider website, what supporting content should surround it, and how to make the finished content sound like the actual business rather than generic AI-generated copy. This will initially be a part-time position with the potential to grow significantly for the right person. ## What you will be doing Your work will include: * Researching topics and search intent before writing * Reviewing Google search results and competitor content * Creating SEO content briefs * Identifying content clusters and supporting article opportunities * Writing service pages, location pages, landing pages and articles * Creating internal linking recommendations * Identifying relevant entities, subtopics and FAQs * Following an existing keyword strategy where provided * Helping expand broad keywords into useful topical clusters * Matching the tone of voice of completely different client brands * Updating and improving existing content * Structuring articles properly using headings and logical information hierarchy * Using AI to accelerate your work without allowing AI to replace your judgement * Fact checking anything generated with AI before submitting it You will not initially be responsible for uploading content into WordPress. Your responsibility is creating high-quality content and recommendations that are ready for our team to review and publish. ## What good work looks like If we give you a plumbing company, SaaS company and professional services business, the content should not sound like it came from the same writer or prompt. Before writing an article, you should naturally be asking questions such as: What is the actual search intent? What pages already exist on the website? What should this page link to? What pages should link back to this page? Is this a standalone topic or part of a larger cluster? What information is competitors consistently covering? What are competitors missing? Does this article genuinely deserve to rank? Could somebody tell that AI helped produce this? If your process is simply keyword + prompt + 1,500-word article, this role will not be a good fit. ## Skills we are looking for You should have experience with several of the following: * SEO content writing * Search intent analysis * Keyword research * Topic clustering * Topical authority * Content briefs * Content optimisation * Internal linking * Competitor research * SERP analysis * Google Search Console * Ahrefs, Semrush or similar SEO tools * WordPress * ChatGPT, Claude or similar AI tools You do not need to know everything. Strong thinking, attention to detail and reliability matter more to us than having every SEO certification available. ## Using AI We actively encourage the use of AI. However, there is a major difference between using AI as a tool and submitting AI-generated content without thinking. AI can help you research, organise, expand, draft and edit. You are still responsible for: * Accuracy * Originality * Search intent * Structure * Brand voice * Relevance * Quality We will reject generic AI content. ## Working arrangement This is initially a part-time remote position. Starting budget: $200 to $300 USD per month depending on experience, availability and output. We care more about consistent high-quality output than tracking every minute you work. If you become someone we can trust across client accounts, there is substantial scope for the role, responsibilities and compensation to increase. We are looking for someone interested in becoming part of the way we operate rather than somebody looking to churn through another freelance writing gig. ## How to apply Please do not send a generic application. Start your application with the words: **Purple Penguin** Applications without those words will be ignored. Then answer the following five questions. ### 1. Show us your work Send links to two pieces of SEO content you personally created. For each one, briefly explain: * What keyword or topic you targeted * What the search intent was * What you personally did * Why you structured the content the way you did ### 2. Show us how you think about clusters Imagine you are working with a UK plumber who wants to rank for: **boiler installation** Give us: * The primary page you would create * Five supporting content ideas * Two related commercial pages * How you would internally link these pages together Keep this concise. ### 3. Tell us how you use AI Explain exactly how you currently use ChatGPT, Claude or another AI tool when creating SEO content. We are not looking for somebody who claims they never use AI. We want to understand your process. ### 4. Spot the problem Tell us why the following approach is weak: "Find a keyword with good volume, ask ChatGPT to write a 2,000-word SEO article about it, add the keyword to the title and headings, then publish it." Your answer should be no more than 150 words. ### 5. Tell us about you Include: * Your current availability * Your expected monthly salary * Your timezone * How many clients or employers you currently work with * The SEO tools you have previously used Finally, at the bottom of your application, tell us your favourite food. This is simply to confirm you have read the entire job description. ## Important Please do not apply if: * You submit completely AI-generated applications * You cannot demonstrate previous writing * You frequently miss deadlines * You need detailed instructions for every small task * You consider SEO writing to mean putting keywords into an article repeatedly * You are applying for dozens of unrelated VA jobs at the same time We are happy to teach our processes. We cannot teach care, curiosity or reliability. If you are someone who enjoys understanding why content performs rather than simply producing more words, we would like to hear from you.

job_title: Long-Term Video Editor — Documentary-Style YouTube Channel (Retention-Focused)
description: Long-Term Video Editor — Documentary-Style YouTube Channel (Retention-Focused) Rate: $30 AUD per finished 12-minute video Volume: 4 videos per week Type: Ongoing, long-term. Not a one-off project. About the channel Forgotten Beasts is a faceless documentary channel about extinct animals, lost species, and creatures people believe might still be out there. Audience is mostly US, UK and Australia, ages 34–55. Think mystery-thriller documentary, not listicle. I write every script myself. You handle the edit: footage sourcing, cutting, sound design, text, pacing. What I actually need from you Views are not the problem. Retention is. I need an editor who understands that the edit is what keeps someone watching past minute three. Here is the standard: First 30 seconds. Target is 90% of viewers still watching at the 30-second mark. No logo, no channel intro, no slow build. Frame one must match the thumbnail exactly — if the thumbnail shows a thylacine, the first frame is a thylacine. Cuts every 2–3 seconds through the opening. Change something on screen every 10–15 seconds. A digital zoom, a pan, a text pop, a hard cut, a music shift. If a clip has to sit longer than 3 seconds, add movement to it. Static frames kill retention. Tension, then release. Never show the payoff shot while the voiceover is still explaining it. Build it, hold a beat, then drop the visual. If everything on screen is loud the whole time, nothing lands. Sound leads picture. Place your SFX a few frames before the visual appears. Low rumbles for size, whooshes on transitions, paper crinkle for old documents and maps. Cut the music completely right before a big reveal. Tease what's coming. When the script mentions an animal appearing later, flash a blurred or silhouetted frame of it for about 10 frames. Blink-and-you-miss-it. It makes people stay for the clear version. Be ruthless with dead air. Remove breathing gaps, micro-pauses, and any second where nothing is happening. Use J-cuts so audio from the next section starts before the visual changes. Retention dies from a hundred small leaks, not one big one. Archival treatment. When the script says an animal was last seen in 1936, the footage should look like 1936. Grain, black and white, film scratches, slight instability. Fancy motion graphics do not matter here. Clean pacing does. What I provide Full script with timestamps, emotion notes and edit cues already marked Voiceover audio Thumbnail and title before you start, so you know what promise the edit has to deliver on Stock accounts if needed Pay, bonuses and revenue share $30 per 12-minute video, paid weekly via Wise or PayPal Retention bonus: +$[10] per video that holds above [50]% average view duration Breakout bonus: +$[50] for any video that passes [50,000] views in its first 30 days Revenue share: once you have delivered consistently for [3] months, you move onto [5]% of the channel's monthly ad revenue on top of your per-video rate The rate goes up as the channel grows. I would rather train one editor properly and keep them for years than cycle through cheap freelancers. If this channel scales, you scale with it. To apply Do not send a generic portfolio link. Applications without the following get ignored. Send 2 examples of documentary or faceless-style work you edited. Tell me which parts were your decisions. Answer this: what is the first thing you would change in an edit if the retention graph dropped hard at the 45-second mark? Confirm you can deliver 4 videos a week, every week. Tell me your software and your turnaround time for a 12-minute video. Shortlisted applicants get a paid test: one 45-second segment from a real script. When something does not add up, you are expected to notice it, investigate what happened, determine the root cause, and resolve it independently. The business is growing quickly, so you should be comfortable working with evolving processes, minimal supervision, and taking ownership of bookkeeping issues from start to finish. About This Role You will take ownership of day-to-day bookkeeping activities, including managing accounts payable, entering and reconciling bills from multiple sources, scheduling vendor payments, performing account reconciliations, and maintaining accurate inventory records. Because this is a food manufacturing business, inventory bookkeeping is an important part of the role. You should be comfortable working with physical inventory and performing unit conversions, such as converting pounds to kilograms, when recording or reconciling inventory-related information. The most important part of this position is your ability to identify and solve problems. If a vendor statement does not match the books, a bill appears to have been entered twice, a bill is missing, or an inventory balance does not make sense, you should be able to investigate the issue and determine what needs to be corrected. You will also be expected to communicate your findings clearly, explain discrepancies and their causes, and document or communicate the actions taken to resolve them.
