description: We are an established Western Australian-owned electrical company based in Perth. With over 12 years of industry experience and more than 400 five-star customer reviews, we directly supply and install solar panels, battery systems, ducted air conditioning and other electrical solutions. We are seeking a highly experienced, professional appointment setter based in the Philippines to manage warm enquiries from Western Australian homeowners. This is not a general virtual-assistant or entry-level call-centre position. We need someone who can communicate naturally with Australian customers, identify genuine opportunities and book high-quality appointments that attend. The Role You will be the first human point of contact for customers enquiring about solar, batteries or ducted air conditioning. Your responsibilities will include: Contacting new website, Google and social-media leads quickly. Building rapport naturally with Australian homeowners. Understanding the customer’s needs without sounding scripted. Confirming homeownership, property location, product interest, timeframe and decision-making process. Asking relevant qualification questions about electricity bills, existing solar systems, battery requirements or air-conditioning needs. Explaining Solar 1 Nation Electricals and our consultation process professionally. Booking qualified showroom or home consultations with our Perth sales consultants. Confirming appointments and reducing cancellations and no-shows. Following up customers who did not answer or were not ready initially. Reactivating suitable older enquiries when requested. Maintaining complete and accurate notes, tasks and pipeline stages in GoHighLevel. Coordinating closely with our Perth sales team. The goal is not simply to book as many appointments as possible. Success will be measured by the quality of the appointments, attendance rate, quotation opportunities and completed sales generated from your bookings. Essential Experience To be considered, you must have: At least two years of appointment setting, telesales or lead-qualification experience. Previous experience speaking with Australian customers. Proven experience booking appointments for solar, batteries, energy, air conditioning, trades or other Australian home-improvement services. Excellent spoken and written English. Strong comprehension of Australian accents. A confident, friendly and natural communication style. Strong listening, qualification and objection-handling skills. Experience managing warm inbound leads and structured follow-up sequences. A reliable computer, professional headset, stable internet and quiet home-working environment. Availability to work full-time during Perth/Philippines daytime business hours. Direct experience with Australian residential solar, batteries or ducted air conditioning will be strongly preferred. The Person We Are Looking For The right person will: Sound professional, natural and trustworthy on the telephone. Listen carefully instead of mechanically reading a script. Understand when to ask additional questions and when to move toward an appointment. Handle objections such as “Just send me a price,” “I am only comparing companies,” or “I need to speak with my partner.” Follow up consistently without pressuring or annoying customers. Take ownership of every assigned lead. Maintain accurate CRM notes and future follow-up tasks. Care about customer experience and the quality of appointments booked. Be dependable, organised and committed to a long-term position. Please Do Not Apply If You have no previous experience speaking with Australian customers. Your background is limited to general virtual-assistant or administrative work. You focus only on dial volume and cannot demonstrate appointment quality. You regularly book customers who are unqualified or unaware of the appointment. You are uncomfortable with follow-ups, objections or performance targets. You cannot provide clear information about your previous results. Performance Measures Your performance will be evaluated using: Speed of response to new leads. Customer contact rate. Number of genuinely qualified appointments booked. Appointment attendance rate. Accuracy and completeness of CRM notes. Number of appointments progressing to quotations and sales. Customer feedback and call quality. Consistency, reliability and follow-up discipline. What We Provide Warm inbound leads generated through our marketing campaigns. An established Australian brand with a Perth showroom and installation team. Training on our products, pricing, qualification criteria and processes. Approved call guides and objection-handling support. GoHighLevel CRM access and structured workflows. Competitive base salary based on verified experience. Performance incentives linked to qualified appointments that attend and completed sales. Stable, long-term employment. Opportunities to progress into a Senior Appointment Setter, Sales Consultant or Team Leader position. How to Apply Please submit your updated CV and answer every question below: How many years have you worked in appointment setting or telesales? Which Australian companies or campaigns have you worked with? Which products or services were you promoting? Were the leads inbound, warm outbound or cold? Approximately how many calls did you make each day? How many qualified appointments did you book each week? What was your average appointment attendance rate? How did your previous employer define a qualified appointment? Which Australian states did you contact? Which CRM and calling systems have you used? Can a previous manager verify your employment and performance? What base salary and incentive structure are you expecting? Please also include a 60–90 second voice or video introduction explaining: Your experience speaking with Australian customers. Your experience booking appointments. How you would respond if a customer said: “I am only comparing prices. Just send me the cheapest option.” Applications that do not include the requested answers and voice or video introduction will not be shortlisted. If you are a high-quality appointment setter who understands Australian customers, values appointment quality and wants a stable long-term role with a growing Perth company, we would like to hear from you.

title: Cold Caller / Appointment Setter – Full-Time/Part-Time
description: We are a U.S.-based digital marketing agency looking for a confident, reliable, and experienced Cold Caller / Appointment Setter to join our team. This is not a customer service position. Your primary responsibility will be making outbound calls to business owners, starting conversations, identifying interest, and setting qualified appointments for our sales team. We are looking for someone who is comfortable picking up the phone, talking to strangers, handling objections, and maintaining a positive attitude throughout the day. What You’ll Be Doing Make outbound cold calls to prospective U.S. businesses Speak directly with business owners and decision-makers Follow provided scripts while still sounding natural and conversational Build rapport quickly Identify whether a prospect is a good fit for our services Handle common objections professionally Schedule qualified appointments for our sales team Accurately update leads and notes inside our CRM Follow up with prospects when appropriate Track calls, conversations, appointments, and results Participate in occasional training and call-review sessions Who We’re Looking For The ideal candidate: Has 2+ years of cold calling, telemarketing, outbound sales, or appointment-setting experience Has experience calling U.S. customers or businesses Speaks clear, fluent, conversational English Sounds confident and comfortable on the phone Can build rapport without sounding overly scripted Understands how to ask questions and keep a conversation moving Knows how to handle rejection and objections Is comfortable making a high volume of outbound calls Is organized and follows up consistently Can work independently without constant supervision Is dependable and shows up on time Is coachable and willing to improve Has experience using a CRM Experience with GoHighLevel / HighLevel is a plus, but not required. This Position Is a Good Fit If… You genuinely enjoy talking to people. You understand that cold calling is a numbers game, but you also know that the quality of the conversation matters. You don’t get discouraged when someone says “no.” You know how to adjust your tone depending on the person you are speaking with. You are comfortable having real conversations instead of simply reading a script word-for-word. Most importantly, you understand that your job is to create enough interest to get the prospect to take the next step and book an appointment. Schedule Full-Time – 8 Hours Per Day, Part-time available for the right person You must be available during U.S. business hours. Exact schedule will be discussed during the interview. Compensation Starting compensation will depend on experience and demonstrated ability. There will also be opportunities for performance-based bonuses/incentives for qualified appointments and results. We are looking for someone interested in a long-term position, not a temporary project. How to Apply Please include the following in your application: How many years of cold-calling or appointment-setting experience do you have? What industries have you cold-called for? Have you called U.S. businesses before? Approximately how many outbound calls were you making per day in your previous position? How many appointments were you typically setting? What CRM systems have you used? Do you have experience with GoHighLevel? What is your expected hourly rate? What hours are you available to work in U.S. Eastern Time? Please send a 60–90 second voice recording introducing yourself and explaining why you believe you would be good at this position. At the very beginning of your application, write: “I’m Ready to Dial” Applications that do not include this phrase and a voice recording may not be considered. We are looking for someone who can become an important long-term member of our team. If you are confident on the phone, consistent, competitive, and enjoy turning cold conversations into opportunities, we would like to hear from you.

title: VIDEO EDITOR WANTED, LONG-TERM, $500/MONTH
description: We run a large short-form content operation, our clips pull millions of views across a big network of accounts, and we're adding editors to the team. Long-term position with steady work every single week. The work: Editing recorded OmeTV sessions into short viral clips. You watch the footage, find the moments worth clipping, and cut them into clean vertical clips with sound effects, captions and good pacing. You're not hunting for perfect moments, normal ones work fine, we just skip the boring small talk. What matters is that a stranger watching can follow what's going on. We provide all the footage, there's always more than you can finish. The pay, two options, you choose: 1. Standard. Steady hours, fixed pay. You work the set schedule, hit the daily numbers, and get the same $500 every month. Nothing to calculate and no surprises. If the footage is thin one day you still get paid the same. 2. Per clip. You get paid for every clip you deliver. Hit the same daily numbers and you land on the same $500, but there's no ceiling on it. An extra hour or two a day puts you around $600, and the ones who really push go past that. Plus $10 on top for every clip that passes 1M views. Both are paid on the 1st and 15th, always on time. No hourly rate and no time tracker either way. Requirements: Full-time, around 8 hours a day, 6 days a week. Fast stable internet and a PC that handles editing smoothly. Short-form editing experience, CapCut is enough. Every clip goes through review and only approved clips are paid, we approve everything as long as the quality is there. We choose few people and keep the ones who deliver.

title: After Effects Documentary Editor
description: We’re hiring an experienced After Effects editor for a new YouTube channel covering mysteries, unexplained events, strange history, and darker subjects. LEMMiNO is our main reference for the general quality and presentation we want. We’ll develop our own visual identity, but applicants should be capable of producing similarly polished documentary visuals quickly and consistently. This is not a basic stock-footage editing position. You’ll receive a completed script and recorded narration. You’ll be responsible for transforming them into a finished 20–30-minute documentary, including: Original After Effects sequences Animated maps, photographs, documents, and timelines Silhouettes, diagrams, and atmospheric recreations Masking, compositing, parallax, and camera movement Relevant archival footage and photographs Music, ambience, and sound design Narration cleanup and final video assembly We need someone who: Has advanced Adobe After Effects skills Is highly skilled with Photoshop Can edit professionally in Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve Has excellent visual storytelling and pacing Can create original visuals instead of relying on random stock footage Can work quickly without sacrificing quality Can make creative decisions without requiring instructions for every shot Communicates reliably and meets deadlines Is interested in consistent, long-term work Experience with 3D software is helpful but not required. Do not apply if your work mainly consists of stock footage, basic zooms, generic transitions, downloaded templates, podcasts, or short-form social-media videos. No AI-generated images or video will be used on this channel. HOW TO APPLY Begin your application with the word “Lemon.” Send your two strongest relevant work samples. Include timestamps showing the After Effects sequences you personally created. Briefly explain what you created in each sequence. List the software you used. Tell us how long you would need to produce a polished 60-second documentary sequence. Include your rate for a finished 20–30-minute video. Shortlisted applicants will be offered the same paid 60-second editing test. We will evaluate visual quality, storytelling, accuracy, communication, and production speed.

title: B2B Cold Caller & Appointment Setter | Property Management Outreach
job_title: B2B Cold Caller & Appointment Setter | Property Management Outreach
description: About This Opportunity I am posting this position and conducting the initial interviews on behalf of one of my clients. My client owns an established carpet cleaning and restoration company serving San Diego County, California. I am helping them find the right person for this long-term position. The company name and complete business details will be shared with serious shortlisted candidates at the appropriate stage of the interview process. The company already has a strong residential customer base. Its next goal is to grow the commercial side of the business by building relationships with property management companies, apartment communities, multifamily properties, and other properties with multiple units. Work Schedule Full-time, long-term position Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. California Pacific Time One-hour unpaid meal break each workday 40 paid hours per week This is an overnight schedule in the Philippines. Depending on daylight saving time in California, the Philippine schedule will generally be: 11:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m., or 12:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. The position always follows California business hours, so the Philippine schedule will change by one hour when California enters or leaves daylight saving time. Please apply only if you can consistently and reliably work this overnight schedule. Compensation Starting pay: $5 USD per hour Approximately $867 USD per month based on 40 paid hours per week Additional performance bonuses Long-term growth potential for the right person We want to be transparent about the starting pay and schedule. In addition to the hourly wage, the selected candidate will have opportunities to earn bonuses when clearly defined performance milestones are reached. Bonus opportunities may include: Scheduling qualified appointments that take place Generating qualified commercial opportunities Helping the company acquire new commercial accounts Reaching agreed-upon outreach or conversion goals The exact bonus amounts and requirements will be explained before work begins. Quality matters more than simply making a large number of calls. Primary Responsibilities Make outbound calls to apartment communities, multifamily properties, and property management companies Focus on commercial properties with multiple units and repeat-service potential Professionally introduce the company’s carpet cleaning and restoration services Identify property managers, regional managers, maintenance supervisors, and other decision-makers Speak professionally with receptionists, gatekeepers, property staff, and decision-makers Ask qualifying questions about each property and its cleaning or restoration needs Learn approximately how many units or properties a prospect manages when appropriate Determine whether the property currently uses a carpet cleaning or restoration provider Follow up with prospects by phone and email Email the company’s commercial services PDF, information, and price sheets Schedule qualified callbacks, estimates, meetings, or appointments for the owner Build professional relationships with property management contacts Follow approved scripts and email templates without sounding robotic This is not a high-pressure residential sales position. The goal is to develop real commercial relationships that may require several calls and follow-ups. Lead Tracking and Follow-Up The selected candidate will receive access to a company-provided Google Sheet containing leads. You will be responsible for accurately tracking: Every call attempt Call dates and times The person contacted Call outcomes and conversation notes Decision-maker contact information Property and unit information when available PDFs and price sheets sent Follow-up dates and next steps Appointments and callbacks Wrong or disconnected numbers Prospects who are not interested Do Not Call requests Accurate notes and consistent follow-up are essential parts of this position. Calling Compliance The selected candidate will be required to install and use the company-approved calling and compliance applications. You must: Confirm that numbers are eligible before calling Never call a number blocked by the system Immediately document and respect Do Not Call requests Follow all company calling procedures and required disclosures Never disable or bypass a calling restriction Training will be provided on the company’s systems and procedures. Recorded Calls and Coaching Outbound calls may be recorded through the company’s approved calling system in accordance with applicable disclosure and consent requirements. The owner will regularly review calls for: Professionalism Communication quality Accuracy Script adherence Proper treatment of prospects Qualification skills Call documentation Overall improvement You must be comfortable receiving constructive feedback and applying that coaching to future calls. Communication Requirements Fluent spoken and written English Clear and easily understood pronunciation Professional, friendly, and natural phone presence Comfortable speaking with U.S.-based business prospects Strong listening and relationship-building skills Able to follow a script without sounding like you are reading it Able to write clear and professional follow-up emails Persistent without being aggressive or pushy Comfortable handling objections and rejection professionally Candidates will be evaluated based on communication clarity, professionalism, experience, reliability, and ability to perform the role. Experience and Technical Requirements Previous cold-calling, appointment-setting, telemarketing, or outbound sales experience Experience calling businesses in the United States Commercial or B2B outreach experience is strongly preferred Comfortable speaking with gatekeepers and asking for decision-makers Strong organization and follow-up skills Experience using Google Sheets Willing to install the required calling and compliance applications Reliable computer and high-speed internet connection Quiet and professional overnight calling environment Reliable headset with clear audio Experience using a CRM or calling platform is preferred Experience with property management, multifamily housing, commercial cleaning, restoration, or home services is a strong advantage How to Apply Please include the following: A short description of your cold-calling or appointment-setting experience The types of U.S. businesses you have called Any experience with B2B outreach, property managers, or apartment communities The calling systems and CRM platforms you have used Your experience using Google Sheets Confirmation that you can consistently work 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. California Pacific Time Confirmation that you understand this is an overnight Philippine schedule that changes by one hour when California’s daylight saving time changes Confirmation that you accept the starting pay of $5 USD per hour plus performance bonuses Voice Sample Required Please include a link to a 45 to 60-second audio recording with your application. Video is not required. In your recording: Introduce yourself Briefly describe your cold-calling experience Explain how you would professionally introduce a commercial carpet cleaning and restoration company to a property manager We will evaluate the recording based on: Clear and easily understood speech Confidence and professionalism Friendly and natural delivery Appropriate speaking pace Ability to communicate without sounding robotic Overall suitability for speaking with U.S.-based property managers Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a live interview and may be asked to complete a simple mock call using a sample script. Please begin your application with the words “Commercial Outreach” so I know you read the complete posting.

title: GoHighLevel Technical Partner — API, Integrations, Custom Builds (Full-Time, US Hours)
job_title: GoHighLevel Technical Partner — API, Integrations, Custom Builds (Full-Time, US Hours)
description: Read this entire post before you apply. There are specific instructions inside it. If you miss any of them, I will not read your application. That is deliberate — this job is largely about following technical specifications exactly. WHO I AM I run Grow With AI, a small US automation agency. We build AI receptionists, lead systems, and custom CRM work for small businesses in trades, legal, and services. I am the founder. Right now it is mostly me. I am hiring the person who becomes the technical half of this company. WHAT THIS JOB ACTUALLY IS This is not a GoHighLevel VA job. This is not "build me a funnel." You will: - Connect GoHighLevel to anything — other CRMs, POS systems, databases, custom software — in both directions - Work directly with the GHL v2 API, OAuth, webhooks, and Private Integration tokens - Build custom dashboards and reporting that GHL cannot do natively - Design and run databases (Supabase or similar) - Build small custom apps and internal tools - Own integrations end to end, including when they break TOOLS YOU GET You will have access to Claude Cowork and our AI tooling. I have no problem with you using AI to do the work — I use it constantly. What I care about is whether you can direct it, catch it when it is wrong, and fix what it breaks. If AI is doing the thinking for you instead of the typing, you will not get through my screening. THE SCHEDULE — READ THIS TWICE Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM US Central Time. In the Philippines that is a graveyard shift. Do not apply unless you are certain you can hold that schedule long term. I would rather you tell me no today than quit in month two. PAY, HONESTLY Starting: $500 USD per month, full-time, plus performance bonuses. I know that is under market for this skill set, so here is the real deal. At six months, if the work has been what I need, the base moves to $900-$1,000. That review is a commitment, not a maybe. At twelve months, if you have stayed with me through the build and the company is where I expect it to be, you are looking at roughly three times what you started on — and it keeps climbing from there. I am not going to pretend that number is guaranteed, because it depends on us growing. What I will tell you is that it is the trajectory I am building toward, and the person in this seat is the person who gets carried by it. I am early, and I am telling you exactly where I stand. If you need $1,200 today, we are not a fit and I respect that. SUBJECT LINE The subject line of your application must be exactly: GHL-BUILDER-2026 - FLAMINGO - [your first name] Yes, flamingo. Type it exactly. Applications with any other subject line are deleted unread. WHO I AM LOOKING FOR Reliability and trustworthiness above everything else. You will have access to client systems and client data. I need someone who says what they will do, does it, and tells me early when something is going wrong. I am not looking for someone who goes quiet for three days and then sends an excuse. DO NOT SEND FILES Do not attach a resume, CV, or portfolio document. Anyone who attaches a file is removed immediately. Instead, paste five bullet points into the body of your message describing the five most technical things you have personally built. HOW TO APPLY Begin your message with the single word: Compass Then answer these five questions, numbered, in this exact order: 1. Describe a system you personally connected to GoHighLevel. What was on the other end, which direction did data flow, and what broke? 2. You are syncing contacts two ways between GHL and another CRM. Both fire a webhook on update. How do you stop the infinite loop? 3. A client wants reporting GHL cannot do natively. Describe how you would build them a custom dashboard, including where the data lives. 4. Tell me about a time AI gave you a confidently wrong answer, and how you caught it. 5. When it is 9:00 AM in Chicago, what time and what date is it where you are? Your entire application must be under 250 words, not counting the five bullets. I am testing whether you can be brief and precise. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT If you pass this stage: a short screen-recorded technical exercise, then a paid trial project ($25 USD, roughly 3 hours, paid whether or not you advance), then a live interview at 9:00 AM Central. I will tell you either way. I will not waste your time.

title: Short-Form Video Editor — Kids Sports & Coding Brand
job_title: Short-Form Video Editor — Kids Sports & Coding Brand
description: About us: We run Keiki Athletes & Keiki Coders — after-school sports and coding programs for kids in Hawaii. We capture tons of fun session footage and want it turned into great short-form video. The role: Turn our footage into polished Reels (9:16) for Instagram & Facebook — mostly short videos, but we're open to other formats (carousels, photo posts, etc.) over time. To start, we hand you a clear brief (concept, clips, caption) plus a searchable, tagged clip library. description: VA Brief: LinkedIn Outreach & Strategy Specialist (Part-Time, 10-15 hrs/week) About us: We're a property buyer's agency helping professionals and investors build wealth through property. LinkedIn is one of our primary channels for finding new clients. We offer a range of property services, including residential and commercial property acquisition, property development, property assessment and due diligence, auction and negotiation representation, purchase support, and portfolio reviews. The goal: Get the contact off LinkedIn and into our database (ActiveCampaign). Every activity on LinkedIn exists to serve that one outcome. What you'll do 1. Build and manage our Sales Navigator lead lists: set up saved searches, refine filters, and identify the right targeting criteria for our ideal client 2. Contribute to outreach strategy. Help shape targeting, messaging angles, and sequencing based on what's actually working, not just execute a fixed script 3. Send connection requests and early messages using our templates where appropriate. These cover the common, repeatable parts of the conversation 4. Personalise where it matters. Know when a templated message won't work and write something tailored instead; this will be a mix of both. 5. Have the ability to hold real conversations once someone engages. Natural, not scripted line-by-line 6. Once there's genuine interest and the prospect has agreed to hear from us, confirm what they've agreed to and obtain their verified contact details (using Apollo or similar). This flows into ActiveCampaign with the correct tag, completing the handoff 7. Log everything in our tracker (connections, conversation stage, outcome, consent captured, email captured) 8. Maintain list hygiene. Withdraw stale pending requests, refresh saved searches as needed 9. Proactively flag what's working and what isn't, and suggest improvements to our targeting, messaging, or tools as you learn the system Must-have requirements • Highly experienced in B2B LinkedIn outreach. Able to show real examples of lists they've built and campaigns/conversations they've run • Excellent written English. Non-negotiable given the calibre of our audience. Messages must not read as ChatGPT/AI-generated • Strong personalisation skills. Comfortable blending templated messaging with bespoke responses depending on the conversation • Experienced with Google Sheets or Excel. This is how we track everything, so comfort building/maintaining a structured tracker is essential • Confident working independently, bringing strategic input, and suggesting improvements to how we run lead generation, not just executing tasks • Confident using tools like Apollo (or similar) for contact enrichment, and comfortable suggesting improvements to how we run our lead generation system we want someone who brings ideas, not just executes tasks Nice-to-have • Experience with ActiveCampaign What you must NOT do • No bots, automation tools, or scraping software. Everything sent manually through LinkedIn/Sales Navigator • Don't ask for an email or pitch anything until there's a genuine signal of interest • Don't use any tool to bulk-source or upload contacts who haven't had a genuine LinkedIn conversation and agreed to hear from us Tools you'll access • LinkedIn/Sales Navigator • Apollo (or similar) for contact enrichment • Our tracker (Google Sheets/Excel) • Our tone/voice guidelines and message templates KPIs we'll track weekly • Quality of lead lists built • Connection requests sent + acceptance rate • Conversations that reached genuine engagement • Emails captured / contacts added to ActiveCampaign. This is the core success metric Pay/experience level Specialist role, not entry-level VA work. Candidates must be able to show examples/portfolio/case study of a B2B LinkedIn campaign they've personally run, including results.

Brief self-introduction. 2. Art mediums you use and are best at. 3. Your availability for long-term continuous work (How many drawings can you finish per week?). 4. Confirmation of agreement regarding rates, shipping workflow, and confidentiality terms. 5. **Samples of your past traditional artwork:** Please attach scanned images or clear photos of your drawings/sketches.

title: Video Editor & Ad Creative Specialist for DTC brand
job_title: Video Editor & Ad Creative Specialist for DTC brand
description: # DTC Performance Video Editor / Creative Strategist We’re looking for an experienced **DTC video editor who understands direct-response creative strategy**, not just someone who can make videos look polished. You’ll be editing Facebook/Instagram/TikTok ads for e-commerce brands using UGC, AI-generated footage, product footage, testimonials, native-style content, statics turned into video, and other direct-response formats. The ideal person understands that a winning ad is more than good editing. You should understand: * Hooks and scroll-stopping first 1–3 seconds * Customer awareness levels * Different marketing angles and avatars * Problem → agitation → mechanism → solution structures * Belief shifts and objection handling * How to visually communicate a mechanism instead of relying only on voiceover * Pattern interrupts * Pacing and retention * When to use captions, B-roll, screenshots, comments, reviews, demonstrations, etc. * Native/UGC-style ads vs overly polished brand ads * How to turn one script into multiple creative variations * Why an ad may have high CTR but poor conversion, or poor hook rate despite strong copy * Direct-response metrics such as hook rate, hold rate, CTR, CPC, CPA, CVR and ROAS ### What You'll Be Doing You'll receive things such as: * Scripts * Hooks * Customer research * Creative briefs * Raw UGC * AI-generated clips * Product footage * Existing winning ads * Competitor references Your job is to turn them into **performance-focused DTC ads**, not simply assemble the clips in the order provided. I want someone who can look at a script and think: "This section is dragging." "The visual isn't proving what the VO is saying." "We need a pattern interrupt here." "This hook needs the result shown before the explanation." "This objection would be stronger with a review screenshot." "We should test three different openings with the same body." In other words, I want an editor who can **think like a creative strategist while editing.** ### Typical Creative Styles You'll work on formats such as: * UGC ads * Native Facebook-style ads * Storytime ads * Advertorial-style video * Problem/solution demonstrations * Before & after concepts * Educational/mechanism ads * Testimonial ads * Reddit/comment-style ads * Founder/expert formats * VSL-style direct-response ads * Mashups * AI UGC + AI B-roll * Competitor-inspired iterations * Hook variations Most videos will be designed for **Meta and TikTok**, usually 9:16. ### What I DON'T Want I'm not looking for an editor whose main focus is: * Cinematic transitions * Fancy motion graphics * Making everything look like a commercial * Random zooms and sound effects with no strategic reason * Following the script blindly * Editing without understanding the target customer A slightly ugly/native ad that converts is more valuable to me than a beautiful ad that doesn't sell. ### Requirements You should have previous experience editing **DTC/e-commerce performance ads**. Please be comfortable with fast testing and iteration. We may produce several variations of the same concept by changing hooks, opening visuals, pacing, proof, CTAs or sections of the body. Experience with Meta ads is especially valuable. Knowledge of tools such as Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, DaVinci Resolve or similar is fine—the specific software matters less than your creative judgment. Experience working with AI-generated creative is a plus. ### When Applying Please send: 1. 3–5 DTC ads you've personally edited. 2. The ad you're most proud of and why you think it worked. 3. Any performance metrics you're allowed to share. 4. An example of an ad where **you contributed to the creative strategy**, rather than simply receiving editing instructions. 5. Your rate per video or preferred pricing structure. 6. Roughly how many ads/variations you can produce per week. Also answer this: **If I give you a 60-second DTC script, what are the first things you think about before you start editing?** I'm specifically looking at your answer to this question because I want someone who understands **performance creative, not just video editing.** ### Paid Trial We'll start with a **paid trial creative**. You'll receive the script, research, product information and available assets. I'm interested not only in the final edit but also in whether you can identify opportunities to improve the hook, visuals, pacing and overall creative before/during the edit. If the trial goes well, there is potential for consistent long-term work producing and iterating DTC creatives.

title: International Business Development & Lead Generation Regulatory Compliance | Flexible Remote Position
job_title: International Business Development & Lead Generation Regulatory Compliance | Flexible Remote Position
description: We are a small international regulatory compliance consulting business looking for a proactive and resourceful professional to support our business development and lead generation activities. You will work directly with an international regulatory consultant who helps manufacturers, exporters, and brands comply with regulatory requirements when selling products in the United States, Canada, Europe, and other international markets. This is a highly flexible, results-oriented position with a monthly base payment plus commission on every client you successfully originate. Previous experience in regulatory compliance, FDA-regulated industries, international trade, or import/export compliance is a major advantage for this position. - What You Will Do: Your primary responsibility will be active B2B lead generation. Rather than waiting for inbound inquiries, you will proactively identify companies that are exporting products internationally and may need regulatory compliance services. Your activities will include: * Researching potential clients using public FDA databases and other online sources; * Identifying companies listed on FDA Import Alerts; * Researching recent FDA Import Refusals and other publicly available FDA enforcement information; * Finding manufacturers and exporters that sell or intend to sell products in the United States, Canada, and Europe; * Researching company websites, LinkedIn, Google, industry directories, trade databases, and other sources to identify relevant companies and decision-makers; * Finding valid company and business contact information; * Sending personalized outreach emails using our company email account; * Introducing our regulatory compliance services to potential clients; * Following up with prospects who have not responded; * Keeping an organized spreadsheet/lead tracker showing every company contacted, contact information, date of contact, follow-ups, responses, and current status; * Handling initial commercial communication with interested prospects. You are also welcome to suggest and test your own lead-generation strategies. Cold calling is optional, if you are comfortable with calls and believe they can help generate business, you may use them, but calls are not required. - What Happens When a Prospect Is Interested? You do NOT need to be a regulatory expert. Your role is to identify opportunities, initiate the conversation, qualify interest, and generate the lead. Once a prospect begins asking detailed regulatory questions or demonstrates serious interest in hiring us, the lead will be transferred directly to the regulatory consultant, who will handle the technical discussion, define the scope, quote the project, and close the sale. Our services include, among others: * FDA Import Alert remediation and removal assistance; * FDA Import Detention and Refusal assistance; * FDA Food Facility Registration and renewal; * U.S. Agent services; * FSVP compliance; * FDA Prior Notice; * FDA regulatory registrations and product listings; * Food, dietary supplement, cosmetic and OTC compliance; * Label and claims compliance; * Import/export regulatory consulting; * U.S., Canadian and European regulatory compliance. There are many opportunities to identify companies that already have an immediate regulatory need. For example, companies appearing in FDA enforcement and import databases may already be experiencing an import compliance issue. There is also an important immediate sales opportunity: the 2026 FDA Food Facility biennial registration renewal period runs from October through December. Food facilities required to register with FDA must renew their registrations during this period. - Compensation: US$50 guaranteed monthly base + 5% commission on every successfully paid client contract originated by you. There are no fixed daily working hours and no required shift. This position is designed to be extremely flexible. title: AutoCad Designer
description: We are seeking a skilled AutoCAD Designer with specialized experience in water engineering and fitting development. In this role, you will bridge the gap between initial concept and production. You will work directly with our engineering team to translate complex ideas, rough sketches, and functional requirements into precise 2D and 3D manufacturing models. The ideal candidate has deep expertise in standard flange configurations, pressure ratings, and designing components suitable for moulding, casting, and precision machining. Key Responsibilities Concept to Model: Translate napkin sketches, verbal concepts, and functional specs into detailed, manufacturable AutoCAD models and production drawings. Component Design: Design a wide array of water fittings, flanges, compression seals, adapters, and custom inline components. Manufacturing Readiness: Prepare production-ready files tailored for injection moulding, sand/investment casting, or CNC machining—accounting for draft angles, wall thicknesses, and tolerances. Standards & Compliance: Ensure all CAD designs comply with relevant water industry standards, pressure classes, bolt patterns, and flange specifications (e.g., ANSI/ASME, DIN, or local water authority specs). Design Iteration: Collaborate closely with engineers and product managers to refine designs based on prototype testing and manufacturing feedback. Documentation: Maintain accurate BOMs (Bills of Materials), revision histories, and technical specification sheets. Qualifications & Requirements Software Expertise: Mastery of AutoCAD (2D drafting & 3D modeling); proficiency in SolidWorks or Autodesk Inventor is a strong plus. Domain Knowledge: Proven background in water engineering, industrial piping, pressure systems, and fluid management. Flange & Fitting Design: Strong working knowledge of flange standards, gasket seats, mechanical joint profiles, and pressure-retaining fittings. Manufacturing Processes: Solid understanding of how components are manufactured, specifically moulding, casting, and machining, to ensure designs are optimized for production. Technical Communication: Ability to visualize abstract engineering concepts and ask the right questions to extract key requirements. Detail-Oriented: Exceptional spatial awareness and accuracy in dimensioning, geometric tolerancing (GD&T), and material selection.

job_title: Direct Response Video Editor for Meta Ads for Medical Clinics (Batch Editing)
salary_detail: Paid Trial First into Full -Time Hire
description: Read this whole post before applying. The instructions at the bottom are part of the test. WHO WE ARE Novaris Global. We run paid advertising for private medical clinics, mostly plastic surgery and aesthetics. Our clients are in Singapore and we are expanding. Our ads run on Meta. When they work, the clinic books consultations. When they don't, we lose money. That is the entire scoreboard. THE MAIN THING YOU WOULD BE DOING Once or twice a month a doctor sits down and records for 30 to 60 minutes straight. He works through a stack of scripts, flubs lines, restarts, goes off on tangents, repeats himself, and says something better on the third take than he did on the first. Nobody slates the takes. Nobody marks where one ad ends. It is one long messy file. Out of that single file we need 30 to 60 finished Meta video ads. Not 30 exports of the same cut. Thirty to sixty ads that each open differently, run differently, and feel like they came from different creatives. That is how Meta finds a winner, and it is the actual skill we are hiring for. That means you: - Watch the whole file and map what is really in there - D ---------- where one ad ends and the next one starts - Pick the strongest take of every line, not the first one - Cut the sentences that add nothing. Warm ups, throat clearing, repeated ideas, and the line that is technically true but kills the pace - Reorder freely. If the best hook is something he said at minute 34, that line goes to second zero - Recombine. The same three sentences in a different order, with a different opening line and a different first ten seconds, is a different ad - Build each one properly. On screen text in the first two seconds, burned in captions throughout, a lower third with his name and clinic, b-roll, sound design, graphics, end card THE OTHER TWO KINDS OF WORK Not everything arrives as a batch. Some weeks you get a single clip and a brief and we need one sharp ad out of it by tomorrow. And some weeks you get a video sales letter. Long form, five to twenty minutes, a doctor walking through an argument end to end. Completely different edit. The hook still has to land in the first few seconds, but now you are holding attention for fifteen minutes instead of thirty seconds, which means pacing, chapter beats, visual variety, and knowing exactly where a viewer gets bored and what to put there. If you have never cut long form, say so honestly. If you have, lead with it. EVERY AD HAS TO FEEL DIFFERENT This is the part almost every editor fails. When you cut 40 ads from one recording, the lazy version is one template with 40 different hooks dropped in. Meta sees through it, the audience sees through it, and the account stalls. We want visible variety across the set. Different caption styles. Different graphic treatments. One ad that leans on text animation, one that is almost bare and lets him talk, one built around a simple diagram, one with heavier b-roll, one that opens on a graphic before he appears. Different rhythms. Different energy. Someone scrolling should never think they have already seen this ad. Play around. Have opinions. Show us range. THE LINE YOU CANNOT CROSS WHILE DOING IT This is a surgeon, not a dropshipper. Every one of those 40 ads still has to look expensive, clean, and calm. Variety in style, never variety in standards. No meme zooms. No shake. No cartoon sound effects. No AI voice. No stock footage of a family smiling at sunset. If an edit would look at home selling a phone case, it is wrong for us. The hard version of this job is doing both at once. Retention editing that actually holds attention, inside a look a private surgeon would put his name on. Most editors can do one or the other. Medical advertising in Singapore is also regulated, and moves that are normal everywhere else are illegal there. No before and after footage. No testimonials. No "best" or "guaranteed." No countdowns or scarcity. We give you the full rule sheet on day one, but you have to be someone who follows a rule sheet exactly, every time, without being reminded. WHAT YOU NEED TO ALREADY KNOW - Hook rate and hold rate, and what actually moves them. If your answer to a weak hook is "add a zoom," this role is not for you - The first two seconds carry on screen text, because most of Meta watches on mute - A retention beat every few seconds. A cut, a caption change, a graphic, a b-roll insert. Something has to change or they are gone - Captions readable at arm's length on a phone, inside Meta's safe zones, not sitting under the interface - Sound design that supports the point instead of decorating it. A whoosh on every cut is amateur work - 9:16 at 1080x1920, correct loudness, correct export settings, and a first frame that is not a blink - Written English strong enough to judge a sentence. You are d ---------- which of a surgeon's sentences survive. That takes real comprehension, not just an ear for rhythm NICE TO HAVE, NOT REQUIRED If you can write, say so. If you can watch a raw recording and tell us "he never said the thing that would make this ad work, here is what he should say next time," that is worth more to us than another year of Premiere experience, and it changes what we pay you. THE SETUP - Full time, 40 hours a week - Your own machine that handles 4K without taking an hour to export - Reliable internet, because you are moving large files - Premiere, After Effects, DaVinci, CapCut, whatever you like. We care about the output, not your toolkit - You work directly with me. Small team, no layers, fast decisions HOW THIS STARTS A paid trial. Real footage, a real brief, real money for your time. We are not going to pretend a reel tells us anything. Plenty of great reels were cut by somebody else. The trial tells us what you actually do when a messy file lands in your lap. If the work comes back genuinely excellent, and we mean excellent and not acceptable, we move straight to a full time offer. If it does not, you keep the money and we part on good terms. BEFORE YOU D ---------- THIS IS TOO MUCH WORK Yes, this application asks more of you than the other posts on this site. That is deliberate. So here is the honest math on what you are applying to. We are hiring one person, once. Whoever we pick stops applying for jobs. You are not applying to a task. You are applying to a department that does not exist yet, with your name on it. Right now every video for every client we have runs through one folder and one to do list. The person we hire builds what replaces that. You set the standard. You make the templates every editor after you works from. You hire those editors and review their work instead of doing it. Head of Video, across every account, fully in house. Not a freelancer we message when something comes up. On the team, in the meetings, in the decisions. You will also see the money side, which almost no editor anywhere gets to see. Hook rate on your cuts. Cost per lead. Which clinic booked how many consultations off which edit. That feedback loop is the entire difference between an editor who is good at software and an editor who is worth whatever they ask for, for the rest of their career. We will hand it to you. And here is why we can pay for that. Our clients do not pay us a flat fee. We take a share of the revenue we generate for them. When your ad wins, we do not save money, we make more of it. So we would far rather pay one exceptional editor well beyond what this platform normally pays than hire five cheap ones and manage them. Your ceiling here is not an hourly rate. It grows with the accounts you are cutting for. A few hours today. If we are right about each other, you will look back on this as the best few hours you ever spent on an application. If none of that moves you, please do not apply. We would rather read ten serious applications than a hundred lazy ones. HOW TO APPLY Do all four. Applications missing any of them get deleted unread. Two of these are what we actually judge: the ads you have already cut, and what you cut for us. The other two take a minute each. Spend your time on the first two. 1. Make THUMBSTOP the first word of your message. 2. Send three to five direct response video ads you personally cut. What counts: ads that actually ran as paid media on Meta, TikTok, or YouTube. Something built to make a stranger take an action. What does not count and will get your application closed: showreels, montages, wedding films, YouTube intros, vlogs, corporate brand videos, event recaps, anything cut to music with no message. Do not send a reel. Send the ads themselves, full length, exactly as they ran. We watch from the first frame, because the first frame is the job. For each one, one line covering: - Who it was for and what it was selling - Whether it ran as paid media, and roughly what it spent if you know - Any numbers you have. Hook rate, hold rate, CTR, cost per result. If you have none, say none. We would rather hear that than a guess - What you personally did on it, honestly. If you cut it start to finish, say so. If you did captions and graphics on somebody else's assembly, say that instead. We will find out either way, and the honest answer has never cost anyone the job If your strongest work is under an NDA, send what you can and tell us what we are missing. 3. Cut something from this file: ---------- THE MINIMUM is five seconds. Just the hook. The opening that would stop someone scrolling, with whatever on screen text, sound, graphics, and cutting you think earns those five seconds. Start from any moment in the file you want. A genuinely strong five seconds is enough to get you shortlisted. THE FULL AD IS BETTER. If you send a finished ad cut from this file, hook through to end card with captions all the way, we will watch every second of it and you go to the top of the pile. It is not required. It is an opportunity, and the people who take it are usually the people we hire. Either way, in two or three sentences: why that moment, why that treatment, and what you cut out and why. Do not post this footage anywhere public. 4. Answer this in writing. You receive a 45 minute file of a surgeon recording what he thinks are eight ads. He goes off script constantly and the single best line he says is at minute 38. What do you do in your first hour, before you cut anything? And how do you get 40 genuinely different ads out of it instead of 40 versions of one? Shortlisted applicants go straight to a paid trial on real client footage.

job_title: Experienced Amazon Online Arbitrage Product Sourcer — Keepa + SellerAmp Required
description: # Experienced Amazon Online Arbitrage Product Sourcer — Keepa + SellerAmp Required **Type:** Part-Time with potential to become Full-Time **Hours:** 20 hours per week **Starting Pay:** $7–$8 USD/hour, based on demonstrated experience **Location:** Remote — **Position:** Long-term for the right person ## About the Role Arkadia Arbitrage is a U.S.-based ecommerce business looking for a **highly experienced Amazon Online Arbitrage Product Sourcer**. This is **not an entry-level Amazon VA position** and it is not a general ecommerce assistant role. Your primary responsibility will be simple: **Find legitimate, profitable, purchase-ready inventory opportunities for our Amazon FBA business.** We are specifically looking for someone who already knows how to source independently using tools such as **Keepa, Revseller and SellerAmp SAS, and who understands the difference between a product that looks profitable at first glance and an opportunity that is actually safe and sensible to purchase.** You should already be comfortable analyzing: * Keepa price and Buy Box history * Sales velocity * Amazon sales rank / BSR * Seller competition * FBA seller counts * Price stability * ROI and net profit * Amazon presence on a listing * Variations and pack counts * Exact product matching * UPC / model number verification * Purchase limits and available quantity * Seller eligibility / restrictions * Potential IP or listing risks **This position is focused specifically on Amazon FBA sourcing. Walmart, eBay, customer service, listing management, and general administrative work are not part of this role.** ## What You Will Do You will use online arbitrage sourcing strategies to identify profitable products from legitimate U.S. retailers and suppliers. Sourcing methods may include: * Manual sourcing * Reverse sourcing * Storefront stalking * Brand sourcing * Retailer sourcing * Keepa Product Finder * Category and product research * Other proven OA sourcing techniques you already use successfully You will document qualified opportunities in our sourcing tracker with accurate supporting information. We already maintain a large internal list of brands and products that our Amazon account is eligible to sell. You will therefore have clear sourcing areas to explore rather than starting completely from scratch. ## Our General Buying Standards Qualified leads will generally need to meet standards such as: * **30%+ ROI** * **$3+ estimated net profit per unit** * **30+ estimated monthly sales** * Reasonable seller competition, generally no more than approximately 15–20 FBA sellers * Stable enough pricing to support the purchase * Exact product / listing match * Correct size, count, variation, model, and UPC where applicable * Product available from a legitimate retailer or supplier * Meaningful quantity available for purchase These are guidelines rather than an invitation to submit borderline products just because they technically reach a number. **Quality matters more than quantity.** Our goal is approximately **1–2 strong, genuinely actionable sourcing opportunities daily and 4-5 per week**, with enough available inventory behind those opportunities to support meaningful purchasing. For example: **Four excellent leads supporting $950 of sensible inventory purchases are more valuable to us than five weak leads supporting only $200.** A lead only counts as successful when it is something we could reasonably purchase—not simply because it was entered into a spreadsheet. ## Required Experience Please apply only if you already have significant hands-on experience sourcing Online Arbitrage products for Amazon FBA. You should be proficient with: * **Keepa** * **SellerAmp SAS** * Amazon product and listing analysis * Google Sheets * Online Arbitrage sourcing You should be able to look at a Keepa chart and explain what the pricing and sales history tells you rather than simply reporting the current Buy Box price. You should also understand that two products that look similar are **not automatically the same product**. Exact UPC, model, quantity, packaging, flavor, color, size, or variation differences must be investigated before recommending a purchase. ## What We Are Looking For The ideal person: * Has successfully sourced profitable OA products for other Amazon sellers * Can work independently without constant training * Is analytical and detail-oriented * Understands Amazon listing risk * Does not submit leads just to meet a quota * Communicates clearly when something is questionable * Is willing to reject a lead when the data does not support buying it * Can explain the reasoning behind their recommendations * Wants a stable, long-term position with a growing ecommerce business We value **accuracy, judgment, and purchasing value** more than raw lead volume. ## Paid Sourcing Test Strong applicants will be invited to complete a **paid sourcing test** before a final hiring decision is made. You will receive specific sourcing criteria and will be asked to locate a small number of real OA opportunities. The test will evaluate: * Product matching accuracy * Keepa analysis * Profitability analysis * Sales and competition analysis * Source quality * Available purchasing quantity * Overall judgment You will be paid for the test regardless of whether you are ultimately selected. ## How to Apply Begin your application with the words: **Arkadia SOURCING** Applications that do not include those words will not be considered. Then answer the following questions: 1. How many years have you personally sourced Online Arbitrage products for Amazon FBA? 2. Which sourcing methods do you use most often? Please be specific. 3. How would you describe your experience level with Keepa and SellerAmp? 4. When reviewing a Keepa chart, what are the most important things you examine before recommending that a client purchase inventory? 5. How do you verify that a retailer's product is an exact match to the Amazon listing? 6. Describe one successful OA product you previously sourced. You may remove or hide the actual product name/ASIN if necessary, but please provide the approximate: * Purchase cost * Amazon selling price * Profit * ROI * Estimated sales * Quantity the client was able to purchase 7. Approximately how many **purchase-ready** OA opportunities were you typically able to provide clients in a 20-hour workweek? 8. Are you currently working for other Amazon sellers? If yes, approximately how many hours per week? 9. Please tell us why you believe you would be a strong fit for a role focused specifically on **high-quality Amazon OA sourcing**. Please do not send a generic application describing every type of virtual-assistant work you can perform. We are specifically hiring an experienced Amazon OA product sourcer. Thank you. We look forward to hearing from you.

title: Video Editor
description: Hi — I'm Dylan. I run a land investing company in the US. We buy raw land, and over the next four months I'm filming a weekly YouTube series documenting me rebuilding one part of the business completely from scratch — the real version, including the parts that don't work. I'm looking for one editor to own all of the video output. Not a project. An ongoing role through the end of the year and beyond if it goes well. What you'd be editing every week 1 long-form YouTube episode — 12 to 20 minutes, documentary / vlog style 4–5 short-form clips cut from that same footage, for Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts 1 thumbnail per episode, generated using AI image tools The raw footage is deliberately messy: recorded phone calls, screen recordings of software, me talking to camera, and calls with my team. Your job is turning that pile into something people actually finish watching. What I actually care about Retention. Tight cuts, no dead air, no 30-second intro. If three seconds are boring, they're gone. You can find the story in the footage. I'm not handing you a script or a shot list. You get the footage and a few lines about what the episode is about. If you need to be told exactly what to do with every clip, this isn't the right role. Clean on-screen text and simple graphics — numbers, labels, callouts. Not motion design. Readable and consistent. Captions on everything. You hit deadlines without me chasing you. This is the big one. Requirements Real experience editing long-form YouTube — talking head, vlog, or documentary style. Please don't apply if your portfolio is only wedding videos, corporate explainers, or gaming montages. It's a different skill and I'll be able to tell. Strong short-form skills. You understand that the first second d ---------- whether the other 29 get watched. Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or Final Cut. CapCut is fine for shorts. Comfortable making thumbnails with AI image tools (Midjourney, Nano Banana, Photoshop generative fill — whatever you actually use). I don't need a graphic designer. I need someone who can iterate on a thumbnail fast. Written English good enough to understand my notes and to ask me a question when something is unclear. Reliable internet and the ability to move large video files without drama. Nice to have You watch business / finance YouTube and know what good looks like in this space Experience cutting recorded sales or phone calls into watchable segments You have opinions about editing and are willing to tell me when I'm wrong about something Hours, pay, and how we'd work Part-time, roughly 15–20 hours per week $800/month to start, moving to $1,000/month after a 60-day review if the work is good You set your own hours. I care about deadlines, not when you work. I'm in California (PST). Weekly rhythm: I drop the footage Friday, you deliver a first cut Monday, revisions and shorts Tuesday, we publish Tuesday. First episode publishes September 16, so I'm hiring this week. Paid on time, every time, twice a month. How to apply Put LAND SERIES in the subject line, and include: Links to 2 long-form videos you edited — tell me specifically which decisions were yours Links to 2 short-form videos you edited One thumbnail you made with AI, and which tool you used What software you edit in How many hours per week you have available right now Answer this: what's one thing you would cut from almost every YouTube video to make it better? I won't read applications without "LAND SERIES" in the subject line or without portfolio links. Shortlisted applicants get a paid test project — I'll send you real footage and pay you for one short edit before I d ---------- . I don't ask people to work for free. Thanks for reading this far, Dylan

title: Marketing Lead

Marketing campaign execution They should be able to take a commercial goal such as: Launch a new collection Increase online revenue Promote a seasonal offer Improve customer retention Launch a new website Introduce a new service And convert it into: Campaign objective Core message Offer Content angles Static concepts Video concepts Organic content Paid creative requirements Email campaign requirements Schedule Deadlines Responsibilities Launch plan They should not wait for you to prescribe every individual post. You provide the higher-level diagnosis and direction. They build and execute the campaign around it. 4. Process building This should be an explicit part of the role—not something you hope they do eventually. They should build and continuously improve: Client onboarding workflow Brand immersion process Campaign planning template Content calendar system Creative briefing template Static ad production workflow Video editing workflow Approval process Content scheduling process Shoot planning system Asset naming and file storage Weekly client review process Performance-to-creative feedback loop Client offboarding or handover process Each time they complete a task, they should ask: “How do we turn this into a system that someone else can follow?” That is how the role evolves from doing everything themselves into eventually managing a larger creative team. 5. Content operations They should own the full flow from idea to publication: Strategy ? concept ? brief ? production ? review ? approval ? scheduling ? performance review That includes: Ensuring content is planned ahead Briefing editors Briefing creators Creating static assets Reviewing initial edits Managing client approvals Maintaining content reserves Scheduling approved content Flagging missing assets Reporting what performed Updating future creative based on results They own whether content is ready—not merely whether they sent someone a message about it. 6. Client activation This is especially important for solving your current bottleneck. Once you close a new client, the Marketing Manager should be capable of moving them through: Onboarding Access collection Brand immersion Existing asset review Campaign priorities Visual direction Content plan Creative briefs Production Approval Scheduling Active campaign delivery You should still lead strategic workshops and major commercial decisions, but the Marketing Manager should drive the client from signed to operational. What the role is not The main Meta buyer A full-time video editor A website developer A customer service assistant A project manager who produces nothing A social media scheduler waiting for instructions A junior designer who cannot make campaign decisions They need to combine creative judgement, hands-on production and operational ownership. The ideal candidate profile You are looking for someone who is: Creatively led Commercially aware Strong at static design Extremely organised Capable of building systems Comfortable taking ownership Able to give clear feedback to editors Interested in brands, campaigns and consumer psychology Fast without becoming careless Able to move between fashion, health, beauty, travel and other clients Confident enough to challenge weak creative Resourceful enough to solve problems without waiting for you Their portfolio should show more than attractive posts. title: Wordpress Ecommerce Website Developer and Graphic Designer
job_title: Wordpress Ecommerce Website Developer and Graphic Designer
description: We're redesigning the visual and front-end layer of our brand ecosystem. There are two distinct tracks below. Apply to one or both — tell us clearly which. Most applicants should apply to one. We'd rather hire two specialists than one generalist who is adequate at both. Track A — Graphic Design & 3D Product Visualization The work 1. Product render library (primary deliverable) We need a consistent, photorealistic render set covering our full catalog of roughly 18 SKUs — lyophilized powder in glass vials with blue aluminum crimp caps, plus a small number of liquid products. We already have one render that defines the target quality: a 3/4-angle GLP-TZ vial, studio lighting, transparent background. That image is the standard. Every other SKU needs to match it — same camera angle, same lighting setup, same shadow treatment, same crop ratio. Consistency matters more than individual image quality here. A catalog grid where every vial sits at a slightly different angle is what makes a brand read as small. Deliverables per SKU: transparent PNG at high resolution, plus white-background WebP optimized for web. Source files (Blender/C4D/KeyShot scene) delivered at project close. Critical: all label text must be pixel-accurate to the artwork we supply. Compound name, milligram strength, and disclaimer text are non-negotiable. Our customers are technically literate and a garbled label destroys trust instantly. If you work with AI-assisted generation, we need real artwork composited in post rather than model-generated text. 2. Presentation packaging visualization We have 2,500 magnetic-closure presentation boxes in inventory: neutral white, square footprint, front-flap magnetic latch producing a visible horizontal seam roughly one-fifth of the box width in height. We need renders of these with our artwork applied, in both standalone and vial-composite arrangements. 3. Web design comps Figma comps for homepage and a representative product page. This is the spec our developer builds against, so we need real specificity: type scale, spacing system, component states, mobile and desktop breakpoints, motion and interaction direction. Not a static picture of a page. Aesthetic direction Think Apple restraint crossed with pharmaceutical clinical credibility. Pure neutral white backgrounds. Generous whitespace. Navy on white — not dark mode. Clean geometric sans typography. Nothing decorative, nothing "supplement industry," no gradients-and-glow wellness styling. Reference for the level of front-end polish we're targeting: ---------- . We have documented brand standards, a locked color palette, and existing logo artwork. You'll receive all of it. Track B — Front-End / WooCommerce Development The work Implement approved Figma comps on our existing WordPress store. Homepage, product pages, catalog grid, and mobile treatment across all of it. This is an implementation role, not a design role. You'll be building against an approved comp. Success is binary: does the live page match the file. We're not asking you to make aesthetic calls, and we won't ask you to guess what we want. Mobile quality is weighted heavily. Most of our traffic is mobile and it's where most builds fall apart. Technical environment — read this before quoting Being straight about the constraints, because they're real and they've cost us debugging time. We have all of this documented and will share the full runbook with shortlisted candidates. WordPress + WooCommerce + Astra 4.13 + Elementor Pro on Hostinger, PHP 8.3 No child theme currently exists. Astra runs as the parent theme, so custom PHP lives in the Code Snippets plugin rather than in version-controlled files. Migrating to a proper child theme with a git repo and rsync deploy is a possible additional scope item — a build brief already exists for it. The host WAF rejects REST request bodies containing literal script or meta tags — 403 or a silent 500. Existing code works around this with wp_enqueue_* and wp_add_inline_script rather than echoing tags. The firewall does plain substring matching, so even tag text inside a PHP comment trips it. LiteSpeed caches aggressively and does not auto-purge on Code Snippets writes, because that plugin uses its own database table and never fires save_post. Manual purge required after every snippet change. Elementor page structure lives in _elementor_data, a single JSON blob that is not exposed to REST. The homepage alone is 159 widgets. Current work is done through render filters rather than by writing to that blob. Two separate snippet plugins are in play — Code Snippets (REST-accessible) and WPCode (not). Some existing CSS is only reachable through wp-admin. Airlift and LiteSpeed both defer JavaScript until first interaction. A previous client-side product grid rendered empty on load. Rendering happens in PHP for that reason. Don't move it back to the client. Also running: AIOSEO, AffiliateWP, Solid Security, PixelYourSite, Omnisend, Woo Discount Rules, and OTTO (Search Atlas), which rewrites headings client-side.

job_title: Short-Form Video Editor - Hormozi-Style Content & Motion Graphics (Long-Term Team Role)
salary_detail: $30 per finished video, negotiable on qu
description: WHO WE ARE MSET is a US marketing agency running paid lead generation for local service businesses. This role edits for MSET itself: our short-form content, our VSLs, our caption-heavy videos. The videos you cut carry real ad spend behind them, so they have to look and feel professional every single time. This is not a churn-out-clips content mill. READ THIS FIRST We are hiring a team member, not a gig worker. Someone we can rely on long term, who becomes part of how this agency operates and grows with it. The per-video pay is how we start, not what this is. And this is not a beginner role: if you are new to editing or new to motion graphics, do not apply. You will not pass the test and it will waste your time and ours. One more thing. This post contains everything we require, and we do not take anyone seriously who applies without reading all of it. Your application will show us whether you did. THE JOB We send you raw talking-head footage plus a script or outline. You turn it into a finished Hormozi-style short: kinetic captions synced to the voice, motion graphics that punch the key moments, b-roll and zoom cuts that keep the pace moving, sound design that makes every graphic land. The edit's job is retention: a viewer who meant to scroll past is still watching 40 seconds later. THE MOTION GRAPHICS BAR This is the main thing we are hiring for, so here is exactly what we mean by high quality: - Graphics that serve retention: keyword pops, animated emphasis, icons and visual callouts that hit exactly on the beat of the voice, not floating decoration. - Clean, professional typography. Deliberate timing. Motion that looks designed, not dragged from a template pack. - Restraint. The best Hormozi-style edits know when to let a sentence breathe. Wall-to-wall effects is a beginner tell. - Hand-built work. We are not looking for someone who uses AI to generate these graphics. We can tell the difference, and so can the audience our ad spend is paying to reach. AI-generated graphic work in your portfolio or your test will not pass. WHAT YOU MUST ALREADY KNOW - Hooks. The first 2 seconds d ---------- the whole video: first frame, opening line on screen, pattern interrupt. - Retention pacing. No dead air, cuts that ride the voiceover, energy that builds instead of flatlines. - Muted-first editing. Most feeds autoplay silent. Captions and graphics have to carry the video with the sound off. - Caption craft. Emphasis on the words that carry the point, not random highlighting. - The Hormozi style specifically: you have studied it, you have cut in it, and you know why it holds attention. DELIVERABLES AND STANDARDS - 9:16 as the primary deliverable, other ratios when we ask. - MP4, H.264, captions burned in. - Music and sound effects only from sources you hold rights to. Watermarked or unlicensed audio is an automatic reject, no exceptions. - One revision pass included per video. We send notes in a single batch, you apply them once, done. - Edit in whatever software you want. We judge output, not tools. NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS - Real, provable experience editing short-form content with serious motion graphics work, for creators, agencies, or businesses that had money riding on the videos. - A real portfolio we can open: a reel, a site, or an organized Drive folder of your work. No portfolio, no consideration. - You can take raw footage plus an outline and come back with something excellent, without a call, without twenty questions. - Reliable on deadlines, every single time. We run content calendars. A late video is a missed slot. One missed deadline without warning ends the engagement. - Attention to detail, because a misspelled caption or an off-beat graphic reads amateur instantly. - Responsive on WhatsApp or Messenger during agreed hours, with honest ETAs. "It will be late, here is when" is acceptable. Silence is not. - You take notes without ego and apply them precisely. DO NOT APPLY IF - You are a beginner or still learning the basics. This is not a starter role. - Your motion graphics come from AI generators or untouched template packs. - You want a one-off gig instead of a seat on a team. - You need every cut dictated to you. - Your portfolio has no caption-heavy, graphics-driven work in it. - You juggle so many clients that 48-hour turnarounds scare you. BONUS POINTS - You have cut for business, marketing, or money channels in the Hormozi and Iman Gadzhi lane. - Your sound design game is strong: whooshes, hits, and risers that make graphics feel physical. - You have seen the performance data on your own edits and changed how you cut because of it. PAY AND GROWTH $30 per finished video, and the rate is negotiable up on quality: show us you cut at the level we are looking for and we pay for it. Work comes in batches as we need it, not on a fixed schedule. The goal is one editor who owns the MSET look long term. Paid through Wise, on time, every time. HOW TO APPLY Reply with the word CUTS as your first line. Then: a link to your full portfolio (reel, site, or organized Drive folder), links to 3 shorts you personally edited with your strongest motion graphics work in them, and one sentence on which of the 3 you would redo today and why. We check applications against every instruction in this post, including ones not repeated in this section. Miss any of them and you get skipped unread. NEXT STEP Shortlisted editors get a paid $20 test edit: our footage, our outline, 48-hour turnaround. The test is the interview. Pass it and the real work starts. ONE LAST THING Put the word KEYFRAME in the title of your application. That is how we know you read the whole post. No KEYFRAME in the title, no reply.
