description: WHO WE ARE MSET is a US marketing agency running paid lead generation for local service businesses: contractors, roofers, remodelers, home services, and similar trades. Our ads run on Facebook and Instagram, and they exist to do exactly one thing: make a homeowner stop scrolling and fill out a form. Every editing decision gets judged against that. Views mean nothing to us. Leads are the scoreboard. READ THIS FIRST We are hiring a team member, not a gig worker. Someone we can rely on every single week, long term, who becomes part of how this agency operates and grows with it. The per-video pay is how we start, not what this is. And this is not a beginner role: if you are new to editing or new to ads, do not apply. You will not pass the test and it will waste your time and ours. One more thing. This post contains everything we require, and we do not take anyone seriously who applies without reading all of it. Your application will show us whether you did. THE JOB You edit our ad creatives. We send you raw footage (real job sites, real crews, real talking-head takes) plus a written outline: the hook, the angle, the offer, the CTA. You turn that into a finished, high-performing ad that could go live the same day. The outline tells you what the ad says. You d ---------- how it hits: pacing, caption emphasis, b-roll choices, sound design, where the cut lands. That judgment is what we are paying for. WHAT WE MEAN WHEN WE SAY YOU MUST KNOW MARKETING This is the part most applicants fail, so read it carefully. We are not hiring a technical editor who waits to be told where to cut. You need to already understand, from experience: - Hooks. Why the first 2 seconds d ---------- the whole ad. First-frame choice, opening line on screen, visual pattern interrupts, and how a hook changes when the audience is a homeowner with a problem versus a bored scroller. - Retention. Scene changes every 2 to 3 seconds, no dead air, cuts that ride the voiceover, caption emphasis on the words that carry the claim. - Muted-first editing. Most of Meta autoplays silent. If your ad needs audio to work, it does not work. - Direct-response structure. Problem, agitation, proof, offer, CTA, and how to compress that into 30 seconds without it feeling rushed. - The formats that win in lead gen, and when each one fits: owner talking direct to camera, job-site walkthroughs, before/after transformations, testimonial cuts, UGC-style phone footage, offer-led ads, VSL-style longer cuts. - The offer. Why the hook and the offer have to match, and why a beautiful ad with a buried offer loses to an ugly ad with a clear one. If you read that list and it felt like your day job, keep reading. If it felt like a course syllabus, stop here. AI GENERATION SKILLS (TELL US IF YOU HAVE THIS) We also want editors who have used AI video generation to assist an edit: Higgsfield especially, or similar tools, plus the prompt-writing skill to get usable output. To be clear about the role AI plays here: our ads are cut from real footage, and AI generation fills gaps: a b-roll shot we could not film, a transition, an accent element. You are never generating a whole ad from a prompt, and an application built on fully AI-made videos will not pass. If you have used AI this way, say so in your application and show an example. DELIVERABLES AND STANDARDS - Every ad delivered in both 9:16 and 4:5. - MP4, H.264, captions burned in, safe margins respected for every Meta placement. - Music and sound effects only from sources you hold rights to. Watermarked or unlicensed audio is an automatic reject and ends the test, no exceptions, because it puts ad accounts at risk. - One revision pass included per video. We send notes in a single batch, you apply them once, done. - Edit in whatever software you want. We judge output, not tools. NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS - Real, provable experience editing ad creatives or short-form content for lead gen or local service businesses. Not music videos, not gaming content, not wedding films. - A real portfolio we can open: a reel, a site, or an organized Drive folder of your work. No portfolio, no consideration. - You can take a folder of raw clips plus a one-page outline and come back with something high-performing, without a call, without twenty questions. - Reliable on deadlines, every single time. We run ad calendars. A late video is a missed launch. One missed deadline without warning ends the engagement. - Attention to detail, because a wrong caption or a missed spec burns ad spend. - Responsive on WhatsApp or Messenger during agreed hours, with honest ETAs. "It will be late, here is when" is acceptable. Silence is not. - You take notes without ego and apply them precisely. DO NOT APPLY IF - You are a beginner or still learning the basics. This is not a starter role. - You have never edited an ad that actually ran with money behind it. - You want a one-off gig instead of a seat on a team. - You need every cut dictated to you. - Your portfolio is cinematic montages with no captions and no CTA. - You juggle so many clients that 48-hour turnarounds scare you. BONUS POINTS - You have edited for contractors, roofers, remodelers, cleaners, or other home services. - You have seen the performance data on your own edits and changed how you cut because of it. - You can suggest a stronger hook than the outline gives you, and you are right. PAY AND GROWTH $15 per finished ad, and the rate is negotiable up on quality: show us you cut at the level we are looking for and we pay for it. Steady weekly volume for editors who deliver consistently. For the right person this grows past editing into a creative strategist role: choosing the angles, writing the outlines, owning creative performance. Paid through Wise, on time, every time. We are hiring a long-term team member and we want this to become your anchor client. HOW TO APPLY Reply with the word HOOKS as your first line. Then: a link to your full portfolio (reel, site, or organized Drive folder), links to 3 ads you personally edited that actually ran for real businesses (say so plainly if any were spec), one sentence on which of the 3 hooks you would rewrite today and why, and a note on any AI video generation experience (Higgsfield or similar) with an example if you have one. We check applications against every instruction in this post, including ones not repeated in this section. Miss any of them and you get skipped unread. NEXT STEP Shortlisted editors get a paid $20 test edit: our footage, our outline, 48-hour turnaround. The test is the interview. Pass it and weekly volume starts immediately. ONE LAST THING Put the word SAWDUST in the title of your application. That is how we know you read the whole post. No SAWDUST in the title, no reply.

Are you better Tuesday morning or Wednesday?" SCHEDULE Monday to Friday, 10:00 PM - 2:00 AM Philippine Standard Time. This aligns with late morning in Texas, which is when these owners answer their phones. 20 hours per week to start. This is a permanent night shift - please do not apply unless you can hold this schedule consistently. COMPENSATION AND TERMS - Salary as listed above, paid twice monthly, on time, every time - Paid one-week trial period before any long-term commitment on either side - Performance review at 90 days. If you hit target, the role moves to full time at an increased rate, plus a bonus on every appointment that converts to a signed client - Philippine public holidays observed - Paid time off after 6 months - Written agreement provided before you start - you will know exactly what you're agreeing to WHAT WE PROVIDE - A dialer and a US phone number - you use no personal minutes - A tested call framework and recorded example calls before your first live dial - The full prospect list, built and maintained for you - Weekly one-on-one coaching from the founder, reviewing your own recorded calls - Direct access to the founder. That is the job, not a problem with the job. - Stable, reliable internet and a quiet, dedicated workspace - Consistency. Preferred: - Prior US outbound B2B calling or BPO experience - Familiarity with any dialer, CRM, or Google Calendar workflow - Experience calling small businesses rather than consumers HOW TO APPLY We review every complete application. title: OPERATIONS & COURSE COORDINATOR
description: OPERATIONS & COURSE COORDINATOR Exceptional Dental Academy | Remote, Philippines-based | Full-time, long-term Exceptional Dental Academy runs hands-on clinical education for dentists across Australia. We deliver two-day courses in Sydney, Melbourne, Perth and Brisbane — currently around one a month, in hotel conference spaces, with sponsor equipment shipped in and a room full of dentists working at benches. Both directors are practising clinicians. The operational side of this business currently runs out of their inboxes between patients. We're looking for one exceptionally organised person, based in the Philippines, to take it over. YOU MUST HAVE WORKED WITH AUSTRALIAN BUSINESSES BEFORE. You'll be dealing with five-star Australian hotels, Australian suppliers and Australian dentists every day. We need someone who already understands how Australian businesses communicate, writes in Australian English, and doesn't need to be taught what AEST means, why nothing moves in the week of Christmas, or how a GST-inclusive quote reads. We'd rather hire someone with three years of genuine Australian client experience than ten years of general VA work. This is not a marketing or social media role. Our marketing is handled elsewhere. This role is venues, logistics, attendees, deadlines and systems. WHAT YOU'D OWN Course venues, end to end. When we d ---------- to run a course in a new city, you own it from brief to bump-out. That means writing the venue brief, working our venue broker and going direct where it's better, comparing quotes on room hire, day delegate rates, minimum spends and inclusions, checking floor plans against a cabaret layout that has to seat a full cohort doing hands-on work, confirming whether the room has a projector or only a screen, comparing catering packages, negotiating the extras that matter (complimentary bump-in the evening before, waived room hire, a hot item added to the buffet), and bringing the directors a shortlist with a recommendation — not a folder of PDFs. Then the paperwork that follows a booking. Venue contracts read, checked line by line against what was actually agreed, and returned signed inside the deadline. Deposit invoices diarised and paid on time. Event detail templates, banquet forms and RFI documents completed — including the catering menu, room set-up, AV requirements, delivery windows and access times — and returned by the date the hotel asked for, not the week of the course. Accommodation for faculty booked. Final invoices reconciled and remittance sent. Attendees. Our courses sell through Eventbrite. You'd manage the listings, monitor the questions that come in daily and answer them properly — what's included, what to bring, where it's being held, whether they can transfer to another city. You'd handle transfers, refunds and rebookings with judgement and warmth, keep the attendee list clean, collect and track dietary requirements, chase outstanding case submissions and forms, send the pre-course information and reminders, prepare certificates, and confirm final numbers to the venue by their cut-off. Suppliers and sponsors. Our courses are supported by dental industry partners who ship consumables and equipment to the venue. You'd coordinate manifests, consignment notes, delivery windows, and make sure the venue knows what's arriving and when — plus banners, table wraps, printed materials and anything else that has to be in the room by 6pm the night before. Keeping the directors organised. Collecting tasks and requests as they come up — from emails, calls and messages — turning them into a single tracked list with owners and due dates, and following them up. If a contract needs a signature by Wednesday, we expect you to have it in front of the right person on Monday and to chase it Tuesday afternoon. You will need to be comfortable following up busy people who are mid-clinic, and comfortable saying "this is now overdue." Building the systems we don't have yet. A course checklist and timeline we reuse every time. A venue and supplier database with what we paid, who we dealt with and what we'd do differently. Contracts and invoices filed where they can be found. SOPs for the things we currently redo from memory each cycle. Within a year we want you to be the person who knows where everything is and where every course is up to. And because this is a full-time role, you'd also own the EDA inbox, the delegate and waitlist database, post-course feedback collection, faculty and speaker scheduling, per-course cost tracking so we can see what each event actually made, and the admin behind our online course products as they come online. We have enough work here for a full week — what we don't have is anyone doing it in an organised way. ABOUT YOU - You have real experience working with Australian businesses, and can give us references from Australian employers or clients. - You are exceptionally organised, and you have a system — not just a good memory. - You can take an objective ("we want to run in Adelaide in March") and come back with a researched, costed shortlist and a recommendation. - You read contracts carefully and notice when a clause doesn't match what was quoted. - You are comfortable picking up the phone to an Australian hotel and negotiating, professionally and pleasantly. A lot of what we need moves faster on a call than over email. - You will follow people up without being asked to, and without being awkward about it. If a director hasn't approved something and the deadline is tomorrow, we want you to say so plainly rather than wait to be asked. - Your written English is excellent — your emails go out representing EDA to dentists and to five-star hotels. - You can run several courses at different stages at once and keep every deadline visible. - You can work independently once you understand the objective, and you want a long-term role. Experience in events, conference coordination, executive assistance, operations, project coordination or training/education is highly regarded. Comfort with Eventbrite, Google Workspace, spreadsheets and a task management system is expected. Experience with Xero, Klaviyo or Canva is a bonus, not a requirement. Dental or healthcare background is not required — we'll teach you the content side. HOURS AND ARRANGEMENT This is a full-time, long-term role. We are not looking for someone juggling three other clients. You'd work the Sydney business day. That means 7:00am to 4:00pm Manila time for most of the year, moving to 6:00am to 3:00pm from October to April when Sydney goes to daylight saving — so you are always aligned with 9am to 6pm in Sydney. The early start is not negotiable: it exists because hotels, suppliers and delegates respond in the Australian morning, and it shifts by an hour twice a year. Please only apply if that suits you long-term. Course weekends. Our courses run Saturday and Sunday, roughly once a month. On those days we need you contactable by phone or message for venue and attendee issues — not working a full day, but reachable. Time off in lieu the following week. WAGE / SALARY PHP 1,500 per day, rising to PHP 1,900 per day after six months, subject to performance. On a five-day week that is approximately PHP 33,000 per month to start, rising to approximately PHP 41,800. The position is permanent and full-time, with 13th-month pay, paid annual leave and paid public holidays, and a three-month probation. This is intended to be a role you stay in and grow with as EDA does — we are hiring the person who will eventually run our operations. WHAT YOU'LL NEED IN PLACE - Reliable fibre internet with a real backup connection — mobile data or a second provider. - Backup power sufficient to get through a brownout or a storm day without going dark mid-course. - A quiet, private space you can take and make calls from, with a decent headset. - Your own reliable computer. We'll provide an EDA email address, and access to Eventbrite, our Google Workspace and our task system. TO APPLY Please start your application with "EDA OPERATIONS" so we know you've read the full description, and send us: 1. A short introduction and overview of your relevant experience, including which Australian businesses you have worked with and for how long. 2. An example of an event, project or business operation you coordinated from beginning to end — including what nearly went wrong and what you did about it. 3. An example of a time you researched multiple suppliers or options and made a recommendation to management. Tell us what you recommended and why, not just what you found. 4. An example of a time you had to chase a manager or client for something they hadn't done. What you said, and what happened. 5. How you keep track of tasks that are waiting on other people. 6. The project/task management systems you have used. 7. Your notice period, your earliest start date, and confirmation that the Manila hours above work for you long-term. 8. A short 1–2 minute video introducing yourself, recorded in one take. We read every application. Shortlisted candidates will have a short video call and be asked to complete a paid practical task — comparing three real venue options and making a recommendation.

ESSENTIAL: Grading and earthworks take-off experience on civil or infrastructure projects, on real jobs you can describe in detail. This is the single biggest thing that will get your application looked at. Send as many of these four as you can. One is better than none. All four will get your application read first. 1. A grading or earthworks take-off spreadsheet showing cut and fill 2. An earthworks heat map, or a cut and fill colour map 3. A pavement take-off mark-up 4. A drainage take-off mark-up REDACT ANYTHING CONFIDENTIAL. WHAT IS ON OFFER - Above market rate pay - Full-time and long-term with one client, not project-by-project gig work - Supported by a dedicated manager whose role is to help you succeed - Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm Australian Eastern Time. (with some variations by agreement) - Ongoing salary reviews HOW TO APPLY Submit your updated resume, attach your work samples, and answer every question below. ATTENTION: you must directly answer these questions in your application to be considered. Applications without answers will not be read. 1. List the files you have attached and what each one is. If you have attached nothing, write NONE. 2. Name two earthworks jobs you took off. A car park levels plan gives you finished surface levels. The pavement build-up is 40mm asphalt on 100mm Class 3 on 200mm Class 4. Landscape areas get 100mm of topsoil. You have already built the existing surface from the feature survey. What surface do you difference against to get the bulk earthworks cut and fill, and how do you build it? 4. Show your arithmetic on this one. Cut is 8,000 cubic metres and fill is 8,000 cubic metres, measured between surfaces. The geotechnical report gives a bulking factor of 25% and a compaction factor of 10% for the site clay. Does the site balance? What do you order in, and what do you cart away? 5. A geotechnical report tells you: uncontrolled fill to 0.8m, stiff clay below, groundwater at 2.6m, refusal at 3.2m, and rock in one borehole only at 2.9m. The structural drawings show a basement pad requiring excavation to 1.5m across the footprint. What do you price differently because of that report, and what do you write as an exclusion or an assumption when the number goes out? 6. A 180m run of DN450 Class 3 concrete pipe falls from 1.2m to 4.1m of cover across five pits. How do you measure and structure this for pricing, and what quantities besides the pipe itself do you produce? 7. Which earthworks quantities end up in a contract but do not appear as a line or a level on the civil drawings? Where do you find them? If you have worked to Australian standards or specifications, name one and one thing it required that changed your quantities. 8. What software do you use, and what would you want us to provide? Say roughly how many years on each. If there is a tool you work best in that you do not currently have access to, name it. 9. What is your expected monthly salary in PHP, what hours do you work right now, and when could you start?

job_title: Compliance & Document Assistant — US Homecare (Part-Time, Long-Term)
description: WHO WE ARE We help small home care agencies in the Midwest stay compliant with state healthcare regulations. Most of these agencies are run by one to three people who are excellent at caring for clients and overwhelmed by the office Work. If they miss a signature, an expired document, or a required training record, they can lose their license. We are the back office that makes sure that never happens while saving them on hours and costs. The company is run by a former home care agency owner who grew a previous agency to over 90 members before starting this business. You will work directly with the owner, not through layers of management. THE ROLE This is a long-term, part-time position, not a short project and not a one-off gig. It start at around 20-25 hours per week. We are adding new agency clients on an ongoing basis, and this seat is expected to grow into full-time work as that happens. You are one of the first hires, and the role will grow with you. This is heavy document production work. You will be formatting e-signature templates, prefilling forms, organizing client files, and building/revising checklists. It is detailed, sometimes repetitive, and unforgiving of sloppiness. If you want variety and creativity from day one, this is not the role. What makes it interesting is what comes after. As you learn the regulations, you take over more of the thinking work: reading a rule, d ---------- what documents it requires, and building the system that produces them. You will write the SOPs for your own job as you go, to help these struggling Home care agencies. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Build and format document templates in BoldSign (very similar to DocuSign): field placement, signer roles, naming conventions - Prefill and prepare client and employee compliance documents from source files - Organize and audit client and employee files in Dropbox against a compliance checklist - Read state licensing rules from Department Human services for example provided to you, and learn how the system works - Track expiring items: background checks, trainings, service agreements, certifications etc. - Write and maintain the SOP for every process you touch - Some claims and billing reviewing in a EHR system to make sure the agency is up to date. WHAT YOU WILL NOT DO - No client contact. No client calls/emails. Everything routes through the owner. - No sales, no lead generation, no social media, no cold outreach. SCHEDULE - 20-25 hours per week, Monday to Friday, with room to grow into full-time if desired - Hours are flexible within reason, but the role requires overlap with US Central Time business hours (roughly 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM CDT). In Philippine time, that window is late night into early morning. Please be realistic about what you can sustain long-term. - You may keep other clients, but not during your committed hours. - $300 - $500 USD per month, depending on experience - Paid twice per month - Pay increases as you get faster, need less oversight, and take on more responsibilities, and increases again as hours grow toward full-time. This is not a vague promise; it is how the role is designed. Additional benefits are discussed after probation period. WHO I AM ACTUALLY LOOKING FOR No prior knowledge of specific US or Midwest healthcare regulation is required. I provide the source material and the detail. Most applicants have little to not experience with a state licensing rule, and that is fine. What I cannot train is this: I need someone who can be handed a regulation they have never seen and come back with a working checklist and a list of smart questions, without being walked through it step by step. Beyond that, I am looking for someone genuinely curious. This role has autonomy, and autonomy only works if you use it. That means: - Asking questions when something does not make sense, instead of guessing or stalling - Noticing when a process is inefficient and telling me, rather than doing it the slow way forever - Bringing ideas and suggestions, not just completed tasks - Learning on your own between tasks instead of waiting for the next instruction If you need every step explained twice, this will not work. If you enjoy taking something confusing and making it orderly, you will do well here. You also need: - Excellent written English. You will write checklists and SOPs that will be relied on. - Genuine attention to detail. One missing signature is a real problem for a real business. - Reliability. If you say something is done, it is done and it is correct. BACKGROUNDS THAT TRANSLATE WELL Paralegal, audit, quality assurance, healthcare administration, medical billing, insurance, accounting, public health, or any office admin role where you managed compliance documents or licensing paperwork. Helpful but not mandatory: BoldSign, DocuSign, PandaDoc, JotForm, Google Workspace, Dropbox, Notion, any US EHR system, or previous work supporting a US home care or home health agency. CONFIDENTIALITY You will handle protected health information covered by US HIPAA regulations, and you will be required to sign a confidentiality agreement. This means a private, secure workspace, not a shared computer and not a public network. GROWTH We are adding new agency clients on an ongoing basis, and this seat is the foundation of the delivery team. The person in this role is expected to move into a senior position, owning processes, assisting new hires, and reviewing their work, as we grow. Hours and pay increase along the way. HOW TO APPLY Do not send a generic cover letter. Reply and answer all nine questions below, numbered, in the body of your application. Applications that skip questions will not be reviewed. Also Put the word "Compliance office assistant" in your subject line or application title 1. List the specific hours you can reliably work each weekday, stated in US Central Time. Reliable high-speed internet, a quiet space with no background noise for meetings, a good working computer, a good pair of headsets with a clear microphone is a required. 2. Describe the most complicated document, file, or process you have ever been responsible for organizing or cleaning up. What was messy about it, what did you do, and how did you know when it was right? 3. Have you ever had to read a policy, rule, contract, or manual and turn it into something usable, such as a checklist, template, summary, or process? Tell me what it was and how you approached it. 4. Tell me about a time you suggested a better way to do something at work, without being asked. What happened? 5. Which of these have you used, and how much: BoldSign, DocuSign, PandaDoc, JotForm, Google Workspace, Dropbox, Notion, any US EHR or billing system. 6. Are you currently working with other clients? How many hours per week, and doing what? 7. What is your expected monthly rate for 20-25 hours per week? 8. Best contact method and number, plus your availability for an interview in the next 12-48 hours. 9. Paste a link to your audio or video introduction. This is required. It does not need to be polished, a phone recording is fine. Answer two things: tell me about yourself, and tell me about a time you had to learn something difficult on your own, without anyone to teach you. Use any tool you like Vocaroo, Google Drive, Loom, YouTube unlisted, or Dropbox. Your resume is optional. Your answers matter more. First group of Interview requests go out starting within 6 to 12 hours of your application, so please make sure you list your preferred method of contact.

description: Read this first This role is a strong fit only if all of the following apply to you: -You have independently led Google Ads strategy across five or more concurrent client accounts in a digital marketing agency. -You are highly capable in Google Search and Performance Max for lead generation, not primarily ecommerce. -You can independently audit and diagnose GA4 and Google Tag Manager conversion-tracking issues and coordinate technical fixes when required. -You are comfortable working with regulated sectors such as legal, healthcare and financial services. -You can overlap substantially with Australian Eastern Time. -You remain deeply hands-on. You personally implement and optimise campaigns rather than only directing others or reviewing reports. How to apply Start your application with the words BLUE PPC. Applications that do not begin with these words will not be considered, regardless of experience. Then complete our screening form here ---------- We will only review candidates who submit the completed screening form. An application message alone is not sufficient. Position overview We are a growing Melbourne-based digital marketing agency hiring a Senior Google Ads Strategist to lead strategy and take full operational ownership of nine active Australian client accounts. Our portfolio focuses on professional services and allied health, including psychologists, physiotherapists, lawyers, dentists, mortgage brokers, executive coaches and buyers advocates. These are lead-generation accounts where success means qualified calls, booked consultations, viable cases and new clients or patients, not traffic or vanity metrics. You will lead Google Ads strategy and execution across the portfolio from day one. You will independently determine how each account should be structured, optimised, measured and improved, then personally implement the work. Initially, the agency owner will retain primary responsibility for client relationships and lead client meetings. You will provide the strategic recommendations, account analysis and talking points that inform those conversations. As you demonstrate strong strategic judgement and communication, there is a genuine path into direct client leadership and a PPC Lead position. You will complete a structured handover covering each account’s objectives, campaign structure, budgets, conversion actions, performance history, active tests, known risks and immediate next actions. Why this role is worth your time You will step into an established portfolio with documented account history, clear client context and organised account notes. You will also receive: -A full-time, long-term remote position. -Complete strategic and operational ownership of nine active Australian accounts managing approximately US$12,500 per -month in combined ad spend. -Direct communication with the agency owner, with no unnecessary management layers. -Genuine autonomy to make and implement strategic decisions. -Clear performance expectations and accountability from day one. -All required tools and access from day one. -A formal performance and compensation review after 60 to 90 days. -A quarterly performance bonus tied to account retention, tracking integrity and lead-quality outcomes. Details will be discussed with the successful candidate. -A genuine progression path into client-facing leadership and broader paid-media team leadership. What you will own Strategy and account direction -Take full strategic and operational ownership of all nine Google Ads accounts. -Review each client’s commercial goals, services, locations, budgets, historical performance, lead quality and conversion journey. -Develop and document a clear strategy for each account, including what should be tested, why it matters and how success will be measured. -Translate commercial goals into campaign structures, targeting decisions, bidding approaches, budgets and testing priorities. -Challenge weak assumptions and recommend a different direction when the evidence supports it. -Identify where campaign structure, targeting, messaging, measurement or landing pages are limiting qualified-lead performance. -Prioritise qualified enquiries, calls, consultation bookings, viable cases and new clients or patients rather than lead volume alone. -Document major strategic decisions and the commercial reasoning behind them. Campaign management and optimisation -Personally build, manage and optimise Search, Performance Max, remarketing and relevant Display campaigns. -Structure Performance Max campaigns for lead generation, including asset groups, audience signals, search themes and appropriate budget separation. -Conduct ongoing search-term reviews and maintain accurate negative-keyword coverage. -Manage keywords, match types, audiences, locations, schedules, devices, creative assets and exclusions. -Apply smart bidding with independent judgement and understand when automation needs stronger controls or better data. -Monitor budget pacing across all nine accounts and identify overdelivery, underdelivery and performance anomalies before they become client problems. -Maintain strong account hygiene and document significant changes, tests and outcomes. Conversion tracking and data quality -Audit conversion tracking across Google Ads, GA4, Google Tag Manager, website forms, phone calls and call-tracking platforms where applicable. -Implement or validate enhanced conversions for leads where appropriate. -Confirm primary and secondary conversion actions are correctly configured. -Ensure bidding strategies optimise toward meaningful business outcomes rather than weak or misleading conversion actions. -Detect duplicate, missing, inflated or misleading conversion data. -Investigate tracking quality rather than assuming the data is correct because conversions appear in the account. -Explain measurement issues, their commercial impact and the correct resolution. -Coordinate technical implementation with developers or the agency owner when required. -You are not expected to be a full-time analytics engineer. You must be capable of independently diagnosing measurement problems and directing the right resolution. Lead quality and commercial performance -Evaluate performance beyond cost per lead by assessing lead relevance, intent and commercial value. -Identify campaigns, keywords, search terms, locations or offers generating poor-quality enquiries and act on them. -Recommend improvements to targeting, messaging, forms, landing pages and conversion definitions. -Understand that professional-services and allied-health leads behave differently. Consultations, appointments, viable legal cases and high-value enquiries require different strategies and qualification standards. -Connect campaign decisions to commercially relevant outcomes. -Escalate material risks early with a clear diagnosis and recommended response. Ad messaging and landing-page recommendations -Develop or coordinate clear, relevant advertising messages and assets aligned with each client’s services, audience and location. -Recognise advertising restrictions affecting legal, healthcare and financial-services clients, and flag potential compliance risks. -Identify landing-page problems affecting relevance, trust, conversion rate or lead quality. -Provide clear recommendations and coordinate improvements with the appropriate team member. -You will not be expected to design or build landing pages yourself. Reporting and communication -Build and maintain client-ready reports in Looker Studio or an equivalent platform. -Provide accurate data, plain-English analysis and commercially relevant recommendations. -Explain what changed, why it changed, what the result was and what should happen next. -Give the agency owner concise strategic talking points before client meetings. -Maintain clear updates on performance, budgets, risks, active tests and unresolved blockers. -Attend one internal weekly performance review, with other updates handled asynchronously. -Never produce reports that merely list platform metrics without interpretation or a recommended action. Portfolio and workload You will own nine active Australian client accounts across professional services and allied health, managing approximately US$12,500 per month in combined ad spend. The portfolio includes: Psychology and allied health Legal services Dentistry Physiotherapy Mortgage broking Executive and high-performance coaching Buyers advocacy These are lead-generation accounts. Performance is judged through qualified calls, enquiries, consultation bookings, appointments, viable cases and new clients or patients, not impressions, clicks or raw lead volume. Your first 14 days Within your first two weeks, you will be expected to complete: -An initial tracking audit across all nine accounts, with primary conversions confirmed and duplication, inflation or missing measurement identified. -An account triage summary covering current performance, known risks, budget pacing and immediate priorities for each account. -An initial 90-day strategy, testing and optimisation roadmap identifying the highest-priority improvements and measurement needs across the portfolio. -A budget-pacing overview confirming which accounts are on track and which require immediate action. -Clear documentation of unresolved issues that need technical support or agency-owner input. These deliverables are designed to assess your strategic judgement, ability to prioritise and working style. They are not a requirement to rebuild nine accounts within two weeks. What success looks like after 60 to 90 days -You independently lead strategy and manage day-to-day execution across all nine accounts without daily supervision. -Every account has clear commercial goals, a documented strategy, current performance status, active tests and known risks. -Strategic decisions are proactive and evidence-led rather than reactive or dependent on agency-owner instructions. -Budgets are paced accurately, and material anomalies are identified before they become client problems. -Conversion tracking has been reviewed across the portfolio, with problems resolved, documented or escalated. -Optimisation decisions reflect qualified-lead outcomes rather than surface-level platform metrics. -Reporting is accurate, commercially relevant, written in plain English and delivered on time. -The agency owner is never surprised by an avoidable account issue. You proactively recommend improvements to campaign structures, tracking, messaging and landing pages. You consistently explain the strategic reasoning behind your decisions. Must-haves Please apply only if you have: At least five years of active, current Google Ads experience managing live client accounts. Proven experience independently leading Google Ads strategy across five or more concurrent client accounts in a digital marketing agency. Strong experience running lead-generation campaigns for service-based businesses. Advanced practical knowledge of Google Search campaigns, including keyword strategy, match types, negative keywords, bidding, ad messaging and account structure. Demonstrated ability to structure and manage Performance Max for lead generation, including asset groups, audience signals, search themes and channel-level interpretation. Proven ability to translate commercial goals into clear campaign strategies and testing priorities. The confidence to challenge weak assumptions and recommend a different strategic direction when required. Demonstrated ability to audit and troubleshoot conversion tracking in GA4 and Google Tag Manager. Experience implementing or validating enhanced conversions for leads. Proficiency in producing client-ready reporting through Looker Studio or an equivalent platform. Strong commercial judgement and the ability to assess performance beyond platform metrics. Excellent written and spoken English. Strong attention to detail and consistent documentation habits. Confidence making independent strategic decisions and explaining your reasoning clearly. Reliable internet, a suitable full-time remote setup and consistent availability overlapping Australian Eastern Time. Nice-to-haves Recent experience working with Australian agencies or Australian clients. Experience with law firms, allied health, financial services or other regulated professional-services sectors. Experience using Google Ads scripts or automation for account monitoring and alerting. Demand Gen campaign experience. Experience building Looker Studio dashboards for multiple clients. Who will succeed in this role You are likely to thrive here if you: Take ownership without waiting to be chased. Think strategically while remaining deeply hands-on. Care about qualified leads and commercial outcomes, not impressions, clicks or platform scores. Communicate risks before they become client problems. Make confident decisions and document the reasoning behind them. Manage nine accounts simultaneously without losing track of important details. Know when to use Google’s automation and when stronger strategic controls are required. Want to progress into client-facing leadership and broader paid-media leadership over time. title: In-House Media Buyer - Meta, Medical Clinic Lead Gen (Head of Media Buying track)
job_title: In-House Media Buyer - Meta, Medical Clinic Lead Gen (Head of Media Buying track)
description: READ THIS BLOCK FIRST. IT SAVES US BOTH TIME. If any of these are untrue, close the tab. We will not make exceptions and we will not read the application. - You have personally managed at least $500,000 in Meta ad spend. Not "worked on an account that spent that." You, in the account, making the calls - You have run lead generation, not ecommerce. Appointments, consultations, calls booked. If your entire history is ROAS on a Shopify store, this is a different job than the one you know - You have worked in medical, dental, aesthetics, or another high ticket service where a lead becomes a booked appointment and then a sale weeks later. Or a vertical close enough that you can explain why it is close enough - You want to be in house, exclusively, for one company. Not a retainer client. Not a fractional seat alongside four other brands. Not your agency taking us on. One company, all of your attention That last one is not negotiable and it is the one people try to negotiate. If you run your own agency or freelance for other clients, we are not the right fit, no matter how good you are. WHO WE ARE Novaris Global. We run paid acquisition for private medical clinics, mostly plastic surgery and aesthetics. Our clients are in Singapore and we are expanding. Here is the part that changes everything about this job. We do not charge a flat retainer. We take a percentage of the revenue we generate for the clinic. If the ads produce nothing, we make nothing. So this is not a role where you optimize toward a dashboard number and file a report. Your decisions are directly, immediately, and painfully connected to whether this company makes money. Cost per lead is not the scoreboard. Cost per booked consultation is closer. Cost per surgery performed is the real one, and that is the number you will be judged on and paid on. Most media buyers have never been held to that. The ones who have tend to be very good, because there is nowhere to hide. THE ROLE You own paid acquisition. All of it, across every client. - Strategy, structure, budget, and every decision inside the ad accounts - Testing. What we try next, why, in what order, and what it would take to convince you that you were wrong - Creative direction on the media buying side. You do not cut the videos, but you d ---------- what needs to exist, what the next 30 ads have to prove, and which angle died and why - Tracking and attribution. Pixel, CAPI, offline conversions, UTMs, and the chain from an impression to a surgery that actually happened - The whole funnel, not just the account. Landing page, form, speed to first contact, show rate, close rate. Half the wins in this business are downstream of the ad and most media buyers pretend that half is somebody else's problem - Reporting that tells the truth, including when the truth is that this week was bad and here is why WHO THIS IS ACTUALLY FOR We are looking for a specific kind of person, and it is not the person with the best resume. It is the person who cannot leave a number alone. You know if this is you. You open the ads manager on a Sunday because something felt off on Friday and it has been sitting in your head since. You have built spreadsheets nobody asked for. You get genuinely irritated by an account you cannot explain. When a campaign works, your first reaction is not relief, it is "why," and you will not be satisfied until you can say exactly why, because a win you cannot explain is a win you cannot repeat. You have opinions about attribution windows. You have been in an argument about broad versus interest stacking. You have a view on where Meta is right now and it is your own view, formed from your own accounts, not something you absorbed from a YouTube video. You do not accept "the account is doing fine." Fine is an insult. There is always another test, another segment, another cut of the data, another thing that has been quietly wrong for three weeks that nobody looked at. If reading that felt like being described, keep going. If it felt exhausting, we are genuinely not the right place and no amount of money will fix that. THE THING WE WANT MOST We want someone better at this than the founder. I run media buying here now and I am good at it. I do not want a pair of hands to execute my ideas. I want someone who looks at how we do things and says "this is wrong, here is why, here is what we should do instead," and is right often enough that I stop arguing. You will have real authority over the accounts. You will also have to defend your calls with evidence, because you will be arguing with someone who knows the platform. That is the job. If you want a boss who does not understand what you do, we are the wrong company. If you have spent years being overruled by people who understood less than you did, this might be the best part of the offer. WHERE THIS GOES Head of Media Buying at Novaris Global. Right now that is one person, which is why we are hiring carefully. As we take on clinics, you stop running every account personally and start building the team that does, setting the standards, and training the buyers under you. In house, on the team, in the decisions, not a contractor we send a Slack message to when something breaks. WHAT WE PAY A base, plus a share of what your accounts generate. We are not going to post a number, because the number depends entirely on who you turn out to be, and the honest answer is that we will pay well above market for the right person and nothing at all for the wrong one. What we will tell you is the structure, because the structure is the point: we get paid on client revenue, so you get paid on client revenue. When you find something that works, you are not asking for a raise, you already got one. If you are excellent and you want a ceiling, we are the wrong company. If you are excellent and you have been annoyed for years that your results made someone else rich, read that paragraph again. WHAT WILL GET YOU REJECTED IMMEDIATELY - An application that talks about strategy and never mentions a number - Cost per lead presented as a result, with nothing about what happened to those leads afterward - "I scaled a client from 5k to 50k a month" with no vertical, no timeframe, no cost per acquisition, and no mention of whether it stayed there - Any suggestion that you would keep your other clients - A generic application. We can tell within one line, and so can you HOW TO APPLY This application is long on purpose. We are not doing introductory calls with people who are not close, so everything we would ask on that call is below. Answer it well and the next conversation we have is a serious one. Start your message with the word ANDROMEDA. PART 1. YOUR NUMBERS. - Total Meta spend you have personally managed, lifetime - The most you have managed in a single month, and in which account - Verticals, honestly, with the medical or high ticket service ones first - For your best lead gen account: what it spent, over what period, cost per lead, cost per booked appointment, show rate, and cost per closed sale. If you do not have the downstream numbers, say so plainly and tell us why they were not available to you. That answer tells us a lot and a missing number is not automatically a problem. Making one up is - Screenshots welcome. Blur the client name if you need to PART 2. FOUR QUESTIONS. SHORT ANSWERS ARE FINE. VAGUE ANSWERS ARE NOT. 1. An account is spending $300 a day. Last week cost per lead was $52. This week it is $31 and lead volume is up 40 percent. The clinic tells you they booked fewer consultations this week than last. Where do you look first, and what are the three most likely explanations in order of probability? 2. One ad set has been stable for three weeks at $200 a day with a $180 cost per booked consultation. You need it at $600 a day within a month. Walk us through exactly how you do it, and tell us what you expect to break first. 3. A campaign has 30 ads live. Two of them are taking 90 percent of the spend. The other 28 have spent almost nothing. The client wants to know why they paid for 28 ads that are not running. What do you tell them, and what do you do with those 28? 4. The clinic's front desk takes six hours to call a new lead. You have no authority over the front desk and the clinic owner is defensive about his staff. What is that costing, and what do you actually do about it? PART 3. YOUR READ ON THE PLATFORM. Two paragraphs on where Meta is right now and what it means for how accounts should be run in 2026. Your own opinion, from your own accounts. We are not looking for a correct answer, we are looking for a real one. If you agree with the consensus, say why. If you think the consensus is wrong, that is more interesting. PART 4. TEAR SOMETHING APART. Go to the Meta Ad Library. Find any plastic surgery or aesthetic clinic running ads right now, anywhere in the world. Look at what they are running. Tell us what you would change and why. Be specific and be harsh. This is the part we read most carefully, because it is the only part where we get to watch you think instead of watching you describe yourself. PART 5. OPTIONAL, AND IT COUNTS. A Loom, ten minutes or less, sharing your screen inside an account you actually run. Walk us through what you are looking at and what you would do next. Blur whatever you need to. Nothing else in this application is as convincing as this. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT We read every complete application. If it is strong, we get on a call, and that call is a working session on a real account of ours, not an interview about your strengths and weaknesses. If that goes well, a paid project on a live account before anyone commits to anything, because you should also get to find out whether we are worth working for.

description: We run a real estate education brand that teaches first-generation buyers how to purchase their first property. Our organic reach works. Our paid acquisition does not exist yet. **Current state, stated plainly so you can d ---------- if this is your kind of problem:** - 14,000 organic views per week across Instagram and YouTube - One email opt-in from that traffic in the last seven days - A free weekly live session that converts well once people attend - A four-tier membership from $47 to $997 per month - A free lead magnet and a 30-day nurture sequence **The gap is conversion, not attention.** We do not need someone to make us go viral. We need someone who can turn attention into opt-ins, opt-ins into attendance, and attendance into paid members. --- ## WHAT YOU WOULD OWN - Paid acquisition on Meta and YouTube, end to end - Landing page and funnel conversion rate, not just click cost - Creative testing against a defined belief, not random variations - Weekly reporting on cost per opt-in, cost per room attendee, and cost per member --- ## HOW WE HIRE **We do not hire from a portfolio. We hire from a paid trial.** **Step one.** Send your three best results with real numbers. Spend, cost per acquisition, and what the business actually made. Screenshots from ad manager, not a case study PDF. If you cannot show numbers, we are not the right fit. **Step two.** Paid trial. We give you a defined budget, our creative library, and our offer. Not click-through rate. **How many real people ended up in a real conversation, and what did each one cost.** Whoever wins the trial gets the ongoing role. --- ## COMPENSATION Paid trial at a flat rate, agreed before you start. Ongoing role is base plus performance. **For the right person who wins the trial and wants long-term upside, we are open to a profit share conversation.** That conversation happens after the trial, in writing, with an attorney involved. We are not offering equity in a job post and you should be suspicious of anyone who does. --- ## WHO THIS IS NOT FOR - Anyone whose case studies have no numbers in them - Anyone who wants to rebuild the brand before running a single test - Anyone who reports on reach and engagement instead of cost per acquisition - Agencies subcontracting the work to someone we never speak to --- ## WHO THIS IS FOR Someone who has spent real money on someone else's behalf, kept a record of what it returned, and can tell me about a campaign that failed and what they learned from it. title: Inbound Lead Handler - Small, Southern US Home Service Company
job_title: Inbound Lead Handler - Small, Southern US Home Service Company
description: If being reachable is just how you're wired - and a message left sitting BUGS you until it's handled - read on. You're the person who answers. When someone reaches out, you get back to them. Not because it's in your job description - because leaving them hanging feels wrong to you. You're where you said you'd be, when you said you'd be there. You keep people in the loop without being chased for updates. It's just what you do. You don't need the spotlight. You need to know that nothing got missed on your watch. The Work We're a crawl space encapsulation company in Nashville. About a hundred people a month reach out to us - Facebook and Instagram, website forms, texts, calls. The owner sells. The GM runs the crews. Nobody owns the middle - and good people don't always hear back. That's the gap. You close it. Put simply, your job is this - Be the first warm human every lead hears from, and make sure they get to the right person with nothing missing. You'll respond fast, kindly, and personally. You'll offer the free inspection and do your best to get it booked. If they need something other than that, you'll make it your responsibility to connect them. Service and warranty calls go to the GM with everything he needs - so he never has to ask twice. Sales conversations go to the owner the same way. You'll keep the record true in the CRM (HighLevel). Your goal: If it happened, it's in there. And a few times a shift, you'll send an update on what you've done, and what's next. Not the job: selling, answering technical questions, building automations. You won't be on an island. Two people will be hands-on with you from day one - and the answers, the access, the context are all there when you ask. The Offer Small team. Real stakes. An owner and a GM who just asked for this role to exist. Your work will be visible. Each booked inspection that turns into a job has a significant impact on the company - and everyone here knows it. We're offering a real team of honest, well meaning guys that wants what you naturally do. Details Full time. $6/hour. US Central business hours. You'll report to the GM (in Nashville) I (David, located in Mindanao) will help you get set up, situated, and find success in this role. GHL experience helps. Any real CRM background works. We hire character and train skill. What can't be taught is HOW YOU'RE WIRED. One thing we're plain about: on the clock means online and available. Every paid hour. We're hoping you take a personal interest in the success of the company and its team members. To Apply Interested? Tell us about a time someone was waiting on an answer, and YOU were the reason they got one. Keep it to one paragraph. In the same message, tell us the hours (Central time) you can be online and reachable. IMPORTANT: Your verbal English skills are crucial - the less accent you have, the better. We don't want the callers to ever doubt or question whether you could be their next door neighbor. If I like your answers to the questions, I'll follow up asking for a quick selfie video :) In Closing If you need to be chased, this isn't it. If the "Details" section read like common sense to you - let's talk.

title: Shopify Store builder
description: # Shopify Store Builder / CRO Specialist – Women’s Fashion E-Commerce We run a growing women’s fashion e-commerce brand selling primarily in the European market. We are looking for an experienced **Shopify Store Builder / E-Commerce VA** who can build high-quality Shopify stores from scratch and create a system that makes adding and launching new products fast and consistent. This is **not simply a product-listing position**. We need someone who understands how to build a professional, trustworthy and **conversion-focused fashion store** — from the overall Shopify theme and product-page structure to product imagery, copywriting, sizing information, bundles, social proof and CRO elements. ## What You'll Be Doing You will help build and optimize our Shopify store from the ground up. Your responsibilities will include: * Building and customizing Shopify stores from scratch * Creating clean, professional women's fashion storefronts for European customers * Building homepage, collection, product and supporting pages * Creating a **high-quality reusable product page template** that can easily be plugged into new products * Designing product pages specifically for **conversion rate optimization** * Importing and building products using **POKY and KOPY** * Using **Claude and ChatGPT** for product copy, research and workflow assistance * Using **Higgsfield** to create and improve high-quality fashion product imagery and creative assets * Selecting, editing and organizing professional product images * Making sure AI-generated imagery looks realistic, consistent and appropriate for a legitimate fashion brand * Writing and improving product titles, descriptions, benefits and selling points * Creating accurate, easy-to-understand **size charts** * Creating product variants, pricing, SKUs and other product information * Building product bundles, quantity offers and upsells * Adding social proof and trust-building elements * Creating clean collection pages and organizing navigation * Optimizing the mobile shopping experience * Maintaining consistent branding, typography, spacing and imagery throughout the store * Quality-checking the entire storefront before launch ## Product Page & CRO Expectations We do not want generic Shopify product pages. Every important product page should feel like it belongs to an established women's fashion brand and should be designed to make the purchasing decision as easy as possible. You should understand how to properly structure elements such as: * Strong product imagery * Clear product titles * Pricing and promotional offers * Variant and size selectors * Size guides * Product benefits and descriptions * Fit and sizing information * Material and care information * Shipping and returns information * Trust elements * Customer reviews and social proof * Product bundles * Quantity offers * Cross-sells and complementary products * Frequently bought together sections * FAQ sections * Clear calls to action * Sticky Add to Cart where appropriate * Mobile-first layouts You should understand **why these elements improve conversions**, rather than simply adding them because you were told to. ## Reusable Product Template One of the most important parts of this position is creating an excellent **plug-and-play product template**. Once the initial store and system are built, we want to be able to add new women's fashion products quickly without rebuilding every page from scratch. The template should maintain consistent: * Layout * Branding * Typography * Product imagery standards * Size-chart formatting * Product descriptions * Social proof * Trust elements * Bundles and offers * CRO sections * Mobile formatting The goal is to create a scalable system where new products can be added quickly while still maintaining a high-quality storefront. ## Tools You Must Be Comfortable With Strong experience with the following is highly preferred: **Shopify** – Store building, themes, product templates, collections, navigation and product management **POKY** – Product importing and product workflow **KOPY** – Product copy and listing optimization **ChatGPT** – Copywriting, research and workflow assistance **Claude** – Copywriting, research and workflow assistance **Higgsfield** – Creating high-quality AI fashion/product imagery and creative assets Experience with additional Shopify CRO, review, bundle, upsell or page-building apps is a strong plus. ## What We're Looking For You must have: * Previous experience building Shopify stores from scratch * Proven experience working with a **fashion or apparel brand** * A portfolio of Shopify stores or product pages you have personally worked on for fashion brands * Strong understanding of Shopify product-page CRO * Strong eye for visual design * Ability to recognize the difference between a generic dropshipping store and a polished fashion brand * Experience creating reusable Shopify product templates * Strong attention to detail * Ability to create high-quality product imagery * Ability to use AI tools effectively without producing generic-looking AI content * Understanding of women's fashion sizing and size-chart presentation * Good written English * Ability to work independently after onboarding * Ability to follow an existing brand style while also making intelligent improvements Experience with visually driven e-commerce brands is a strong plus. Knowledge of European e-commerce and women's fashion customers is also highly preferred. ## Quality Standard We care much more about **quality and attention to detail than simply completing tasks quickly**. The finished store should look like a real European women's fashion brand — not a quickly assembled dropshipping website. We expect you to notice things like inconsistent image ratios, poor spacing, awkward copy, incorrect size charts, weak product images, inconsistent fonts, unnecessary sections, poor mobile formatting and anything else that reduces trust or conversion rate. You should be the type of person who notices these problems without needing us to point out every single one. ## About the Role This is intended to become a long-term position for the right person. The initial phase will focus heavily on **building the Shopify store, establishing our design standards and creating the reusable product-page system**. Once the store structure and templates are established, the role will expand into launching products, improving existing pages, testing new offers and continuously improving the storefront. We want someone who can eventually take ownership of the Shopify storefront rather than requiring step-by-step instructions for every task. ## How to Apply Please send: 1. Links to **2–5 Shopify stores for fashion or apparel brands** you have personally worked on. 2. Examples of fashion product pages you built or optimized. 3. Briefly explain exactly what you did on each store you send us. 4. Tell us about your experience working directly with fashion or apparel brands. 5. Tell us which of these tools you have experience with: **POKY, KOPY, ChatGPT, Claude and Higgsfield.** 6. Tell us about any Shopify CRO, bundle, upsell or review apps you have experience using. 7. Send an example of what you consider a **high-converting women's fashion product page** and briefly explain why you think it converts well. Please do not send stores you did not personally work on. **Start your application with the word "VELVET"** so we know you read the entire job posting. Applications without VELVET at the beginning will not be considered.

title: Senior Bookkeeper - AP/AR, Finance Operations (Agency + Ecom)
job_title: Senior Bookkeeper - AP/AR, Finance Operations (Agency + Ecom)
description: Wavy Studios is marketing agency who does client work and builds our own in-house brands (ecommerce/service based). We've grown to the point where our finances and internal operations are held together by the founder's evenings, and that's not a plan. We're hiring the person who takes it over properly. This is a broad, foundational role. You'll own the books end to end, make sure money we've earned actually arrives, and bring order to the administrative machinery of a growing studio. What you'll own (1) The books. Day-to-day bookkeeping, reconciliations across banks, cards and payment processors, and a monthly close on a fixed calendar. (2) Receivables. Invoicing on time and against contract terms, and chasing what's overdue (3) Payables. Supplier and freelancer bills checked against what was approved and what was delivered, then paid in clean weekly runs. (4) Reporting. A monthly management pack with real commentary, a rolling 13-week cash forecast, and project-level profitability so we know which work is worth doing. (5) Client and vendor admin. Contracts and SOWs out and signed, deposits and stage payments tracked, retainer renewals surfaced early, freelancer rates and approvals kept tidy. (6) Studio operations. Our tool stack and seats, joiner and leaver checklists, contractor paperwork, subscription audits, and the process docs that stop knowledge living in one person's head. (7) Our external partners. Day-to-day relationship with our accountant and payroll provider, and the year-end pack that keeps them efficient. What we need Several years running full-cycle bookkeeping for a business, closing months without supervision Strong QuickBooks Online experience - comfortable with chart of accounts structure, project tracking and bank rules, not just entry Real reconciliation experience, including payment processors, transfers and the awkward cases A track record of collecting overdue invoices without damaging relationships Solid spreadsheets: pivots, lookups, and building a cash-flow model from scratch Clear, warm writing — you'll be the voice of a lot of our administrative email Genuine discretion. You'll see everything.

title: Social Media Marketing
description: # SOCIAL MEDIA & FAN PAGE ASSISTANT **Remote | Part-Time | ₱10,000 PHP/month | 15 hours/week** We're looking for someone who is **very online, creative, and understands internet culture** to help grow music through short-form content. You should genuinely enjoy **K-dramas, anime, memes, edits, movies, and online fan culture.** ## THE GOAL The strategy is simple: **Get people to discover songs from different angles.** Instead of simply posting a song and telling people to listen, we'll use the music in different types of content that people already enjoy watching and sharing. For example: * K-drama edits * Anime edits * Memes * Relatable content * Aesthetic videos * Movie edits The goal is for someone to discover the **content first**, and then discover the **song naturally through the content**. ## THE 4 ACCOUNTS Once fully onboarded, you'll manage **4 separate social media accounts**, each with a completely different content theme. ### 1. K-Drama Edits Romantic, emotional, funny, or dramatic K-drama scenes using the music. ### 2. Meme / Relatable Short memes and relatable situations using the music. The text on screen should be something someone would **actually want to send to a friend**. ### 3. Anime Edits Emotional, romantic, funny, or cinematic anime scenes using the music. ### 4. Aesthetic Dreamy, emotional, cinematic, beautiful, or visually interesting content using the music. **Optional:** If you have a strong idea for a Western movie account, you can propose it as an alternative to one of the above. **IMPORTANT:** Keep the content completely separate between accounts. Each account should feel like its own page with its own audience and identity. --- # TRIAL — FIRST WEEK The first **week is a paid trial**. During the trial, you will only be responsible for **2 accounts**, rather than all 4. We'll decide together which two themes to start with based on your strengths. ### Days 1–3 Do not immediately start posting. Spend the first 3 days naturally using the accounts: * Scroll through relevant content * Watch videos in your niche * Like videos * Save videos * Leave genuine comments on relevant videos * Study which videos perform well * Study captions and hooks * Study what people share and engage with * Learn the culture of each community The goal is to understand **what already works within each niche**. You can take inspiration from successful posts and adapt their **caption structures, hooks, formats, and ideas** into original content. ### Days 4–7 Start posting. **Post once per day on each trial account.** That's **2 posts per day total** during the trial. We'll use this week to evaluate your: * Creativity * Content instincts * Editing ability * Understanding of internet culture * Understanding of the different niches * Consistency * Ability to create content people want to share * Overall fit If the trial goes well, you'll move on to managing all **4 accounts**. --- # POSTING Once fully onboarded: **Post once per day on each of the 4 accounts.** That's **4 posts per day total**. ### K-Drama / Anime / Movie Edits Videos should generally be: **10–30 seconds** Choose scenes that match the emotion, lyrics, or feeling of the song. ### Meme / Relatable Keep videos: **Under 10 seconds** The text should be the main hook. The goal is to make someone immediately think: **"This is literally me."** or **"I need to send this to someone."** --- # CROSS-POSTING After posting on TikTok: 1. Download the video 2. Post it to YouTube Shorts 3. Post it to Instagram Reels Content can be adapted slightly for each platform when necessary. **During the trial, focus on TikTok only.** --- # IMPORTANT — OFFICIAL AUDIO When posting on TikTok and Instagram, **always use the official song audio when available**. This allows people to discover the song through the audio and easily add/save it to their music library. --- # WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR You **must understand internet culture**. We're looking for someone who: * Loves memes * Loves K-dramas * Loves anime * Enjoys edits * Understands TikTok culture * Understands online fandoms * Knows what makes people share content * Has a good sense of humor * Understands current internet language and trends * Can recognize why a video is performing well * Is creative and willing to experiment You don't need to be an expert editor. **Good content instincts are more important.** --- # COMPENSATION **₱10,000 PHP/month** Approximately **15 hours per week**. There is also potential for **performance bonuses** when videos perform exceptionally well. ### Performance Bonuses * **50K views:** ₱100 * **100K views:** ₱200 * **250K views:** ₱500 * **500K views:** ₱1,000 * **1M+ views:** ₱2,000 Only the **highest tier reached** is paid for each individual video. **Maximum performance bonus: ₱20,000 PHP per month.** Bonuses are based on organic views on eligible content created as part of this role. --- # HOW TO APPLY Please send: 1. A short introduction about yourself 2. Any fan pages or social media accounts you've managed 3. Examples of edits, TikToks, Reels, memes, or Shorts you've made 4. Your favorite K-drama 5. Your favorite anime 6. **3 examples of content you think would work well with music** 7. Your availability and time zone We're looking for someone who **loves the internet, understands memes and fandoms, loves K-dramas and anime, and knows how to turn a song into something people actually want to watch and share.**

title: Finance Manager
description: CONTROLLER / SENIOR FINANCE & ACCOUNTING MANAGER Southern Domestic Diva Southern Domestic Diva is seeking an experienced, highly analytical Controller / Senior Finance & Accounting Manager to take ownership of the financial operations of a growing, multi-entity service company. This is not a basic bookkeeping or accounting assistant position. We need a proactive financial operator who can protect cash flow, strengthen financial controls, aggressively manage accounts receivable, reduce unnecessary expenses, improve profitability, prevent unnecessary debt, and build scalable systems capable of supporting $4 million+ in annual revenue and continued growth. 1. XERO & ACCOUNTING MANAGEMENT Advanced Xero proficiency is required. Maintain accurate, current books across multiple business entities, bank accounts, credit cards, revenue streams, and service divisions. Reconcile bank accounts, credit cards, payment processors, deposits, invoices, and general ledger activity. Properly categorize income and expenses and allocate transactions to the correct entity and division. Identify, research, and resolve accounting discrepancies without waiting for leadership to discover them. Prepare accurate Profit & Loss statements and maintain clean, tax-ready books and supporting documentation. Maintain strong internal financial controls and improve accounting processes as the company scales. 2. ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE & COLLECTIONS The AR process is not complete when an invoice is sent. It is complete when the money has been collected, properly recorded, and reconciled. Own Accounts Receivable as one of the highest-priority functions of the role. Maintain accurate AR aging and continuously review 30/60/90+ day balances. Follow up consistently by phone and email; communicate directly with corporate Accounts Payable departments. Track promised payment dates, confirm payments arrive, and escalate significantly past-due accounts. Resolve invoice discrepancies, PO issues, and client-specific billing requirements that delay payment. Develop systems that accelerate collections and provide leadership clear visibility into outstanding AR. 3. SQUARE & PAYMENT PROCESSOR RECONCILIATION Monitor Square payments, settlements, fees, and deposits and match customer payments to invoices and bank deposits. Reconcile discrepancies among Square, Xero, company databases, and bank activity, including systems that do not automatically integrate. Identify missing, duplicate, incorrect, or unmatched transactions and maintain supporting payment ledgers when necessary. Be comfortable adapting to additional or different third-party payment processors. 4. 13-WEEK CASH-FLOW FORECASTING Own and update a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast every week. Forecast beginning cash, expected collections, payroll, payroll taxes, bills, operating expenses, debt/financial obligations, planned expenditures, and projected ending cash. Compare projected receipts with actual receipts and identify potential cash shortages well before they become emergencies. Recommend corrective actions, accelerate critical collections, and help establish appropriate operating reserves. 5. EXPECTED FUNDS & PAYROLL PLANNING Own and improve the company Fund Expectation spreadsheet showing anticipated incoming revenue and outgoing obligations. Track expected payment dates, upcoming bills, payroll requirements, payroll taxes, and funds expected during payroll weeks. Forecast whether expected cash will adequately cover payroll and other obligations and communicate potential funding gaps early. Leadership should always know current available cash, expected incoming cash, bills due, outstanding receivables, and upcoming payroll needs. 6. DEBT PREVENTION & CASH PROTECTION Help the company operate through strong cash-flow management rather than unnecessary borrowing. Monitor liabilities and future cash requirements, evaluate the cash impact of major purchases, and present alternatives before financing is considered. Monitor interest, financing costs, bank fees, merchant fees, and other drains on cash. Develop strategies to improve working capital, strengthen reserves, and reduce reliance on debt. 7. WEEKLY GROSS & NET PROFITABILITY Complete and analyze weekly revenue, gross profit, gross margin, net profit, net margin, direct labor, subcontractor costs, and operating expenses. Compare performance week over week and flag low-margin or negative-profit accounts and projects. Investigate why profitability changed and recommend corrective action; providing numbers without analysis is not sufficient. 8. LABOR & CREW-TIME PROFITABILITY Work with operations and scheduling to compare scheduled/budgeted labor hours with actual crew hours. Monitor labor cost as a percentage of revenue, overtime, inefficient staffing patterns, and recurring jobs that exceed allotted time. Analyze labor profitability by client and quantify the financial impact of labor overruns. Recommend pricing, staffing, scheduling, or time-limit changes and monitor whether those changes improve profitability. 9. CLIENT, PROJECT & DIVISION PROFITABILITY Analyze profitability by client, project, recurring account, and service division, including residential, vacation rental, commercial, construction, and specialty services. Identify highest- and lowest-margin services, underpriced accounts, negative-profit work, labor margins, subcontractor margins, and revenue concentration. Make recommendations regarding pricing, labor allocation, service structure, and corrective action. 10. BILL MANAGEMENT & COST REDUCTION Own and maintain an accurate bill spreadsheet, track due dates, and prevent unnecessary late fees. Review recurring expenses including software, insurance, telecommunications, banking, merchant processing, vendors, supplies, and administrative costs. Identify duplicate or unnecessary expenses, research lower-cost alternatives, compare vendors, and recommend renegotiations. Proactively identify ways to save money and track savings actually achieved. Cost reduction is an ongoing responsibility, not an occasional project. 11. BUDGETING & BUDGET VS. Cole Insure is a growing US independent Medicare agency, serving veterans and seniors in 25 states. We are hiring 2-3 elite Calling VAs, not ten, not twenty. You will be a named member of a small US team, working directly with our licensed agents, not a seat in a call center farm. Why top setters want this seat: You never prospect cold.
