Build and manage FBA shipment plans — including inventory limits and replenishment cadence - Set up and manage Amazon PPC advertising campaigns — automatic first, refining to manual over time - Monitor listing performance — conversion rate, sessions, BSR — and optimize continuously - Manage review acquisition and respond to customer questions and feedback Phase 4 — Shopify Store Setup - Build and manage a Shopify storefront for one of the products - Write product copy — descriptions, FAQs, and brand story content - Set up payment processing, shipping rules, and order fulfillment workflow - Connect social media channels and set up basic email capture Phase 5 — Ongoing Operations - Monitor inventory levels and initiate reorders before stockouts occur - Track monthly P&L — revenue, cost of goods, Amazon fees, ad spend, and net profit - Identify and execute listing optimizations on an ongoing basis - Communicate daily during the launch phase — what was completed, what is next, what is blocked - Build and document SOPs for all recurring tasks so the business is fully systematized REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS Must Have - Hands-on Amazon FBA experience at an operational level — listing creation, FBA shipment management, inventory tracking, and PPC. Experience contributing to or owning a product launch is strongly preferred. You must be able to describe the complete steps from production to live listing from real experience — not from research. - Experience coordinating with manufacturers or suppliers — you know how to get answers, manage timelines, and keep production moving when things slip - Strong written English — you will write product listings, customer communications, and Shopify copy that must read as native US English - Proven ability to build and execute a structured plan across multiple workstreams without needing daily instructions - Meticulous follow-through — if you commit to something it gets done on the agreed timeline, no chasing required - Proactive communicator — you send updates before being asked and surface problems before they become crises - Comfortable working through ambiguity — you build the plan rather than waiting for one Strongly Preferred - Direct experience launching a product on Amazon FBA from scratch — from first production run to first sale - Amazon PPC campaign management — keyword research, bid optimization, campaign structure - Shopify store setup and management experience - Experience sourcing packaging materials — boxes, inserts, labeling - Familiarity with Amazon research tools such as Helium 10 or Jungle Scout - Basic graphic design or Canva experience for listing images or social content Nice to Have - Experience with Amazon Vine, review strategies, or launch promotional tactics - Social media content creation for e-commerce — Instagram, Pinterest, TikTok - Experience working directly with US-based clients or vendors THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF - You have not worked hands-on with Amazon FBA — this is not a role for someone learning the platform for the first time - You need detailed daily instructions to know what to do next - You are uncomfortable being challenged on your plan or working through multiple rounds of revision - You prefer repetitive structured tasks over ambiguous problem-solving - You are looking for a short-term engagement — this requires a minimum 12-month commitment COMPENSATION Base Rate: $6-10/hour depending on experience — paid weekly via Wise Profit Share: 15% of combined monthly net profit across both products Profit Share Starts: Once products are live and generating net profit — approximately month 3 to 4 Net Profit Defined As: Revenue minus cost of goods, Amazon fees, ad spend, shipping, and packaging Transparency: Full monthly P&L shared — you see every revenue and cost line Example: If both products generate $3,000 combined net profit in month 5 — you earn $450 in profit share on top of your base. At $6/hour base for 40 hours per week that is approximately $960/month base plus $450 profit share — $1,410 total. As the business scales your profit share scales with it. HOW WE WORK - Fully remote — Philippines-based candidates preferred - Flexible hours — but availability during US business hours required for manufacturer and supplier coordination - The launch starts with planning. Your first responsibility is to build a comprehensive launch roadmap drawing on your own FBA experience. No dropped balls. - Daily check-in throughout the launch phase — what was completed, what is planned for tomorrow, what is blocked. Cadence moves to weekly once operations are stable and trust is established. - Daily timesheet — simple Google Sheet logging tasks and hours worked - WhatsApp as primary quick communication channel — responsiveness during working hours is expected - Full financial transparency — monthly P&L shared so you always understand the business you are building - Decisions are made together initially. Walk us through every step you would take — from coordinating that production run through to a live Amazon FBA listing generating its first sales. Include the tools you would use at each stage and the problems you would anticipate. 3. The core team is intentionally small, trusted, and given real ownership over their function rather than a list of daily tasks handed down from above. As the company scales, this team is expected to scale with it, both in title and in responsibility. About the Role This role owns the financial visibility layer of the business: what came in, what went out, what it cost to acquire a customer, and whether each offer is still profitable at its current price. You will process payroll, reconcile the books against the bank, and produce the recurring revenue, ROI, and cash flow numbers that leadership reads every week without asking anyone. This is a trust-based role handled under a strict access boundary: you will monitor bank activity through view-only, read-only access with no transfer capability, no card issuance rights, and no signing authority. You are the second set of eyes on the money, not a second signer on the account. Key Responsibilities - Process weekly payroll for the core team and contractors: confirm hours or agreed pay against each person's rate, prepare the payment run, and confirm on-time disbursement. - Reconcile every bank account weekly against the bookkeeping ledger using view-only bank access. Flag any transaction that does not match a recorded entry within 24 hours of finding it. - Track revenue, cost per lead, contribution margin, and return on ad spend by pillar and by campaign (MurseZan, ZamDance, Zantavius Music, ZannyAcademy), and flag anything crossing its set ceiling or floor. - Maintain accounts payable and accounts receivable records. Follow up on outstanding invoices and flag any receivable aged past 30 days. - Prepare and deliver a weekly one-page cash flow and ROI summary for the Friday leadership review: cash position, runway in weeks, spend against ceiling, blended cost per lead, and revenue by pillar. - Feed verified numbers into the Money panel of the CEO Dashboard so financial status is visible without anyone having to ask. - Maintain price floors and discount authority records; confirm no live campaign or offer runs below its approved contribution margin. - Support tax and compliance documentation for contractor payments (1099s or the local equivalent) at year-end or as required. - Escalate any discrepancy, missed payment, or irregular transaction the same day it is found, never at a reporting deadline. description: # Inbound Lead & Appointment Coordinator (Virtual Assistant) **Full-Time | Remote | 40 hours/week** We're a growing fence installation company in the US, and we're looking for a reliable, organized, and professional Virtual Assistant to handle incoming customer inquiries and support our sales process. **This is not a cold-calling position.** Our customers contact us directly through our website, Google, or phone because they're already looking for fence installation or repair services. Your main job is to respond quickly, book estimate appointments, and keep the sales process organized. ## Your Responsibilities **Lead Handling & Appointment Setting** - Answer inbound customer calls - Call new website/form submissions quickly - Ask a few basic questions about the fence project - Book estimate appointments for new fence installations - Request photos from customers for small fence repairs - Follow up with leads who didn't answer - Confirm appointments - Keep customer information and notes updated in our CRM **Estimate Follow-Up** - Follow up with customers after estimates are provided - Ask whether they have questions or are ready to move forward - Keep follow-up tasks organized in the CRM - Escalate interested customers, pricing questions, negotiations, or complicated questions to the salesperson *You will not be responsible for negotiating or closing sales.* **Estimating & Sales Support** - Create simple fence/property sketches using Google Maps/Google Earth - Prepare customer estimates in our CRM using information provided by the salesperson - Use our existing estimate templates - Enter fence footage, materials, gates, removal, pricing, and other details provided by the salesperson - Send estimates after approval - Keep customer records organized *You will not determine pricing yourself — the salesperson provides the scope and price.* ## What We're Looking For - Clear, professional English, spoken and written - Comfortable talking to American customers by phone - Friendly and confident without being pushy - Highly organized, detail-oriented - Can follow a consistent process - Learns new software quickly - Responds quickly to new leads and follow-up calls - Comfortable working independently - Reliable internet connection and a quiet space for calls **Nice to have:** - Experience with GoHighLevel (GHL) - Experience with Google Maps/Google Earth, CRMs, construction or home-service businesses, appointment setting, or estimating ## What This Job Is NOT - Not aggressive telemarketing - No cold calling - You won't be expected to pressure anyone into buying Most customers have already reached out because they want a fence estimate. Your job is simple: **Respond → Book → Organize → Follow Up** Our salesperson handles the actual sales appointment, pricing, negotiation, and closing. ## A Typical Customer Call A new customer submits a request for a fence estimate. You call to find out whether they need a new installation or a repair. Then you book the estimate appointment. For a small repair, you request photos and log the details in the CRM for the team to review. Your experience with GoHighLevel, if any 4. Your internet speed and computer setup 5. A 60–90 second video introducing yourself as if speaking with a customer in the United States 6. We are now looking for a highly capable Head of Operations who can progressively take full ownership of the company’s daily operations. This is not a basic Virtual Assistant role. We are looking for someone who can think, organize, make decisions, improve systems, create clear SOPs, manage people and eventually run the entire operational side of the company with minimal involvement from the founder. YOUR MAIN OBJECTIVE Your objective will be to make Lando operate smoothly, professionally and independently without the founder being involved in daily operations. You will initially handle many tasks yourself. As the portfolio grows, you will recruit, train and manage additional Virtual Assistants and specialists. You will be responsible for the system, even when individual tasks are later delegated to other team members. YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES Daily operations: * Manage guest messages across Airbnb and other communication channels * Coordinate housekeepers and confirm every cleaning * Coordinate maintenance workers and local service providers * Manage check-in, check-out and access issues * Handle guest complaints, emergencies and service recovery * Track every i ---------- until it is completely resolved * Request and verify photos after cleaning or maintenance * Maintain accurate property information, instructions and checklists * Make sure no task, arrival, issue or owner request is forgotten Property and owner management: * Communicate professionally with property owners by email and messaging * Collect missing property information, documents, photos and equipment details * Coordinate new property onboarding * Create and update Airbnb listings * Keep property accounts, calendars and settings accurate * Organize photographers, maintenance, supplies and property improvements * Prepare clear updates and reports for owners * Identify risks before they become complaints Systems and process improvement: * Document all recurring processes as clear SOPs * Build checklists, decision trees and escalation procedures * Audit our current processes and recommend improvements * Automate repetitive tasks using AI, Make, Zapier or similar tools * Organize tasks and information using Google Workspace and project management software * Create weekly operational dashboards * Maintain a structured database of properties, owners and service providers * Continuously look for ways to improve quality, speed and efficiency Team management: * Help recruit future Guest Communication VAs and operational assistants * Train new team members using SOPs and recorded processes * Review their work and provide feedback * Build schedules and backup coverage * Monitor performance and accountability * Make sure the team maintains Lando’s service standards Lead management: * Make sure every new lead from Airbnb or our website enters the CRM * Collect and organize the information needed by the French-speaking salesperson * Assign leads immediately and notify the salesperson * Monitor response times and follow-up status * Maintain an accurate sales pipeline You will not be responsible for closing French sales calls. A French-speaking salesperson will handle them. LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION Excellent written and spoken English is required. French is not required. Most French communication will be completed using AI translation, approved templates and clear internal guidelines. French voice messages can be transcribed and translated using AI. You must be extremely careful when checking: * Names * Dates and times * Addresses * Prices and refunds * Instructions * Promises made to guests or owners We expect you to use AI intelligently, but never send unverified AI output. French phone calls will be handled separately. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR You may be a strong fit if you: * Have at least three years of experience in operations, project management, property management or hospitality * Ideally have previous Airbnb or short-term rental experience * Have coordinated guests, housekeepers, maintenance workers or vendors * Have created SOPs, checklists or operational systems * Have managed or trained other team members * Are exceptionally organized and detail-oriented * Learn new software quickly * Are comfortable using ChatGPT, Claude or similar AI tools * Can solve problems without waiting for constant instructions * Take responsibility when something goes wrong * Communicate clearly and professionally * Know when to make a decision and when to escalate * Have a reliable computer, Internet connection and backup Internet * Are looking for a serious, long-term position Experience with any of the following is a strong advantage: * Airbnb * Guesty, Hostaway, Hospitable or another PMS * Google Workspace * GoHighLevel * ClickUp, Asana or Notion * Make or Zapier * ChatGPT or Claude * WhatsApp Business * Short-term rental operations HOW WE EXPECT YOU TO ESCALATE PROBLEMS We do not want messages that simply say: “What should I do?” Before escalating, you should provide: 1. What happened 2. The potential impact 3. What you already checked 4. The possible solutions 5. Your recommended solution 6. The deadline for making the decision Critical safety, security, legal or access issues must always be escalated immediately. WORKING HOURS This is a full-time position of approximately 40 hours per week. Your regular schedule must overlap with Paris business and guest-arrival hours. A likely schedule would be approximately 4:00 PM to 1:00 AM Philippine time, adjusted when European daylight-saving time changes. The agreed schedule may include one weekend day. There is a path to USD $1,800 or more as: * The portfolio grows * You take full ownership of operations * The founder is removed from daily operations * You successfully recruit and manage additional VAs * You consistently improve service quality and efficiency Performance bonuses may also be introduced based on operational quality, reliability, process improvements and company performance. This is a one-time specialist project, not a traditional VA position. The main goal is simple: when a serious investor lands on the GoldSignal Pro page, they should quickly understand: - What they get - Why it is valuable - Why it is different from information they can find for free - Why the subscription is worth paying for - What makes GoldSignal credible - What action they should take next GoldSignal includes research and data around insider buying, major ownership stakes, investor portfolios, strategic accumulation, public filings, quantitative signals, alerts, research reports, and a curated set of investable ideas for paid members. I want help improving: - Product positioning - Offer structure - Value proposition - Above-the-fold messaging - Headlines and copy - Pricing presentation - Feature/value hierarchy - Calls to action - Trust and credibility - Objection handling - Overall conversion flow - How the highest-value parts of the paid product are presented Important: I do NOT want an aggressive or hype-driven investment sales page. GoldSignal should still feel like a serious, modern financial data and research platform. Think high-quality SaaS / financial intelligence product, not a "get rich quick" stock newsletter. I already have the product, website, research, data, pricing, and general brand direction. I need someone who can step back, understand the customer and the offer, and organize the page so the value is immediately clear and compelling. Ideal deliverables: 1. Audit of the current paid landing page 2. Identification of the biggest conversion problems 3. Recommended positioning and offer structure 4. Rewritten landing-page copy 5. Recommended page hierarchy 6. Pricing and value-presentation recommendations 7. Suggestions for trust, proof, objections, and calls to action 8. A wireframe, annotated mockup, or clear visual guidance that can be handed to a developer / AI coding workflow You do not need to code the page. Strong marketing judgment, copywriting, customer psychology, and conversion thinking are more important. title: Operations Manager — Coaching Program (AI & Automation Knowledge Required) | Long-Term, Full-Time
job_title: Operations Manager — Coaching Program (AI & Automation Knowledge Required) | Long-Term, Full-Time
description: If you're looking for a job where someone tells you what to do each morning, this isn't it. We already have people who can hand out tasks. What we don't have is someone who looks at how we run, sees what's broken, and fixes it before anyone asks. If that sounds like you, keep reading. If it doesn't, no hard feelings — save yourself the application. Who we are We're Digital Kairos. We run Brick by Brick, a cohort-based coaching program that helps consultants, coaches, and business owners build their brand and get clients on LinkedIn. Members join in classes of about 30, do daily homework, hit milestones, get on teaching calls, and lay bricks — literally, we mail them one. We're a small remote team, mostly US-based, and we move fast. Our members pay real money and they get real results, and the reason that works is that the operations behind them are tight. Right now those operations run on people remembering things. We want them to run on systems. That's your job. ------------------- What you'll actually do: Run the machine. Every cohort has a rhythm: applications come in, people get approved, they pay, they get onboarded, they get channels and access, they do homework, they hit milestones, they unlock calls, they graduate, some move up to our next-level program. You own all of it, start to finish, for every member. Nothing slips through. Build the machine. This is the part that matters most. Right now too much of the above happens by hand — 30 individual messages sent one at a time, progress counted manually across 30 channels, recordings uploaded one by one. You'll use Claude, Zapier, and whatever else works to automate it, so the next class costs us less time than the last one. We already have a list of things waiting to be built. You'll add to it. Organize us. Our team lives in Slack and we're mid-migration into Notion. Things live in three places and belong in one. You'll bring structure — clean systems, written processes, one source of truth — and hold us to it. Take care of our members. You'll message our members more than anyone else on our team does. When someone falls behind, you notice. When someone's confused, you fix it before it becomes a complaint. When someone wins, you catch it and make sure it gets celebrated. This part isn't admin work — it's the experience people paid for. Tell us what's happening. Over-communicate. Every week we want to know what shipped, what's at risk, what you noticed, and what you're changing. If you go quiet, we assume something's wrong. ------------------- Your first 90 days So you know this is a real job with real work waiting, here's some of what's actually sitting on the list: - Write the cohort rulebook — every deadline, threshold, and unlock in one document, so nobody has to ask again - Automate our application and onboarding flow (it's been on our list since June) - Fix a broken Zapier automation between our contract and invoicing tools - Automate our milestone messages, which are currently sent by hand, one member at a time - Build a dashboard that shows who's behind, replacing manual counting - Write our offboarding process, which currently exists only in people's heads ------------------- What you need to have - 2+ years running operations for a cohort program, membership, mastermind, online course, or coaching business. You've done this specific kind of work, not adjacent work. - Slack at an admin level — channels, user groups, workflows, permissions - Notion as a builder — you make databases and views, you don't just fill them in - Zapier or Make — you've built multi-step automations with conditional logic, and you've debugged one that broke at a bad time - AI as a daily tool. We run on Claude. You should already be using AI to do your actual work, not experimenting with it on the side. If you've set up projects, custom instructions, or recurring automated tasks, say so. - Skool, Zoom, Calendly, Google Workspace — or the confidence to be fluent in a week - Excellent written English. You'll write messages that go directly to our paying members. We need to trust you to hit send. - Availability that overlaps US business hours — roughly 9AM–5PM US Central, which is about 10PM–6AM Philippine time. Being straight with you: this is a night shift. Please only apply if that genuinely works for your life. ------------------- Nice to have - Dashboard building, other no-code tools, experience writing SOPs for a team that had none, experience running two cohorts at once. Pay and growth - $1,200 USD/month, full-time - 90-day review with a clear path to $1,500/month — tied to documenting the cohort playbook and shipping two working automations, not to a calendar date - Quarterly performance bonus tied to member completion rates and automations shipped - 13th month pay - Paid time off and Philippine holidays - This is a long-term role with room above it. As we grow, this seat grows — more programs, more systems, and eventually people to lead. We're hiring someone to build a career here, not to fill a gap. ------------------- What working with us is like We're direct and we move fast. We'd rather you try something and get it wrong than wait for permission. If you're stuck for more than an hour, ask — but come with what you already tried. We don't micromanage, and we don't want to. The tradeoff is that we need you to be the kind of person who doesn't need it. For the first 30 days a teammate will review your member-facing messages while you learn our voice. After that, you send them yourself. ---------------------------------- HOW TO APPLY Read this carefully. We're using it to filter, and most applications will not make it past this section. 1. Subject line. Use exactly this, filling in the blank with your favorite automation tool: Brick by Brick Ops — [your favorite automation tool] 2. In your message, answer these two questions. Keep it short — a few sentences each. We care about specifics, not polish. Q1. Tell us about one workflow you automated. What tool did you use, what broke, and what did you do about it? Q2. Here's a real situation. You have 30 members. Nine of them are behind on homework. There's a teaching call in four hours, and the rule for this week's homework requirement isn't written down anywhere. What do you do in your first hour — and what would you build so this never happens again? 3. Record a 2-minute Loom and paste the link. We watch all of them, and we can tell when it's the same video sent to fifty companies. Answer these three, in order: - Who are you and what do you do now? - Show us how you actually use AI in your work. Don't describe it — share your screen and walk us through something real you built or use. - What made you apply to this job specifically? And tell us one thing you'd change about how we've described the role, or something you noticed we might be getting wrong. Applications without a Loom won't be reviewed. Applications with a generic Loom won't either. ------------------- What happens next: if your Loom lands, we'll send you a short practical exercise — about an hour, using a real (anonymized) week from our program. Then one conversation with our founder and our Head of Community, then an offer. We move quickly. We're excited to meet you. Please only apply if you read all of this — we'll know.

title: Finance Operations Lead / Controller — Global Finance, AI & Automation
job_title: Finance Operations Lead / Controller — Global Finance, AI & Automation
description: Summary We are looking for an experienced, highly reliable Finance Operations Lead / Controller to help own and continuously improve the finance function across a growing global business. This is not a traditional bookkeeping role, and it is not a strategic CFO role. CPA license preferred We need someone who can operate in the middle: Understand the complete financial cycle Ensure the numbers are reliable Review and guide the work of finance administrators/bookkeepers Identify risks before management has to ask Improve processes and controls Support finance operations across multiple countries and entities Use AI, automation and lightweight internal tools to make the finance organization more accurate, scalable and efficient The most important qualities for this role are reliability, trust, maturity, ownership and financial judgment. We are looking for someone who can be trusted to look after the finance operation, recognize when something does not make sense, ask the right questions and follow issues through to resolution. AI and automation experience is important, but it does not replace strong finance fundamentals. What You Will Own Financial Operations & Control You will help oversee the complete finance operating cycle, including: Month-end close and financial reporting P&L and balance-sheet review Bank and balance-sheet reconciliations Accounts receivable Accounts payable Billing Cash management Working-capital monitoring 13-week cash-flow forecasting Journal-entry review Accruals and prepayments Budgeting and budget-versus-actual analysis Financial controls Management reporting Audit and year-end support Coordination with external accountants, tax specialists and other advisors You should be comfortable looking across the entire financial operation rather than being specialized only in AP, AR, tax or another individual area. Global Finance Operations Our business operates across multiple markets. You do not need to personally be an expert in every country's tax, legal or accounting rules. You do need enough financial maturity and experience to recognize when something may create a: Tax issue Compliance issue Accounting issue Cross-border issue Cash-flow risk Control weakness Reporting issue You should be comfortable saying: “I don't yet have enough information to approve this. Here are the questions we need answered, here is the risk I see, and here is where we may need specialist advice.” We value that judgment much more than someone pretending to know every answer. Leadership & Ownership You will help supervise and develop finance administrators and bookkeepers. This includes: Reviewing their work Establishing clear procedures Creating appropriate controls Identifying recurring mistakes Coaching team members Improving documentation Assigning ownership clearly Ensuring important activities are completed without management repeatedly following up We are looking for someone who naturally takes responsibility for the outcome, not simply completion of a task. If something looks wrong, you investigate it. If something is unclear, you ask. If a process repeatedly fails, you improve the process. If management has missed a risk, you raise it. AI, Automation & Finance Systems A major part of this role is helping us build a more modern finance operation. We want someone who is already experimenting with or actively using tools such as: Claude Claude Projects Claude Code ChatGPT or similar AI tools AI-assisted coding tools Automation platforms APIs Advanced spreadsheets Scripts No-code / low-code tools Finance system integrations You do not need to be a professional software engineer. You should, however, be comfortable using technology and AI to solve operational problems. Examples of what we want to build You may help create: Scheduled financial analyses Automated daily or weekly finance reviews Exception-based reconciliation workflows AR aging analysis and collection prioritization Automated billing checks Cash-flow monitoring Budget-versus-actual analysis Expense anomaly detection Month-end close checklists Balance-sheet account review workflows Scheduled audit and control checks Management reporting AI-assisted investigation of unusual transactions Finance knowledge bases SOP and policy assistants Internal finance dashboards Workflow tools for finance administrators The objective is not to automate financial judgment away. The objective is to automate repetitive work and make exceptions, risks and decisions easier for experienced humans to identify. How We Think About AI We are looking for someone who understands the difference between: What can safely be automated and What still requires human judgment, review and approval. For example, AI may help: Analyze transactions Compare reports Identify anomalies Prepare summaries Investigate supporting information Draft communications Prioritize exceptions But important accounting decisions, financial controls and money movement still require appropriate human review. You should naturally think about: Accuracy Auditability Controls Data security Approval workflows Human verification Documentation when designing AI-enabled finance processes. What We Care About Most 1. Reliability If you say something will be done, it gets done. Management should not have to repeatedly follow up. 2. Trust & Integrity You will have visibility into highly sensitive financial information. We need someone with mature judgment and a strong sense of professional responsibility. 3. Financial Judgment You notice when the numbers don't make sense. You know what questions to ask. You understand that a report being generated successfully does not mean the report is correct. 4. Ownership You follow problems through to resolution instead of simply handing them to someone else. 5. Critical Thinking You challenge assumptions respectfully and are comfortable telling management when you believe something requires further investigation. 6. Curiosity & Learning You actively learn new systems, technologies and ways of working. 7. Process Improvement You naturally look at repetitive or error-prone processes and ask: “Can we design this better?” Experience We Are Looking For Ideally you have: 7+ years of progressive accounting or finance experience Experience as a Financial Controller, Assistant Controller, Accounting Manager, Finance Manager, Finance Operations Lead or similar Experience owning or substantially managing month-end close Strong understanding of financial statements Strong balance-sheet reconciliation experience Cash-flow forecasting experience AP and AR oversight Budgeting and variance analysis Experience reviewing other people's accounting work Experience managing or mentoring finance staff Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills Experience with QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite or similar accounting systems Strong professional English Experience working with North American or international businesses Experience supporting multiple entities, countries or currencies is strongly preferred. CPA, CA, ACCA, CMA or equivalent credentials are valuable but not mandatory if you have exceptional practical experience. Regional & Multi-Entity Experience Experience maintaining or reconciling a chart of accounts across multiple entities or countries, and working knowledge of regional compliance requirements (tax filings, statutory reporting, or coordinating with local accounting/tax advisors across jurisdictions), is a strong plus. Banking, Financing & Growth Experience (a plus, not required) We would love to hear from candidates who have helped a growing business move up a stage of financial maturity — for example, building the reporting and controls that supported a bank facility or lender relationship, running cash-flow forecasts used for financing decisions, supporting an investor or due-diligence process, or helping a company expand into new entities or countries. We are not looking for someone whose main claim is a large institutional fundraise. We are looking for real, demonstrated progression — something like: "When the company was $15M, I helped build the financial reporting, improved working capital, prepared the bank package, helped secure a facility, and built the systems that supported the company as it grew to $40M." Backgrounds We're Especially Interested In SaaS / software / technology; IoT / telecom; technology-enabled services; logistics, fleet or transportation; PE-backed growth businesses; startups or scale-ups that became meaningful businesses; multi-entity entrepreneurial companies; subscription or recurring-revenue businesses; and businesses that combine hardware with recurring software or services. Big Four experience is a great foundation, but we're most interested in people who went on to operate inside a business afterward. AI / Automation Experience We would particularly like to meet candidates who can demonstrate something they have actually built. Examples include: A Claude Project used as a finance knowledge or analysis system An automated monthly reporting process A recurring financial audit/checking workflow A reconciliation tool An AI-assisted AR or collections process A financial dashboard A workflow connecting several systems An automated variance-analysis process An internal finance tool built using AI-assisted coding A process that substantially reduced manual finance work Simply saying “I use ChatGPT” is not what we are looking for. We want to understand: What problem did you identify? What did you build? How did it work? What controls did you put around it? What changed as a result? Location & Schedule We are particularly interested in candidates based in LATAM because strong overlap with the Toronto / Eastern North American workday is important. Candidates elsewhere may still be considered if they can provide substantial working-hour overlap. Compensation depending on experience, demonstrated financial judgment, leadership capability and ability to improve systems. We may also consider beginning with an experienced candidate on a part-time or trial basis. Hiring Process We intend to move quickly, but we will evaluate this position carefully. The process will include: Application review Short screening interview Financial judgment interview Paid practical assessment Final discussion Reference checks Practical Assessment Finalists will receive a fictional company's financial and operational information, which may include: P&L Balance sheet General ledger Bank reconciliations AP aging AR aging Payroll information Budget Cash-flow forecast Prior-period results You will be asked to identify: Problems Risks Unusual trends Missing information Questions you would ask What you would investigate What you would require before approving the financial reporting There will also be a process-improvement / AI exercise. We may provide a manual finance workflow and ask you to explain how you would redesign it using better processes, automation and AI. We care about how you think, not simply whether you find every planted accounting error. To Apply Put the keyword LEDGER in your subject line. Before question 1, answer this reading check in your own words (the answers are in this post — this is how we know you actually read it): a. Where are we especially interested in candidates being based, and why? b. Name two of the AI tools or platforms we mention in this post that we'd like you to already be experimenting with. Then please answer the following questions. 1. Finance Ownership What is the most significant finance operation you have personally owned or managed? Please explain your responsibilities, company size and team size. 2. Financial Judgment Tell us about a financial number, report or assumption that looked reasonable but that you challenged. What made you question it, and what did you discover? 3. Reliability Tell us about a finance process or responsibility where other people depended on you every week or every month. How did you make sure it was completed accurately and on time? 4. Month-End A bookkeeper tells you that the month is closed. What do you personally review before telling the CEO that the financial statements are reliable? 5. Cash Flow What are the most important judgment-based assumptions in a 13-week cash-flow forecast? 6. Global Operations Tell us about your experience supporting companies operating across multiple countries, entities or currencies. 7. AI / Automation Describe one finance process that you personally automated or substantially redesigned. What existed before? What did you build? Which tools did you use? What changed afterward? 8. AI Tools What have you built using Claude, Claude Projects, Claude Code, ChatGPT, AI coding tools, APIs, scripts, Zapier/Make or similar technologies? Please be specific. 9. Controls What finance activities would you not fully automate using AI, and why? 10. Process Design Imagine five finance administrators spend several hours every Monday manually collecting reports, updating spreadsheets, reviewing customer balances and identifying issues. How would you approach improving that process? 11. Management Challenge Tell us about a time you disagreed with a CEO, CFO or senior manager about a financial issue. What did you do? 12. Practical Details Please provide: Current location Current working hours/time zone Desired monthly compensation in USD Earliest available start date LinkedIn profile, if available Any examples, screenshots or descriptions of finance tools or automations you have built 13. AI/Automation Loom (required) Record a short Loom (max 8 minutes) walking through one real finance automation, tool or process you personally built for a team — not a generic tour of an AI tool. Show the before, the actual build (a script, a Claude/ChatGPT workflow, a Zapier/Make chain, a spreadsheet system, whatever it was), the controls you put around it, and what changed as a result. If you honestly have not built anything like this yet, say so plainly in one line, and instead walk through, live and thinking out loud, how you personally would use Claude to redesign the Monday-morning manual-reporting workflow described above. Applications without this Loom will not be reviewed.

title: AI Video Producer & Editor - German Market Cat Supplement Brand
job_title: AI Video Producer & Editor - German Market Cat Supplement Brand
description: AI VIDEO PRODUCER & EDITOR - GERMAN MARKET CAT SUPPLEMENT BRAND Remote | Part-time, growing | Start: ASAP | $5 per hour READ THIS FIRST This job post is long and this application will take you 30 to 45 minutes. That is on purpose. I am hiring ONE person. I would rather get 5 serious applications than 200 lazy ones. If you send the same message to 40 job posts a day, close this now - you will not get through. But please do not be scared off either. You will not be inventing anything. You get the script, the product photos, the reference ad, the format specs, and every single tool paid for by me. What you need is to already be good at this and to deliver on time. If that sounds like you, keep reading. THE MOST IMPORTANT REQUIREMENT - READ BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE You must already be able to do this work today. I am not hiring someone to train. I am not hiring someone who wants to learn AI video generation on my account and on my time. I am hiring someone who is already producing AI video ads right now, in production, for real brands or for their own offers. And you must apply with a PORTFOLIO. Links to actual finished videos you made yourself. No portfolio, no reply. That is not a threat, it is just how I will sort through the applications. If your work is not linked in your message, I will never see it and I will never ask for it. Tutorials, test renders and course projects are not a portfolio. Neither is an agency reel where you cannot tell me which part was yours. I want to see finished ads or finished videos that went out into the world. ABOUT US We run a cat supplement brand on Shopify, selling to Germany, Austria and Switzerland (the DACH market). We are doing six figures per month and we scale with paid ads on Facebook and Instagram. Every ad we run is produced with AI. No film crew, no studio, no actors, no shipping products to creators. That is the whole model, and it is why this role exists. THE BIG IDEA - WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL EDITING JOB Right now our creative output is the bottleneck. Not the budget, not the product, not the audience - the number of finished ads we can put in front of people. That is a strange and very specific problem to have: we can fund more ad spend than we can produce ads for. In paid advertising, creatives burn out. An ad that prints money today is tired in three weeks, and if there is nothing new to replace it, the whole account cools down. So the number of ads you deliver is not a production statistic. It is the ceiling on how big this brand can get. That is the job. This is a doer role, not a manager role. You produce. Nobody reports to you and you do not build a team. If that changes later, it changes because you made it obvious that it should. WHAT YOU WILL PRODUCE You must be able to produce all of these yourself, from a script I write: - AI UGC ads - a generated person on camera talking about the product, with their cat - VSL and advertorial cuts - longer sales videos cut to a script, with captions and B-roll - Cartoon, claymation and stylized animation - cat content that is not photoreal - 1:1 rebuilds of winning ads - we hand you an ad that already works and you rebuild it exactly, changing one variable. Same structure, same pacing, same feel, different hook or different actor. - The cut itself - burned-in German captions, clean sans-serif, inside the safe zone, hook in the first two seconds, no dead air, exported to spec, vertical 9:16 About the 1:1 rebuilds, because this is where people drop out: if the reference has a cut on beat four, your version has a cut on beat four. "Close enough" is not a delivery. If you need creative freedom to stay motivated, you will not enjoy this role - and we would both rather find that out now. THE GERMAN PART - AND WHY IT IS NOT A PROBLEM Our ads are in German. You do not need to speak a word of German. I write every script. I give it to you finished, in German. You generate the voiceover from my text, you burn in the captions from my text, and you cut it. What I do need is that you are careful with a language you do not speak. That means: no dropped umlauts, no autocorrect quietly turning my words into something else, no captions cut off mid-word because you could not tell where the sentence ends. You copy what I send you exactly, character for character, and when the caption text and the voiceover do not match, you tell me instead of guessing. People who have edited in a foreign language before know exactly what I mean. It is not hard - it is just attention. STOP. READ THIS PART CAREFULLY. Here is the first filter: The very first word of your application message must be MANGO. Not in the middle. Not at the end. The first word, on its own line, before anything else. Like this: MANGO Hi Erik, ... If your message does not start with MANGO, I will not read it - no matter how good your portfolio is. This is not a joke and I will not make an exception. Most applicants will fail this, and that is fine. ACCOUNTABILITY AND COMMUNICATION This is the part I care about most, so I am going to be very clear. I am not looking for someone who never has a problem. Everybody gets sick. Power goes out. Family emergencies happen. Typhoons happen. I have zero problem with any of that. What I have a problem with is silence. If you are ill, if your internet dies, if a render fails and the delivery will be late - send me one message. Before the deadline, not after it. That is all I ask, and if you do it, we will always find a solution together. Going quiet on a delivery is the one thing that ends this immediately. Not because I am strict, but because I plan ad launches around your delivery date and I cannot plan around someone I have to chase. Beyond that, I expect three things: - You ask before you produce. When a brief is unclear, you ask first, instead of delivering five wrong ads and then explaining them. - You flag what will not work. If a script cannot be built visually, tell me before you start, not after the render. - You work independently. You do not need to be reminded or micromanaged. WHAT YOU MUST BRING (hard requirements - no exceptions) 1. A PORTFOLIO. Links to 2-3 finished videos or ads you made yourself. Own work only. This is requirement number one and there is no way around it. 2. 2+ years producing or editing short-form video, and at least the last year of it working with AI-generated footage. 3. You have shipped AI video in production - for clients, for a brand, or for your own offers. Not tutorials, not test renders. I want to see the actual videos. 4. Hands-on with a serious AI generation stack of your choice, and the judgment to know when a generation is unusable and has to be redone instead of shipped. Which tools you use is up to you - I pay for them either way. 5. CapCut or Premiere Pro for the cut, your pick, as long as the output is consistent. 6. Comfortable working with AI voiceover (ElevenLabs or similar), including voices in a language you do not speak. 7. Conversational English, spoken and written. 8. Reliable internet and a machine that can actually handle video work. 9. Willing to sign a freelance contract and a short NDA before you get access to our assets. 10. Willing to do a short unpaid test task before we get on a call. It is small - roughly one to two hours of work - and it is the same thing you would do on the job. BONUS (not required, but it moves you to the top of my list) - You have produced paid ads before, not just organic content - Experience in the pet niche - cats especially - After Effects - You have edited in a language you do not speak - Music-driven ads, avatar ads, Disney-style or claymation animation - You have built your own generation workflow and can explain why it is faster than the obvious one THE TOOLS - I PAY FOR EVERYTHING I pay for every tool account, every subscription and every generation credit. You never spend your own money on this job, and you never pay for a credit out of your own pocket. Which AI generation tool you produce in is your choice. If you are fast in Higgsfield, use Higgsfield. If your stack is Veo, Kling, Sora, Midjourney, Runway or something I have not heard of yet, use it and tell me why it is better. Same for the cut - CapCut or Premiere, whatever you are fastest in. What I care about is the finished ad, not the software. Tell me in your application what you need and I will buy it. Voiceover runs through ElevenLabs or comparable. Communication runs on WhatsApp and email. Files live in a shared drive with a fixed folder structure and naming convention. WHAT I PROVIDE - Every tool, every subscription and every generation credit, fully paid - The script for every ad - you never write copy, and you never have to write in German - Product photos, existing footage, brand assets and reference ads, so "done" is never a guess - Format specs, so you always know what correct looks like - One revision round per delivery, with specific feedback, not vague feedback - Direct access to me. No account manager, no layers. WORKING HOURS AND WHERE THIS ROLE IS GOING - 100% remote, from anywhere in the Philippines - The work is asynchronous. No shift, no fixed working hours, no being on call. You get a brief, you deliver by the agreed date, and how you organize your day is your business. - No overlap with my time zone required. I am in Europe. You will not be asked to work nights. - Right now: roughly 10 to 15 hours per week. It depends on how much we are testing. I am not going to pretend this is a fixed 40-hour job today. - Where this is going: we are scaling and creative volume is our bottleneck, so the hours grow. The plan is to grow this into a much bigger role for the right person - more hours, more responsibility, more pay. - One fixed 30-minute call per week, camera on. We agree on the day and time together once you start, and then it stays there. That is where we go through what landed, what did not, what you need from me, and what I want produced next. I give direct feedback and I expect you to use it. I also expect you to tell me when a brief is bad or a spec makes no sense. That call goes both ways. - English is our working language. HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED 1. Finished videos delivered per week 2. Turnaround time per delivery - agreed date, hit every time 3. Revision rounds per video - target: one or fewer 4. Spec compliance - correct format, safe zone, captions, naming, folder 5. German text accuracy - captions and voiceover exactly as I sent them 6. Communication - I always know where you are COMPENSATION (all amounts in USD) $5 per hour, for the hours you actually work, tracked. At 10 to 15 hours per week that is roughly $200 to $320 per month today - and both the hours and the rate grow as we scale. I move people up when they earn it. I have never lost a great person over money and I do not plan to start. Also included: - Paid twice a month, on time, via Wise or PayPal - Every tool, subscription and generation credit paid by me - Bonuses when the business does well - when we grow, you grow - Paid Philippine public holidays - 13th month bonus after one full year - Freelance contract and NDA - Long-term position - I want one person who gets faster every month, not a one-off gig One honest note: at today's hours this is a part-time income. If you currently work with another client, that is completely fine with me, as long as my deliveries are on time. As we scale, this role is meant to become your main one. HOW TO APPLY Apply here through OnlineJobs.ph. Do not email me - I read everything in this system and nowhere else. Start your message with MANGO on its own line. Then answer all 6 questions. Be specific - vague answers are the fastest way to get rejected. 1. YOUR PORTFOLIO. Links to 2-3 videos or ads YOU made. Own work only - no agency reels, no team projects, no "I was part of the team that". For each one: which tools you used, which parts were AI-generated, and what exactly your part was. If there are no links in your message, I will not reply. 2. YOUR AI WORK SPECIFICALLY. Which AI generation tools do you produce in today, and what have you actually shipped with them? Pick one AI video you linked above and walk me through how you made it - what you generated, what failed, and what you had to redo. 3. YOUR SPEED AND YOUR SETUP. How many finished 15-second vertical ads can you produce in one working day, starting from a script? A real number, not "many". Which cutting program do you use, what computer do you work on, and what is your internet speed? 4. FOREIGN LANGUAGE. You will build ads in German from my scripts. You do not need to speak German. Tell me: how do you make sure captions in a language you do not speak end up 100% correct on screen - no missing letters, no cut-off words, no mismatch with the voiceover? Have you edited in a language you do not speak before? Which one? 5. YOUR SITUATION. When can you start? How many hours per week can you commit right now? Are you okay with $5 per hour with tracked hours, and with a short unpaid test task before we get on a call? What tools would you want me to pay for? 6. A 60-SECOND RECORDING OF YOURSELF SPEAKING ENGLISH. Loom, a voice message, an unlisted YouTube link, whatever is easiest. Introduce yourself and walk me through one of the videos you linked. No production, no script, no editing - phone camera or just audio is completely fine, and I mean that. This is the one thing you send me that is not supposed to look produced. I am not judging your setup or your confidence on camera. I want to hear how you speak English. Applications that do not start with MANGO, or that skip any of the 6 questions, or that have no portfolio links, will not be reviewed. I am strict about this on purpose - following a brief exactly is the single most important part of this job. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT 1. I read your application and look at your portfolio 2. Short unpaid test task on a real brief - one finished ad, about one to two hours of work. I send you the script, the assets and the specs. 3. Video call in English, camera on, with the people whose test task convinced me 4. Hire, first paid deliveries, then we review the rate I keep the number of test tasks small on purpose, so if you get there, you are already a serious candidate. I read every application that follows the instructions, and I reply fast. If this sounds like you, apply today. I am hiring one person and I am hiring quickly. Start your message with: MANGO

A list of the software platforms you have personally used. A screenshot of your internet-speed test. Your available working hours in Eastern Time. Your earliest available start date. Whether you currently have a job or support other clients. Contact information for one professional reference. title: Amazon / Bol.com Listing & Catalog VA
description: Happy on Web is a Dutch e-commerce company selling consumer electronics accessories (e-bike batteries and chargers, audio, adapters, smart home) on ---------- , Amazon, eBay, Kaufland and French marketplaces. 1,400+ products, growing fast. ## The job Every marketplace has its own rules for product pages: which images are allowed, which fields are required, how categories, EANs and product data must be filled, which words and claims are not allowed. The rules change, and we add new products every week. Your job is to make sure every product we sell meets those rules — now, and every time something changes. Concretely: - You work through our full catalog product by product, using a written checklist we give you, and record per product what you checked and what you found. - You check images (logos, certification marks, packaging claims, image requirements), category and product type, EAN/GS1 data, required fields (product safety data, manufacturer information), and listing text. - Our listing text is in Dutch, German and French. You run it through a translation tool and screen it against a list of flag words and patterns we give you. If anything matches, you flag it and paste the original sentence. - Where the checklist tells you what the correct value is (wrong or missing fields, category, EAN data, image requirements), you fix it yourself — and you log every change in a before/after column in Google Sheets, so every edit you make can be traced and checked. - Text is different. You don't rewrite titles, descriptions or specifications in Dutch, German or French. If text violates a rule, you flag it with the original sentence, and a colleague who reads the language d ---------- and writes the fix. You never guess what a product spec should be. - You do notice patterns. If the same field is missing on forty products in a row, if a flag word catches everything, if the checklist doesn't cover something you keep running into: you write it down and send it to us as a suggestion. Separately from your tracker, and without changing how you work until we say so. - Once the full catalog is done, the work continues: new products before they go live, re-checks when a marketplace changes its rules, and later the same for our other marketplaces. - Second phase, once the audit routine runs: you also handle the follow-up with the marketplaces. That means opening seller support cases (rejected images, EAN conflicts, wrong category, blocked or suppressed listings, policy questions) using our templates, tracking them, and answering the marketplace's replies. This is seller-side case work with ---------- and Amazon, not buyer-facing customer service. Output: one tracker row per product. Every row has a source (screenshot, field name, URL, exact sentence). "None" or "looks fine" is not a valid entry. If you checked something and found nothing, you write down what you checked. This is repetitive, precise work at around 40 products per day. If you get bored by checklists, this is not your job. If you like a list that gets shorter every day and a tracker that is always correct, it is. ## What we need from you - Experience working in a marketplace seller back-end (Amazon Seller Central, ---------- , eBay or similar) on the product data side: listings, catalog, product fields. Not customer service, not ads. - Spreadsheet discipline: you can work through thousands of rows without skipping one, and your tracker is readable by someone who has never seen it. - You follow a checklist exactly. When the checklist doesn't cover a case, you don't guess: you flag it and ask. - You think while you work. You see when the same problem keeps coming back, and you tell us what you think is behind it. We want those suggestions; we don't want you acting on them on your own. - You can work with text in a language you don't read using translation tools, and you say so when a translation is not good enough to judge. - Clear written English. We work asynchronously; almost all communication is written. Not needed: Dutch, design skills, PPC, ---------- experience specifically. ## Who this job is not for Please don't apply if you are mainly a: - Graphic designer or product image designer. There is no design in this job. - PPC / Amazon Ads specialist. We don't run ads in-house. - Amazon growth, brand or marketplace manager. Nobody manages anything here; you check products against a list. - General VA (admin, email, social media, appointment setting). We select on marketplace product data experience, not on being flexible. - Buyer-facing customer service (answering customers, returns, chat support). Note the difference: seller support cases with ---------- or Amazon about listing and policy issues are part of this job, and experience with those is a plus. Answering buyers is not. If your profile is a mix of many of the above, you will not be selected. We want someone who has done product data work in a marketplace back-end and likes doing it precisely. ## What we select on Only these four things, in this order: 1. Hands-on experience in a marketplace seller back-end on the product data side (listings, catalog, product fields). Show it with specifics, not with a tool list. 2. Proof that you can do large repetitive data work accurately (your answer to point 2 below). 3. Written English: clear, short, answers the question asked. 4. Whether you followed the application instructions exactly. We select on depth, not on numbers: one platform where you really did the product data work beats five platforms you touched. Years on a resume, certificates and tool lists don't tell us that — your specifics do. A plus, not a requirement: you have opened and followed up seller support cases with Amazon or ---------- about listing or policy issues (suppressed listings, image rejections, EAN or category problems). If you have, tell us in point 4 below. To show us you have read this far: put the word ROSENBERGER in the subject line of your application. ## What we offer - $650/month, full-time (40 hours), fixed monthly rate paid via Wise - Long-term position, normal contract, no trial-project construction - Start date: Monday 14 September 2026 - Software and tools paid by us - Written SOPs and a checklist. You are not expected to know the rules by heart; you are expected to apply the checklist exactly and to tell us when it doesn't cover a case. ## How to apply Send us: 1. Which marketplace back-ends you have worked in, how long, and what you did in them. 2. One example of a large repetitive data-checking job you did (any kind): how many items, how you kept it accurate, how you tracked your progress — and one thing you noticed while doing it that you passed on to whoever you worked for. 3. Your availability from the start date above. 4. Optional: one seller support case you opened yourself with Amazon or ---------- about a listing or policy issue. What the issue was, what you wrote, what the outcome was. Skip this point if you haven't done it; don't invent one. Keep it short and specific. Don't claim accuracy — show it in your answer to point 2. Applications that don't answer points 1 to 3 will not be read. Selection: short email exchange, then a video call.

title: Project Manager – Publications & Creative Projects
description: Full-Time | Remote | Philippines Spiritus is an international Catholic sacred-music organization bringing together music, art, faith, ecology, and cultural heritage. Our projects involve musicians, artists, writers, churches, cathedrals, schools, cultural institutions, and environmental organizations around the world. Spiritus is entering a major period of growth, with new performances, recordings, publications, international collaborations, and ecological initiatives now in development. We are looking for an exceptionally organized and detail-oriented Project Manager – Publications & Creative Projects to join our team in the Philippines. This is an unusual role combining project management, editorial and publication work, document preparation, research, recruitment, and creative production. It would be particularly well suited to someone with experience in publishing, editorial design, graphic design, communications, document production, or creative project management who is ready to take on broader responsibility. The right person will have the opportunity to gradually take ownership of major Spiritus projects and grow into a larger leadership role within the organization. What You’ll Work On One of your first major projects will be helping manage the production of a beautiful approximately 200-page commemorative art book documenting a sacred-music recording project in France. The book will combine extensive photography, essays and spiritual reflections, musical analysis, texts and translations, captions, credits, and other materials. We intend it to have the quality and visual sophistication of a book published by a major museum, gallery, or cultural institution. You will help manage the assembly of the book from beginning to end, including: Organizing hundreds of photographs and other visual assets Collecting and tracking essays, texts, translations, captions, credits, and other materials Coordinating with writers, editors, designers, translators, photographers, and other contributors Preparing, formatting, and proofreading documents Maintaining detailed records of what has been received, what is missing, what requires revision, and what still needs approval Working closely with the book designer to make sure every element is complete and correct Helping manage revisions and final preparation for publication Maintaining organized project files, trackers, and documentation You do not need to be a professional book designer. We expect to hire a specialist designer for the major art book. Your role will be to help organize and manage the large amount of material that goes into the publication, work closely with the designer, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks. Other Spiritus Projects You will also assist with a wide range of other Spiritus projects, including: Preparing materials for CDs and CD booklets and coordinating with manufacturers Organizing text, photography, credits, metadata, and other publication materials Creating and editing polished documents and presentation materials Helping manage an international project collecting nature photography, video, and sound recordings Overseeing and guiding ongoing searches for project submissions Conducting detailed online research and outreach Researching cultural institutions, publications, universities, organizations, and potential collaborators Running recruitment searches for specialized creative professionals Managing job postings and applicant pipelines Screening applicants and reviewing resumes and portfolios Researching promising candidates and preparing strong shortlists Helping coordinate other Spiritus projects as the organization continues to grow As you gain experience with Spiritus, you may gradually take greater ownership of projects, coordinate other team members, and independently manage larger areas of work. Who We’re Looking For Above all, we need someone who is extremely organized, meticulous, resourceful, reliable, and capable of taking ownership. Strong candidates may come from backgrounds such as: Publishing or editorial production Book, magazine, or publication design Graphic or document design Communications Creative project management Arts or cultural organizations Media production Editorial operations You should have: Exceptional attention to detail Excellent written English Strong organizational and project-management ability Good visual judgment and typography/layout instincts Experience preparing sophisticated documents or publications Strong skills with Adobe InDesign and/or other professional design and document-production software Strong proofreading and editorial skills The ability to organize large quantities of text, images, files, and information Strong research skills and confidence finding people and information online The ability to manage many small details without losing sight of the larger project The ability to communicate clearly with writers, designers, vendors, applicants, and other collaborators Strong follow-through and reliability The initiative to identify and solve problems independently rather than simply waiting for instructions Experience with books, publications, museums, cultural institutions, music, photography, visual arts, or international creative projects is especially welcome. The Kind of Person Who Will Succeed Here You are probably a good fit if you are the person who notices when: A caption or credit is missing A filename is inconsistent A photograph has not yet been approved A contributor still owes us a document Two versions of a file are being confused Something in a layout does not look right A deadline is approaching and someone needs to follow up A project would work better if there were a clearer system behind it You should enjoy bringing order to complex creative projects and taking something with hundreds of moving pieces and helping turn it into a beautiful, finished result. About Spiritus Spiritus creates ambitious sacred-music and cultural projects with an international scope. Our work brings together music, Catholic faith, beauty, ecology, culture, and the natural world, often in collaboration with churches, cathedrals, musicians, artists, scholars, educators, cultural organizations, and environmental groups. Current projects involve participants and collaborators across the United States, Europe, Africa, Asia, and elsewhere. We are a small and growing organization, so this is not a narrowly defined corporate position. The right person will have the opportunity to become deeply involved in our projects, take increasing responsibility, and grow with the organization. Learn more about our work at Spiritus.art. Location: Philippines, remote Schedule: Full-time Reports to: Spiritus Philippines Manager To Apply Please send: Your resume/CV A short introduction explaining why this particular position interests you Examples of publications, books, documents, layouts, presentations, or other visual/editorial work you have produced or helped manage A brief description of the most complicated project you have personally organized or coordinated A short explanation of how you kept that project organized and made sure important details were not missed We care much more about quality, judgment, organization, initiative, and attention to detail than about having a particular degree or job title.

title: Full-Time Legal Virtual Assistant / Case Manager
job_title: Full-Time Legal Virtual Assistant / Case Manager
description: About the Role We are looking for a highly organized, proactive Legal Virtual Assistant to help manage multiple active California legal matters from start to finish. This is not simply a document-organizing position. You will help keep every case moving, make sure deadlines are tracked, filings are prepared correctly, supporting evidence is organized, hearings are prepared for in advance, and nothing important falls through the cracks. The goal is simple: every case should be organized, current, deadline-ready, filing-ready, and hearing-ready at all times. Responsibilities You will help manage approximately 10-15 active legal matters and may be responsible for: Maintaining a master legal tracker showing every case, deadline, hearing, filing, outstanding task, and next action. Reviewing court orders, minute orders, emails, correspondence, discovery, and case documents and updating the tracker accordingly. Preparing filing packages, exhibits, declarations, supporting documents, proofs of service, and court forms for review and signature. Checking court filing requirements, formatting requirements, filing instructions, and procedural deadlines. Making sure filings are complete before submission, including signatures, attachments, exhibits, captions, case numbers, and required supporting forms. Monitoring court dockets and identifying newly filed documents, rulings, hearing dates, or changes that require action. Maintaining organized folders for each case with consistent naming and version control. Creating hearing preparation packets containing the key filings, orders, evidence, timelines, arguments, and documents needed for the hearing. Preparing concise case summaries and timelines so the principal can quickly understand the current status of each matter. Organizing evidence including emails, text messages, recordings, transcripts, photographs, court documents, and other exhibits. Helping prepare discovery requests, discovery responses, deficiency lists, subpoenas, and supporting materials under direction. Tracking meet-and-confer deadlines, discovery deadlines, response deadlines, filing deadlines, service deadlines, and hearing dates. Coordinating signatures, service, electronic filing, document delivery, transcript requests, and other administrative case requirements. Researching California court procedures, local rules, forms, and filing requirements when requested. Following up proactively when documents, responses, signatures, court information, or other items are still outstanding. Maintaining a clear daily list of what is completed, what is pending, what is blocked, and what needs immediate attention. Hearing Readiness Every upcoming hearing should be prepared well before the hearing date. You will help confirm: What the hearing is about What orders are currently in effect What has already been filed What still needs to be filed Filing and service deadlines Important evidence and exhibits Relevant communications and prior orders Documents needed during the hearing Outstanding issues requiring a decision Follow-up actions after the hearing You should never wait until the day before a hearing to begin organizing the case. Filing Readiness Before any filing is considered ready, you should verify the filing package for completeness and flag anything missing. This includes checking court forms, captions, case numbers, dates, signatures, exhibits, declarations, attachments, pagination, proofs of service, filing instructions, and supporting documents. You are not expected to independently practice law or provide legal advice. Your responsibility is to make sure the legal work is organized, researched, documented, reviewed, and operationally ready. What We Are Looking For We want someone who is extremely organized, dependable, detail-oriented, comfortable working with large amounts of information, and capable of managing multiple deadlines without constant supervision. You should be comfortable with Google Drive, Google Docs, Google Sheets, Gmail, PDF documents, online court systems, electronic filing systems, AI tools, legal research, and document management. Experience with California family law, civil litigation, discovery, restraining-order matters, appeals, or self-represented litigants is a major advantage. Working Standards Be online, settled, prepared, and ready before scheduled meetings. Take ownership of tasks through completion. Do not simply identify a problem and hand it back. Research it, organize what you found, explain what is missing, and propose the next action. Communicate proactively. Do not disappear when something becomes difficult. Demonstrate progress before asking questions whenever possible. Every assigned task should ultimately have a clear status: Completed, Pending, Waiting on Someone, or Blocked, with the next action identified. Accuracy is extremely important. Never guess about a deadline, court requirement, filing status, or legal fact. Verify it and provide the source. Success in This Role You are succeeding when: No important deadline is missed. Every case has a clear next action. Documents can be found immediately. Filings are prepared ahead of deadlines. Hearings are organized in advance. Evidence is properly categorized and accessible. Outstanding items are actively followed up. The legal tracker accurately reflects the real status of every matter. The principal does not need to repeatedly ask what happened or what needs to happen next. Compensation: $700/month, full-time. This is intended to be a long-term position for someone who can become the operational owner of the legal case-management process.

Our ads run free by default; if one needs paid promotion, you flag it and we approve it in writing. No writing our ads. We provide the text; you post it as written.
