We start every editor on a lighter workload — a smaller number of videos per week — for the first stretch. Not because we're testing whether you can hold a job, but because we want to see how you fit: how you take feedback, how you handle a script we hand you, how you communicate when something's unclear, and whether the work holds up once the novelty wears off. It also gives you time to learn our customer, our angles, and what a "winning" video looks like in our account specifically. From there it scales. As the fit proves out and your creatives start performing, the volume goes up, the pay goes up, and the arrangement moves toward a secure, permanent full-time seat — with a defined monthly retainer rather than per-project work. To be clear about what we're offering: Phase 1 — Fit: Lower volume, paid per project or at a smaller retainer. Heavy feedback from us. We're both figuring out if this works. Phase 2 — Ramp: Volume increases, you take on the VSLs and the AI cartoon projects with less hand-holding, pay increases accordingly. Phase 3 — In-house: Full-time, secure retainer, you own the creative pipeline and have real input on direction. Room to grow into a creative lead as we bring on more editors. We're not looking for someone to fill a gap for three months. We're looking for the person who's still here in two years running our creative. The slow start is how we get there without either of us wasting the other's time. If you need immediate full-time income from day one, this probably isn't the right fit right now — and that's fine, just be upfront about it. What you'll actually be making 1. Long-form VSLs (Video Sales Letters) The core of the role. 2–7+ minute sales videos built off scripts we provide. You'll be responsible for: Pacing the entire video so retention doesn't collapse — pattern interrupts, cuts, zooms, motion, sound design, text emphasis, visual proof Sourcing your own b-roll. Stock libraries, licensed footage, UGC-style clips, screen recordings, archival, whatever the script calls for. You find it. You don't ask us to send it. In some cases we will also provide clips and we have a bunch of softwares that you can use to make this process easier aswell. Generating AI video to fill the gaps stock can't cover — visualizing mechanisms, metaphors, before/after states, scenarios that don't exist as footage. Building the visual language for a section, not just laying clips over a voiceover Kinetic text, callouts, subtitles, on-screen proof elements, testimonial treatments Sound design and music that carries emotional beats without burying the VO 2. AI cartoon / animated videos (short form AND long form) We're producing a growing volume of fully AI-generated animated content — story-driven ads, explainer content, character-led narratives. You'll take a script and: Build a consistent character and world (this is the hard part — character consistency across dozens of shots is a real skill and we'll be testing for it) Generate the shots yourself using AI image + video tools Handle lip sync, voiceover, and audio Cut it into a video that actually flows as a story rather than a slideshow of AI clips Deliver in both short form (15–60s, vertical) and long form formats 3. Short form paid ads Hook-first ads for Meta / TikTok. High volume, fast iteration. Multiple hook variants of the same body. You'll be cutting these constantly, and you'll be expected to have opinions about which hooks are worth testing. What we need you to be good at Non-negotiable: Editing that converts, not just editing that looks good. You understand hooks, retention curves, pattern interrupts, why the first 3 seconds d ---------- everything, and how to build toward a CTA. If you've never thought about a video in terms of watch time or CPA, you're not ready for this seat. Sourcing your own footage. Independently. You know where to find good b-roll, Generating AI video yourself. Not "willing to learn" — actually doing it now. You know how to prompt, how to iterate when a generation is wrong, how to maintain consistency, and how to upscale and clean up output so it doesn't look like AI slop. Strong technical craft — clean cuts, deliberate pacing, proper audio levels, colour that matches across mixed sources, subtitles that don't look like an afterthought. Speed. We ship a lot. Quality at volume is the whole game. Ownership. You get a script and a brief and come back with a finished asset. You flag problems early. You don't go quiet for four days. Tools — you should be fluent in most of these or their equivalents: Editing: Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, or CapCut. AI video: Higgsfield, Veo, Kling, Runway, Sora, Hailuo, Seedance — or whatever you've found works better AI image: Midjourney, Flux, Nano Banana, Ideogram Voice: ElevenLabs or similar Upscaling / cleanup: Topaz, Magnific Bonus: Descript, Adobe Podcast, motion graphics templating, basic scripting/automation for batching Removing text from video: Vmake Nice to have: You've written or restructured direct response scripts before You've worked on offers in health and wellnes niche You can take a competitor's winning ad, break down why it works, and build a better version You track what's new in AI video weekly because you find it genuinely interesting Who this is NOT for Editors who only work from supplied assets People who see AI tools as a threat or a gimmick "Cinematic" editors who make beautiful videos that don't sell Anyone who needs to be chased for updates Agencies or people who'll pass the work to a junior. We want the person doing the work. What you get A real seat on a growing team. We start light on purpose, but the destination is a secure full-time role — and if it works, we build our creative operation around you. Direct feedback loop on your work. You'll see spend, retention data, and CPA on the creatives you cut. Most editors never get this — it's the fastest way to get genuinely good. Budget for tools and subscriptions. We're not going to bottleneck you over a $50/mo AI credit plan. Performance bonuses when your creative becomes a winner. Room to grow into a creative lead role as we scale and bring on more editors under you. Fast decisions. Small team. No layers of approval. How to apply Please follow this exactly — it's the first filter. Send your portfolio. We want to see, specifically: At least one long-form VSL or long-form sales video you cut At least one AI-generated video you produced yourself (cartoon/animated preferred) Short form paid ads if you have them For 2–3 of those videos, tell us in one or two lines each: what the goal was, what you did to hold attention, and any performance numbers you're allowed to share (spend, ROAS, retention, CTR — whatever you have). Tell us your AI stack. Which tools you use for what, and one problem you've solved with them that most people get wrong. Your rate and your realistic capacity — how many long-form videos and how many short form ads per week. Turnaround time on a typical 10-minute VSL, assuming script and VO are provided. Confirm you're okay with the ramp-up structure — starting at lower volume and building toward full-time. One line is enough.

WHAT THE WORK IS Every week I send you raw footage. You send me back finished video. Per month: - 4 long videos, 3 to 5 minutes each, me talking to camera - 20 to 24 vertical clips cut from that same footage, for Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts - B-roll cut into short labeled segments I can reuse The look is already built. I will give you the template, the motion graphics files, the fonts, the colors, and written instruction sheets for every graphic. Your job is to apply it the same way every time. Not to redesign it. WHAT I NEED YOU TO BE GOOD AT - Adobe Premiere Pro. Organized projects, labeled bins, not 200 clips on one timeline. - Cutting a talking-head video so it moves. Taking out the ums, the false starts, and the parts where I lose my train of thought, without it sounding chopped up. - Reframing horizontal footage to vertical so my head is not cut off. - Clean captions. Correct spelling, good timing, not covering my face. - Basic color correction. Matching shots so my footage looks the same from cut to cut, and applying the preset I give you. I am not looking for a creative grade. I want it consistent. - Audio cleanup. Even levels through the whole video, room noise down, nothing clipping. If a viewer has to reach for the volume knob, the edit failed. - Hitting a deadline. And if you cannot hit it, telling me before it passes, not after. - Writing to me in clear English. If a brief is unclear, ask me. Do not guess and hope. WHAT THIS IS NOT This is not a creative director job. I am not looking for someone to reinvent the style every month. I want someone reliable who makes the same good thing over and over and gets faster at it. If you want full creative freedom, this will frustrate you. THE ARRANGEMENT Part time, ongoing, paid monthly. Same amount every month for the volume above. Rate depends on your experience and how the test goes. I would rather hire one person and train them well than keep starting over with new editors. If you are looking for a few weeks of work, this is not it. HOW TO APPLY Put the word ORANGE at the top of your message so I know you read this. Then send me: 1. Two links to talking-head videos you edited. For each one, tell me exactly what you did. Your available hours per week, and your time zone. 5. One sentence: what makes a talking-head video boring? Applications without the word ORANGE will not be read. Shortlisted applicants get a small paid test edit. I pay for the test whether I hire you or not.

It is a hands-on combination of digital asset management, creative content production, AI-powered visual creation, and digital marketing. Mission of the Role: You will own the lifecycle of our visual content, from raw material to organized assets to polished content that can be used for marketing, sales, our website, social media, and presentations. A successful person in this role should constantly be thinking: “What valuable content do we have, what are we missing, and how can I turn it into something useful?” Key Responsibilities: 1. Digital Asset & Project Portfolio Management • Take ownership of the company's growing library of photos, videos, renderings, drawings, graphics, and other visual assets. • Gather assets coming from multiple sources, including project managers, installers, job sites, internal communication channels, renderings, phones, drone footage, and management. • Develop and maintain an organized, scalable Digital Asset Management system. • Recommend the best platforms, workflows, naming structures, folders, tagging systems, and processes for managing our assets. • Make assets easy to search, retrieve, share, and reuse. • Review incoming content and identify what is valuable, what needs improvement, and how it can be used. • Maintain organized portfolios of completed and ongoing projects. • Ensure valuable content does not get lost simply because nobody noticed or organized it. 2. Photo, Rendering & Visual Production • Select and prepare the best images from projects. • Retouch, crop, color-correct, clean up, enhance, and professionally present photographs. • Improve job-site photos that were taken under less-than-ideal conditions. • Work with architectural/design renderings and transform them into more realistic, polished marketing visuals when appropriate. • Create new visuals using existing drawings, layouts, renderings, photos, and AI tools. • Create before/after, progress, comparison, project showcase, and similar visual content. • Handle day-to-day digital graphic design needs without requiring an outside graphic designer for every small task. 3. Video Content We do not expect high-end film production. We do expect strong, practical digital video skills. Responsibilities include: • Gather raw video from job sites, phones, project managers, installers, and future drone footage. • Identify the best clips and turn raw footage into useful content. • Trim, combine, clean up, resize, and enhance video. • Add captions, text, graphics, transitions, music, voiceovers, or other elements when appropriate. • Remove or replace unwanted audio. • Combine photos, renderings, progress footage, and finished footage into project videos. • Produce reels, progress updates, before/after videos, finished-project showcases, and other short-form content. • Repurpose one set of footage into multiple pieces of content when possible. 4. Directing Content Capture You will not personally be present at every project. Therefore, part of your responsibility is helping our field team capture better raw material. • Create simple shot lists and instructions for project managers and installers. • Proactively request specific photos, videos, angles, progress shots, or drone footage. • Identify missing content before the opportunity is gone. • Educate team members on what makes footage useful for marketing. • Think ahead about what will be needed to properly showcase a project after completion. 5. Social Media & Digital Presence Own the day-to-day execution of our digital presence, particularly: • Instagram • LinkedIn • WhatsApp Status • Google Business presence • Company website • ---------- • Other relevant platforms as they develop Responsibilities include: • Develop content from our existing project assets. • Write or refine captions and supporting copy. • Create and publish posts, reels, project showcases, and updates. • Maintain a consistent posting schedule. • Actively optimize content for maximum reach, traffic, engagement, and exposure on each platform. Understand how each platform’s algorithms, formats, timing, keywords, hashtags, trends, and other best practices affect visibility, and continuously test and improve our approach based on performance. • Adapt content appropriately for different platforms rather than simply posting the exact same thing everywhere. • Monitor and respond appropriately to comments, messages, and DMs. • Keep the company's online presence active, polished, professional, and consistent with our established brand guidelines. • Look for opportunities to repurpose existing material rather than constantly needing new content. 6. Website & Project Portfolio • Keep the website visually current and up to date. • Maintain the website’s project portfolio and visual content on an ongoing basis, ensuring it remains current, polished, accurate, and reflective of the company’s latest work. • Upload completed projects with strong imagery and well-written descriptions. • Organize projects so prospective customers can easily understand the work being presented. • Maintain and improve the online portfolio as new work becomes available. • Handle basic website content updates and minor technical/HTML-related work when needed. • Coordinate with outside technical professionals when an update is beyond the scope of this position. 7. Email & Other Digital Marketing When email marketing campaigns are used: • Prepare and organize the visual content. • Build or assist with email layouts. • Insert images, links, buttons, and other digital assets correctly. • Handle basic formatting/HTML as necessary. • Coordinate with others when copywriting or more advanced technical work is required. 8. AI & Technology Advanced practical use of AI is an important part of this position. We want someone who actively explores how modern tools can make work faster, better, and possible. This may include AI for: • Image generation and enhancement • Rendering enhancement and photorealistic visualization • Photo editing and cleanup • Video production and editing • Voiceover/audio • Graphic creation • Content development • Copy assistance • Workflow automation • Asset organization • Research and productivity We are not looking for someone who simply knows how to type prompts into ChatGPT. We want someone who is curious about new technology, experiments with tools, learns quickly, and continually improves the workflow. Required Experience & Skills: We are primarily interested in ability and portfolio, not degrees or job titles. The ideal candidate will have: • Approximately 2–5+ years of relevant hands-on experience in digital content, multimedia, creative production, digital marketing, or a related field. • Strong creative judgment, the ability to independently recognize what looks professional, what content has marketing potential, and what needs improvement without requiring detailed direction for every task. • Strong photo editing and enhancement abilities. • Practical video editing experience. • Good graphic design skills and a strong visual eye. • Experience creating content specifically for social media. • Understanding of social media platforms, formats, trends, and engagement. • Experience working with AI-powered creative tools. • Strong organizational and digital file-management skills. • Ability to learn new platforms and software quickly. • Basic website/content-management experience. • Basic HTML knowledge is preferred. • Excellent written English. • Clear spoken English for internal meetings and communication. • Strong attention to detail. • Ability to work independently and take ownership. Cultural & Brand Adaptability: Our company serves customers with specific preferences, expectations, communication styles, and cultural nuances. The successful candidate must be able to: • Observe and quickly understand the culture and audience of the company. • Learn subtle differences in communication, imagery, style, and presentation. • Avoid assuming that what works for one audience automatically works for another. • Follow established brand guidelines while developing a strong understanding of what feels appropriate for our customers. • Accept feedback and quickly adapt. Who Will Thrive in This Position: You will likely do very well here if you are the type of person who: • Sees an interesting job-site photo and immediately thinks, “We can do something with this.” • Doesn't wait to be told every individual task. • Enjoys both creativity and organization. • Likes turning messy raw material into something polished. • Notices missing information and goes after it. • Enjoys experimenting with AI and new technology. • Can research a problem and propose a solution. • Can build a system instead of simply following one. • Understands that creating great content and properly organizing it are equally important. • Takes ownership and follows things through to completion. Work Schedule: This is a full-time remote position working on our standard Eastern Time schedule: Monday–Thursday: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM Eastern Time Friday: 9:00 AM–1:00 PM Eastern Time Candidates must be consistently available for communication, collaboration, and meetings during these hours. Equipment & Work Environment: Because this is a remote creative position, the selected candidate must have: • A modern, reliable computer powerful enough to smoothly handle professional photo editing, video editing, graphics, browser-based AI tools, and multitasking. • 32 GB RAM minimum; 64 GB preferred. • Modern Intel i7 / AMD Ryzen 7 / Apple Silicon equivalent or better preferred. • Dedicated modern GPU with at least 8 GB of VRAM preferred, suitable for professional video editing, rendering, and AI workloads. • 1 TB SSD storage. • Reliable high-speed internet suitable for regularly uploading and downloading large photo and video files. • Webcam and good-quality headset/microphone. • A quiet, professional, designated workspace. • A second monitor is strongly preferred. The selected candidate is expected to provide and maintain the standard hardware, software, tools, and resources commonly required to perform this type of professional creative work. Specialized, enterprise-level, unusually expensive, or company-specific tools may be provided by Space Art Cabinetry at the company's discretion. Portfolio Required: Applicants must submit examples of previous work. We are particularly interested in seeing examples involving: • Photo editing/enhancement • Social media content • Graphics • Video editing • Project or portfolio presentation • AI-generated or AI-enhanced creative work Please clearly explain what you personally did on each example. Hiring Process: Candidates who appear to be a strong fit will go through: 1. Initial application and portfolio review. 2. Video interview. 3. Practical skills test using sample materials similar to what you would receive in this position. 4. Final interview. 5. Paid introductory/trial period. The practical test may include raw project photos, videos, renderings, and other assets. Candidates may be asked to demonstrate how they would organize the assets, improve them, turn them into useful content, and d ---------- how that content should be presented or distributed. Compensation: Hourly position. Compensation will be determined based on experience, portfolio quality, technical ability, and performance during the practical skills evaluation. Performance and compensation may be reviewed after the initial employment period. ________________________________________ The bottom line: We are looking for someone who can take ownership of our company's digital assets and digital presence, from a raw photo sitting in a job-site chat to a polished image, project portfolio, website update, reel, or social media post. If you are highly organized, visually creative, technically capable, AI-driven, and naturally look for ways to turn raw material into valuable content, we would like to hear from you.

title: EXPERIENCED XACTIMATE RESTORATION ESTIMATOR - $3000 month
description: # EXPERIENCED XACTIMATE RESTORATION ESTIMATOR ## Full-Time Remote | Phoenix, Arizona Hours **PLEASE READ THIS ENTIRE JOB POST BEFORE APPLYING.** There are specific application instructions throughout this post. **If you do not follow ALL application instructions, you will not be considered for the position.** We are looking for someone who pays attention to details, follows directions, and takes their career seriously. Consider the application process your first opportunity to show us how you work. --- # THIS IS NOT AN ENTRY-LEVEL POSITION **Xactimate experience is REQUIRED.** You must already be proficient at reviewing restoration documentation and building detailed, accurate Xactimate estimates and invoices. If you have never written Xactimate estimates yourself, please do not apply. If you only have basic Xactimate exposure, please do not apply. If you need someone to teach you how to write restoration estimates from the beginning, this is not the right position. We are specifically looking for an **experienced estimator who can contribute quickly and continue becoming an expert in the field.** **Symbility experience is a major bonus.** --- # ABOUT OUR COMPANY We are an established restoration company serving Phoenix, Arizona and surrounding cities for the past 15 years! We handle property damage projects involving: * Water damage * Fire and smoke damage * Mold remediation * Asbestos abatement * Reconstruction * Roofing * Insurance claims We have been in business since 2012 and have built our company around doing quality work, taking care of customers, and continually improving how we operate. We are looking for someone who wants more than a temporary freelance job. **We want someone who wants to become part of our team, grow with the company, improve their skills, take on more responsibility, and increase their growth and income as their value to the company increases.** --- # YOUR PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY You will work with our restoration team to turn our field documentation into accurate, detailed, defensible estimates and invoices. Our field team will provide documentation including: * Photos * Videos * Measurements * Moisture documentation * Technician notes * Equipment information * Scope notes * Insurance information * Other supporting documents You will review that information and build professional estimates and invoices. You should understand restoration well enough to recognize when documentation supports additional legitimate line items that may have been missed. We do not want someone who simply enters whatever information is handed to them. **We want an estimator who understands the work, thinks critically, catches missing items, asks good questions, and produces a complete and defensible scope.** --- # TYPES OF ESTIMATES YOU MAY WRITE You should be comfortable working with several types of property damage claims, including: ### Mitigation * Water mitigation * Emergency services * Demolition * Cleaning * Contents manipulation * Mold remediation * Asbestos abatement ### Reconstruction * Drywall * Paint * Flooring * Cabinets * Countertops * Trim * Doors * Framing * Insulation * Electrical * Plumbing * General reconstruction * Larger loss reconstruction ### Fire * Fire damage * Smoke damage * Cleaning * Contents * Demolition * Reconstruction * Large-loss estimating ### Roofing You may occasionally assist with: * Roof repairs * Roof replacements * Storm damage * Insurance roofing claims * Supplements Roofing experience is preferred but is not required if your restoration estimating experience is strong. --- # ADJUSTER COMMUNICATION & CLAIM NEGOTIATION This position is not limited to writing estimates. You must also be comfortable communicating professionally with insurance adjusters and other claim representatives. Responsibilities may include: * Reviewing carrier estimates * Comparing carrier scopes against our scope * Identifying missing or incorrect line items * Preparing supplements * Providing supporting documentation * Responding to estimate revisions * Discussing legitimate scope differences * Explaining why specific work or line items are necessary * Following up on outstanding approvals * Negotiating scope and pricing disagreements * Moving claims toward resolution and approval Our goal is not to add unnecessary items to claims. Our goal is to make sure the estimate accurately reflects the work that was legitimately required or needs to be completed and that our documentation supports our scope. You must be comfortable professionally defending your estimate. --- # THE PERSON WE ARE LOOKING FOR We want someone who: * Is punctual - If you aren't consistent and cant show up for your shift lets not waste each others time * Has significant hands-on Xactimate estimating experience * Can write estimates independently * Understands restoration terminology and processes * Understands insurance restoration claims * Understands mitigation and reconstruction scopes * Knows how to identify commonly missed legitimate line items * Understands supporting documentation * Can review and challenge carrier estimates * Is comfortable communicating with adjusters * Writes professional emails * Communicates clearly with our internal team * Pays extremely close attention to detail * Takes ownership of their work * Meets deadlines * Does not need constant supervision * Can manage multiple estimates at the same time * Asks questions when documentation is incomplete * Wants to continually improve We especially want someone who takes pride in becoming **exceptionally good at their craft.** If you enjoy learning Xactimate, understanding restoration, finding legitimate missing scope items, and building extremely thorough estimates, you're likely an EXCELLENT fit. --- # REQUIRED EXPERIENCE You must have: * Professional Xactimate experience * Experience personally writing Xactimate estimates * Strong knowledge of Xactimate line items * Restoration and/or insurance estimating experience * Strong written English & spoken English * Strong attention to detail * Ability to work independently * Reliable computer * Reliable high-speed internet Preferred experience: * Symbility * Water mitigation * Mold remediation * Asbestos * Fire restoration * Reconstruction * Roofing * Supplements * Adjuster negotiations * Large-loss estimating * Insurance restoration contractors --- # HOURS This is a **full-time remote position.** You will work primarily during **Phoenix, Arizona business hours.** You must be available and responsive during your scheduled working hours because you will be working directly with our Arizona team and communicating with insurance representatives. --- # COMPENSATION **Starting compensation: $6.00-$14.00 USD per hour, depending heavily on experience and demonstrated ability.** This is not intended to be a dead-end position. There will be opportunities for: * Pay increases * Performance bonuses * Increased responsibility * Professional development * Leadership opportunities * Long-term career advancement We reward people who create value, take ownership, continually improve, and make the team better. --- # HOW TO APPLY **Read this section carefully.** Your application must include ALL of the following. ## 1. EMAIL/APPLICATION SUBJECT The title or subject of your application must contain: **ESTIMATOR HIRING MANAGER** If "ESTIMATOR HIRING MANAGER" is not included at the beginning of your reply, your application will not be considered. --- ## 2. ANSWER THESE QUESTIONS Copy these questions into your application and answer each one. 1. How many years have you personally used Xactimate? 2. On a scale of 1-10, how would you rate your Xactimate ability? 3. What types of estimates have you written? List all that apply: * Water mitigation * Mold * Asbestos * Fire * Reconstruction * Roofing * Contents * Large loss * Other 4. Have you written mitigation invoices from technician photos, notes, drying logs, and equipment documentation? 5. Have you written reconstruction estimates from photos, measurements, Matterport, sketches, or field documentation? 6. How many years of Symbility experience do you have? 7. Have you personally communicated or negotiated scope with insurance adjusters? 8. Describe your experience handling supplements and disagreements with carrier estimates. 9. What are some Xactimate line items or charges you commonly see missed on water mitigation estimates? 10. What are some commonly missed items you look for when reviewing reconstruction estimates? 11. What is the largest estimate you have personally written? 12. Approximately how many estimates can you accurately complete during a normal week? 13. Which estimating or restoration certifications do you currently have, if any? 14. What restoration companies, estimating companies, adjusting firms, or insurance-related companies have you previously worked with? 15. Are you currently working for another company? If yes, explain your current schedule. 16. Are you able to work full-time during Phoenix, Arizona business hours? 17. Why are you looking for a new position? --- # 3. SUBMIT ESTIMATE SAMPLES Please submit **2-3 estimates or claims that YOU personally wrote.** We would prefer to see different types of losses if possible. Examples: * Water mitigation invoice * Reconstruction estimate * Fire estimate * Roofing estimate **If you will feel more comfortable, please remove or redact customer names, addresses, claim numbers, phone numbers, and any other confidential information before submitting them.** We want to evaluate: * Estimate organization * Level of detail * Line-item selection * F9 notes * Scope completeness * Supporting explanations * Estimating strategy * Overall professionalism Do not submit someone else's work. We will know as soon as we get you to the interview stage Be prepared to explain the estimates you submit during your interview. --- # 4. RECORD A 3-5 MINUTE LOOM VIDEO Send us a Loom video introducing yourself. Your video should explain: * Who you are * Your restoration estimating background * Your Xactimate experience * Your Symbility experience, if applicable * Types of claims you have worked on * Your experience dealing with adjusters * Your experience writing supplements * What you believe separates an average estimator from an excellent estimator * Why you believe you would be a strong fit * What you want your career to look like over the next 2-3 years **Please keep the video between 3 and 5 minutes.** We are not judging video production quality. We want to understand how you communicate, how well you understand estimating, and whether you would be a good fit working directly with our team. --- # IMPORTANT We expect a lot from the person we hire, but we also want to create a position that the right person will want to stay in for years. We are looking for someone who wants: * Stability * Growth * More responsibility * Increased income * A strong team * A company that is continually improving * The opportunity to become an expert in their field If you are an experienced restoration estimator who knows Xactimate extremely well and wants an opportunity to grow with an established restoration company, we want to hear from you. **Remember:** * Read the entire posting. * Put **ESTIMATOR** **HIRING MANAGER** in your application title. * Answer all 20 questions. * Submit 2-3 examples of estimates YOU personally created. * Submit your 3-5 minute Loom video. * Follow every instruction. **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**

title: Customer Service, Sales & Booking VA — Excellent Australian Communication Required
job_title: Customer Service, Sales & Booking VA — Excellent Australian Communication Required
description: I’m looking for a highly capable Virtual Assistant to help manage customer enquiries, sales, bookings, follow-ups and daily administration for a busy Australian service-based business. This is NOT a basic admin role. You will communicate directly with customers, qualify enquiries, help convert genuine enquiries into bookings, manage deposits and booking information, follow up potential customers and keep our daily trackers and booking dashboards accurate. Because you will represent the business directly, excellent communication skills are essential. AUSTRALIAN COMMUNICATION STYLE IS ESSENTIAL You must be able to communicate naturally and comfortably with Australian customers. Australian customers generally prefer communication that is: - Warm and conversational - Friendly but professional - Direct and easy to understand - Less formal - Concise - Human and personalised - Focused on answering the actual question being asked I am specifically NOT looking for someone who relies heavily on: - Scripted or canned responses - Generic customer service language - Overly formal communication - Excessive apologising - Long explanations when a short answer will do - AI-generated sounding responses - Repeating information that hasn't resolved the customer's question - Acknowledging a customer without actually solving their issue If a customer asks three questions, I expect all three questions to be answered. If a customer becomes confused or frustrated, I expect you to recognise it, reread the conversation, identify what hasn't been resolved and adjust your response accordingly. You need to understand what the customer is actually asking — not simply respond to keywords or follow a script. YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES You will manage enquiries from initial contact through to confirmed booking. This includes determining: - What day and time the customer wants - Which service they are interested in - Whether they want any extras - Whether they have requested something that isn't offered - How to appropriately handle requests for unavailable services - Whether the customer appears genuine, needs more time or is wasting time - Whether they are ready and willing to pay the required deposit - Whether the deposit has been paid and received - Whether the booking has been confirmed - Whether the correct address and booking information has been sent You will also be responsible for: - Responding to ALL enquiries during your working hours - Responding to new AND ongoing conversations within approximately 10 minutes - Following up genuine enquiries - Helping convert enquiries into bookings - Managing booking communication - Maintaining professional boundaries - Updating the Daily Enquiry Tracker - Updating the Weekly Bookings Dashboard - Keeping customer and booking information accurate - Knowing when something should be escalated to me PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS I expect: - 100% of enquiries responded to during working hours - Responses generally within 10 minutes - Customer questions answered correctly and completely - Customers properly qualified before booking - Booking procedures followed accurately - Daily Enquiry Tracker completed - Weekly Bookings Dashboard kept up to date - Warm, natural and conversational communication - Minimal avoidable customer complaints - Accurate customer and booking information Accuracy and communication quality are more important than simply sending a large number of messages. WHO I'M LOOKING FOR You will be a strong fit if you: - Have excellent written English - Understand Australian conversational communication - Communicate naturally rather than sounding scripted - Have strong customer service and sales skills - Have appointment-setting or booking experience - Understand how to qualify leads - Can recognise buying signals and time-wasters - Have excellent attention to detail - Can work independently - Know when to solve something yourself and when to escalate - Can handle frustrated customers calmly - Learn quickly from feedback - Take responsibility for mistakes - Do not need constant supervision Experience working with Australian businesses or Australian customers will be highly regarded. LONG-TERM OPPORTUNITY A generous long-term benefits and bonus package is available to high-performing candidates after 6 months of successful continuous engagement. IMPORTANT This is a customer-facing position. You will eventually be trusted with direct access to customer conversations and booking systems, so reliability, judgement, confidentiality and attention to detail are essential. You will not receive full access immediately. Successful applicants will first complete an interview and practical assessment so I can evaluate how you communicate, think and handle real customer situations. STRICT NO-AI POLICY The use of generative AI is strictly prohibited throughout the application, interview and assessment process for this role. This includes tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or similar tools used to write, rewrite, improve, translate, formulate or generate any part of your application or interview responses. I need to assess YOUR genuine communication skills, judgement, English ability and ability to respond naturally to customers. Any applicant found to have used generative AI during the recruitment process will be automatically disqualified. The same policy applies throughout your engagement if you are selected for the role. Unauthorised use of generative AI in customer communications will be treated as a serious breach of the role requirements and will result in immediate termination of your contractor engagement. If you rely on accessibility or assistive technology for a disability, please let me know so that an appropriate accommodation can be considered. HOW TO APPLY Please do NOT send me a generic cover letter. I want to see how you actually communicate. At the beginning of your application, write: “I understand Australian communication.” Then answer the following questions in your own words: 1. A customer sends you three different questions in one message. What would you do to make sure you don't a ---------- answer only one or two of them? 2. A customer has asked the same question twice because your previous response didn't properly answer what they were asking. They now sound frustrated. How would you handle it? 3. What are some signs that a customer is becoming frustrated during a written conversation? 4. What is the difference between acknowledging a customer's concern and actually resolving it? 5. How would you communicate with an Australian customer differently from a very formal corporate customer? Customer Scenario A customer messages: "I've already told you twice that I want Saturday afternoon. I just need to know whether 3pm is available and how much the deposit is. I don't need all the other information again." Write the EXACT response you would send to this customer. Keep it short and natural. Do not tell me what you would say. Write the actual message you would send. Please answer these questions yourself rather than giving me generic or AI-generated responses. If your communication style is overly scripted, extremely formal or does not directly answer the questions above, you will not progress to the next stage.

description: Senior Python AI Agent Developer (LangGraph, RAG, pgvector) TYPE OF WORK: Full Time SALARY: $ ---------- USD per month, based on demonstrated experience HOURS PER WEEK: 40-50 BEFORE YOU APPLY Put your one-paragraph answer to Question 1 at the very top of your message. Applications that do not start with that answer are deleted unread. We are not being difficult, we just get a lot of copy-paste applications and this is the fastest way to find the people who actually do this work. ABOUT HEARTSTAMP HeartStamp is a US AI-native greeting card platform. People create a one-of-a-kind card with us and we print and mail it to the door, or deliver it as an animated digital card. We launched in the US in 2026 and we are shipping fast. We are a small distributed team and every engineer owns a real part of the product. THE ROLE We are hiring a Senior Python AI Agent Developer to work on Stampy, our conversational card assistant, with a clear path to owning it end to end. Stampy is not a simple chatbot. It is a stateful, tool-using agent that understands what a customer wants, searches a live catalogue of tens of thousands of cards, drives image generation, and hands off into a print-ready pipeline. It is the product. The hard part of this job is not getting a model to answer. It is making the answer reliable. Did the captured intent survive the handoff. Did the right tool get called with the right value. Does the flow recover when the model drifts. Can you prove any of it with an evaluation suite instead of guessing. If you have shipped agents to real users, you already know that the failures that hurt are the confident wrong answers, not the crashes. You will work directly with our Tech Lead and Principal Engineer, and you will own decisions, not just tickets. THE HARD PART Read this section carefully. It is the real job and it is what we will talk about if we speak. A conversational agent and a product catalogue speak different languages. The agent can express far more than any storefront has pages for, and the translation between those two vocabularies is where agent products quietly break. Not with errors. With plausible answers that are wrong. The layer that turns what a customer means into catalogue state, and keeps both vocabularies honest with each other, is the highest-value thing you will own here. Getting it right is mostly not a model problem. It is a contract problem, a state problem, and an evaluation problem. If that sounds interesting rather than tedious, we should talk. WHAT YOU WILL DO The agent layer - Build and maintain stateful, tool-using LLM workflows in LangChain and LangGraph: structured outputs, routing, checkpoints and memory, approval gates, multi-step flows. - Own the deterministic layer around the model: reliable slot and state capture, stage gating, guarding tool calls, and graceful recovery when the model goes off track. - Integrate multiple LLM providers (OpenAI, Google Gemini, Vertex AI, OpenRouter, xAI) with model selection, prompt versioning, rate limit handling and fallbacks. We are model agnostic on purpose. - Manage interactive performance: per-turn latency budgets, response streaming, prompt caching, model routing for sub-tasks, and cost versus speed trade-offs. Retrieval - Build and tune our RAG pipeline on pgvector: embeddings, HNSW indexing, chunking and metadata design, hybrid retrieval, ranking, relevance tuning, and fallback strategies. - Retrieval that serves a real catalogue with real inventory, not a document question and answer demo. The resolution layer - The mapping between conversational intent and catalogue state: occasion slugs, recipient and filter tokens, style tokens, and the routes they resolve to. - Keeping the agent's vocabulary and the storefront's vocabulary in sync, as a checked contract rather than a runtime guess. - Round-trip guarantees: if we put a value in a URL, reading it back gives you the choice that produced it. Proving it works - pytest, async tests, mocked external services, and agent evaluation suites. - Golden datasets, automated behavioral tests, retrieval metrics, LLM-as-a-judge, and production feedback loops. - Structured logging, tracing, error monitoring, and LLM tracing with LangSmith. You will also work in - FastAPI: async APIs, Pydantic, REST design, auth, error handling, integration tests. - PostgreSQL with SQLAlchemy or SQLModel, and query performance. - Celery and Redis for background AI pipelines: retries, idempotency, backfills, long-running jobs. We have people who own the infrastructure, so you do not need to be deep here, but you need to be comfortable. REQUIREMENTS - At least 5 years of professional Python engineering, including owning production services. - At least 2 years building LLM features, agent workflows, semantic search, or RAG systems that real customers used. - Real experience shipping retrieval on PostgreSQL and pgvector, not only prototype chatbots. - Solid FastAPI experience inside a distributed system of APIs, workers, queues and third party services. - Experience evaluating AI output quality using golden datasets, behavioral tests, retrieval metrics, or LLM-as-a-judge. - Good judgment on reliability: provider outages, model failures, retries, graceful degradation, and feature-flagged rollouts. - Comfortable with Docker, CI/CD, and AWS. - Strong written English. You will be arguing about architecture in Slack with senior engineers and writing design notes people act on. - Able to overlap at least 4 hours daily with 9am to 5pm US Eastern Time. This is required, not preferred. NICE TO HAVE - Enough TypeScript to follow a bug across the boundary. Some of our worst defects live half in Python and half in the frontend filter state. You do not need to be a React developer, but you need to be able to read it. - Multimodal AI, especially image generation or image understanding pipelines. Strongly preferred. - DeepEval, LangSmith evaluations, Sentry, or PostHog. - S3-compatible storage, image moderation, or content safety. - A consumer product where AI output directly drives a purchase or a creative result. WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT - Not a prompt writing role. We already have a prompt engineer and a card library team. - Not a research role. What you build ships to customers this quarter. - Not a rebuild from scratch. The platform is live. You are strengthening and extending it. - Not an infrastructure role. We have a DevOps engineer and a principal engineer who own that. SCREENING QUESTIONS Short and specific beats long and general. Applications without answers will not be reviewed. 1. An agent captures the user's intent correctly, the value is present and correct in the request, and the user still gets the wrong result. Nothing errors and all tests pass. How do you find this, and what check do you add so it cannot happen again? 2. Describe an evaluation suite you built for an agent or retrieval system. What did it assert, how often did it run, and what did it catch that a unit test would not? 3. You have a multi-step conversation where the model sometimes skips a required step. How do you make it reliable without making it feel scripted? 4. Describe a retrieval system you shipped on PostgreSQL and pgvector. What was the corpus, how did you chunk it, and how did you know the ranking was good? 5. What are your current working hours, and what overlap can you commit to with 9am to 5pm US Eastern? HOW TO APPLY Answer to Question 1 at the very top of your message. Then your resume, a link to production work you can talk about in detail, and your answers to the rest. We review daily and move fast. Strong candidates get a short paid trial task: a small, self-contained problem drawn from the kind of work you would actually be doing. About two hours, paid at your rate, and it is the closest thing to the actual job we can show you before we commit.

title: Klaviyo Email Marketing Specialist — Full-Time, Hourly, Long-Term
job_title: Klaviyo Email Marketing Specialist — Full-Time, Hourly, Long-Term
description: To be clear up front: this is hourly-paid, full-time, long-term work. Not a one-off project, not a "few hours when there's something to do" gig. There is a steady pipeline of stores every single week, and we're hiring someone to own it for the long run. About the role We operate a portfolio of 100+ e-commerce stores across multiple markets (US, UK, AU, NL, SE, NO, FI, PL and more). Every store runs the same three-stage email program, and you own all of it: 1. Every new store at launch — Klaviyo account, verified sending domain, and an automated post-delivery review-request email live from supplier. 2. Stores that hit a revenue threshold — a full flow set cloned from an existing store in the same market, rebranded and set live. 3. Top-performing stores — seasonal campaigns (Black Week, Christmas, January sale, Valentine's) built once as a master and rolled out per store. The core working principle: we clone, we don't build from scratch. Templates, flows and campaigns already exist for every market. Your job is to duplicate them, rebrand them flawlessly, test them end to end, and keep the tracking board accurate. Volume and precision matter more than creative flair here. What you'll do + Set up new stores in Klaviyo — create the account, connect Shopify, confirm order and fulfillment events are flowing in. + Configure sending domains — dedicated sending domain per store, DNS records completed until fully verified, sender identity on the store's own domain. + Launch review-request automations — cloned from a same-market store, rebranded, triggered after delivery, tested end to end before go-live. + Clone and localize full flow sets — welcome, abandoned checkout, browse abandonment, post-purchase. Same market only; branding, links, codes and settings all mirrored and verified. + Build and roll out seasonal campaigns — one master campaign duplicated across top stores, segmented to engaged audiences, scheduled per market and timezone, results logged. + Rebrand with zero leakage — after every clone, search every email for the source store's name. Zero hits allowed before go-live. Wrong logo, wrong link or a stale brand name reaching a customer is the failure mode we're hiring against. + Test everything — preview sent, every link clicked, discount code redeemed in checkout, trigger fired, mobile rendering checked. "It's live" is not the same as "it works." + Keep the board updated in real time — with 100+ stores, the project board is how the whole team sees coverage. A step isn't done until it's verified and logged. + Protect deliverability and compliance — suppression lists respected, working unsubscribe in every send, review requests only to real customers who received their order, and never worded to ask for a positive rating. What we're looking for * Required - Hands-on Klaviyo experience — accounts, flows, campaigns, segments, templates, and the settings behind them (triggers, filters, delays, smart sending). - Sending domain / DNS setup — you've added a dedicated sending domain and completed SPF/DKIM/CNAME records to verified, without hand-holding. - Shopify familiarity — the Klaviyo integration, discount codes, and how order/fulfillment events map into flows. - High-volume, checklist-driven discipline. This is repetitive work done at scale. We need someone who runs the same checklist on store #94 as carefully as on store #3. - Reliable full-time availability with a fixed daily overlap window, and daily communication in written English. - Trustworthy with account access across a large portfolio. * Nice to have - Experience managing email across many brands or accounts (agency background works well). - Email deliverability knowledge — warming, engaged-segment strategy, list hygiene. - Multi-market experience (multiple languages/currencies). - Familiarity with Monday.com or a similar project board. What we offer + Full-time, paid bi-weekly. + Consistent, predictable workload. New stores launch continuously — the pipeline doesn't dry up. + A long-term position, not a trial project. We want someone to grow into owning email across the whole portfolio. + Documented SOPs, existing templates and reference stores for every market — you won't be inventing the process. + Clear ownership: email coverage across the portfolio is your number. How to apply Send a short application including: 1. Your Klaviyo experience — roughly how many accounts have you set up or managed, and in what kind of setup (agency, in-house, freelance)? 2. Walk me through setting up a dedicated sending domain in Klaviyo — which records you add and how you confirm it's actually verified. A few sentences is enough. 3. Your process for cloning a flow set from one store to another — specifically, how you make sure nothing from the source store leaks into the new one. 4. Availability — hours per week, time zone, daily overlap you can commit to, and earliest start date. Start your message with the word "CLONE" so we know you read the full post. Applications that skip questions 1–4 won't be reviewed. Everyone who answers them gets a reply.

job_title: TikTok & Instagram Short-Form Video Editor — UGC & Social Content
description: # TikTok & Instagram Short-Form Video Editor — UGC & Social Content I’m looking for a **creative, reliable short-form video editor** who understands how to turn raw clips into engaging TikTok and Instagram Reels. This is **not a long-form editing position**. I’m specifically looking for someone who understands short-form content, can work from references, and knows how to **combine different clips together to create a complete, natural-flowing video**. ## What You’ll Be Editing My content can vary, but it will primarily include: * School/education-related content * Trading/finance-related content * Websites and online tools * UGC-style videos * Talking-head clips * Screen recordings and website demonstrations * Short-form promotional/content videos I have a folder with **pre-recorded clips that you can use**, including: * Different intros/hooks * Middle clips showing websites or other content * Several outro clips * UGC-style templates I regularly record For example, I have a recurring video format where I introduce **3 websites that people have been gatekeeping**, and then show the websites throughout the video. If I need a **specific clip, intro, or outro** that isn't already in the folder, I can record it and provide it to you. ## Working From Inspiration This is a **very important part of the role**. I’ll provide you with **accounts and specific videos that I want my content to feel similar to**. Your job is to study the references and do your best to replicate the **editing style, pacing, structure, captions, transitions, and overall feel** while applying it to my own footage. I don't expect an exact copy. I want you to understand the creative direction and make the best version possible with the footage available. Ideally, I want to be able to send: **My clips + an inspiration video/account + basic instructions** …and have you put everything together without needing me to explain every individual cut. ## Editing Style I’m looking for editing that feels **native to TikTok/Reels** and keeps people watching. You should understand how to use: * Strong hooks * Fast but natural cuts * Removing unnecessary pauses * Punch-ins and zooms * Screen recordings * B-roll * Images and graphics * Pattern interrupts * Sound effects * Music when appropriate * Creative transitions * Good pacing and retention A major part of the job will be **making separate clips gel together naturally** so the final video feels like one cohesive piece of content. ### Captions Captions are important and need to be clean and properly timed. My supervisors require captions to generally be formatted at **2–3 words per line**, rather than large blocks of text. Captions should be easy to read, visually engaging, and consistent throughout the video. ## What I’m Looking For I’m not just looking for someone who knows how to use CapCut or Premiere Pro. I want someone who has a **creative eye** and can look at my footage and figure out how to make it more engaging. You should be: * Creative * Reliable and responsive * Fast and efficient * Good at following references * Comfortable making your own editing decisions * Good at combining different clips * Familiar with TikTok/Reels editing * Detail-oriented * Able to meet quick deadlines ## Workflow & Availability I’ll provide the footage through an **organized Google Drive folder** with the available clips, hooks, website footage, outros, and templates. I typically need around **4–5 videos per day**, although this can vary depending on the workload. I generally need videos returned within **10–12 hours**, or faster whenever possible, because I need to submit them to my supervisors for approval. The workload can range around **30–40 hours per week**, depending on how many videos need to be completed. ## Pay & Long-Term Opportunity The starting rate is **$4 USD per completed video**. I’m looking for someone who can potentially work with me **long term** and become familiar with my content style. The goal is to eventually make the process very simple: **Clips + inspiration + instructions → Finished TikTok/Reel** ## How to Apply Please send: 1. Your short-form editing portfolio 2. **3–5 of your BEST TikTok/Reels/UGC edits** 3. Your editing software 4. Typical turnaround time 5. Availability 6. How many videos you can realistically edit per day/week 7. Confirmation that you’re comfortable with **$4 USD per completed video** **Please don’t send 50+ videos.** Send the **3–5 edits that best demonstrate your ability to create engaging, creative short-form content.** I’m looking for someone who can take my existing clips, understand the style I’m going for, and **turn them into content that actually feels like it belongs on TikTok.**

description: FINE Group Entertainment We are a global entertainment group working across music, comedy and other ventures. Reading the data daily and moving spend to what is working, not to what was working last week. Owning the reporting that tells us what a campaign actually returned. The AI Building on agents that do defined jobs and then proving they do them well. That means designing them and scoping a task narrowly enough that an agent can understand it, writing the prompts and system instructions, wiring them into the data they need, whether that is the ad platform APIs, our sheets, our dashboards or our own content library. Agents that watch creative fatigue and tell us when an asset is burning out. Agents that generate and vary ad copy and hooks at volume, then rank the variants. Utilizing your own taste and gut feel along with real data from agents that can watch long-form sets, podcasts, sessions, interviews and short-form and score the clips against our external creative team clips for likely performance before we spend. Agents that analyze sentiment at scale across our clients and tell us what is actually landing. Agents that tag creative by attribute so we can see which attributes drive performance rather than guessing. What you need Real, demonstrable AI fluency. You prompt well, you know what these tools can and cannot do, and you have built things with them that other people use. Deep hands-on experience running paid social and search with real budgets. A sharp eye for creative that performs, and the judgement to kill your own work when the data says so. Comfort with data and the habit of proving what worked rather than asserting it. The pace to keep up in a business running several things at once. Nice to have Experience in music, entertainment or media. Short-form video and clipping know-how. Any coding or automation background with Python, APIs, Zapier, n8n, or whatever you have used to make systems talk to each other. Experience writing evals or testing model output systematically. Grokbot, Claude, Open AI experience as well. Why this one is different You will not be plugging campaigns into someone else's playbook. There is no perfected existing AI stack here for you to inherit and maintain. Instead you are taking the native tools we have created and systematically improving on them. Real tools, real budgets, real room to shape how we do this. If you want to be at the point where AI and marketing actually meet, rather than posting about it. Then tell us about one agent or automation you have built, what it does, and how you know it works. Show us examples and evidence. title: L1 Help Desk Technician for MSP
job_title: L1 Help Desk Technician for MSP
description: About Simple IT Simple IT is a U.S.-based managed service provider (MSP) — we’re the outsourced IT department for small and mid-sized businesses. We manage their networks, security, and day-to-day tech support so they can focus on running their business. We’re a small, close-knit team that takes real pride in doing IT support right: clear communication, real fixes, and a genuinely good experience for the people who call us. The role As our L1 Help Desk Technician, you’re the first voice our clients hear when something isn’t working. You’ll handle the day-to-day tickets that make up most of a service desk’s work — password resets, printer issues, email problems, new-computer setup, and general troubleshooting — following our documented procedures. When something is genuinely beyond L1, you’ll hand it up cleanly to our L2 technician — and early on, that will happen often. That’s expected, not a shortfall: you’re not expected to know everything on day one, and recognizing what you don’t know is exactly the skill we’re hiring for. You’ll start with a structured onboarding — shadowing our team, working tickets without phone pressure while you build confidence, and moving to live calls only once you and your mentor agree you’re ready. Support and coaching continue well past your first week. What you’ll do ● Answer client calls and emails professionally, and work the ticket queue for common, repeatable issues — password resets, printer setup, email troubleshooting, new-computer deployment, and license/account requests ● Follow our written procedures (SOPs) to resolve issues consistently and correctly ● Verify who you’re talking to before making any sensitive change — security is part of every ticket, not a separate task ● Document clearly as you work — what you tried, what you found, and how it was resolved — so any teammate could pick up where you left off ● Recognize when an issue is outside L1 and hand it off cleanly with the details our L2 technician needs to take it from there ● Keep clients informed while their ticket is open, so nobody is left wondering what’s happening What we’re looking for ● Help desk or technical support experience — IT support, a call center technical support role, or equivalent hands-on troubleshooting experience. New to formal IT support but genuinely strong with computers and a fast learner? Tell us in your application. ● Comfortable on the phone in English — clear, fluent spoken and written English, with the ability to communicate calmly and professionally with U.S.-based clients by phone, email and ticket notes, even when they're frustrated. ● Working knowledge of Windows, Microsoft 365, and everyday business software — you don’t need to be an expert, but you should be comfortable finding your way around them. ● A genuine troubleshooter’s mindset — you ask questions to find the real problem rather than guessing, and you’re honest when you’re stuck rather than pretending you’re not. ● Reliable equipment & workspace — you’ll need a quiet, professional workspace in a private room; a computer capable of running our support tools (multi-monitor setup preferred) with a battery backup (UPS) to protect against power interruptions; a quality headset; high-speed internet (50 Mbps or more), with a backup connection preferred; and a webcam for interviews and team calls. We’ll clarify during the interview which tools and accounts Simple IT provides versus what you’re expected to bring. ● Coachable. You’ll get real-time feedback in your first months, especially on calls. We’re looking for someone who takes that well and improves from it. What success looks like We built a structured 90-day ramp so you’re never guessing what’s expected. Early on, you’ll work common tickets off the phone with close support, then move to calls with a mentor listening in, and progress to working independently as you demonstrate you’re ready — on your timeline, not an arbitrary one. By the end of that ramp, we’d expect you to handle most of your own call and ticket volume, resolving the majority of what comes in, and escalating the right things for the right reasons. Growing into backend work Once you’re steady on tickets and calls, the role widens. This isn’t day-one work — it comes in as you build confidence, the same way phones did. ● Coverage checks — confirming client devices are protected by the security tools we deploy, and following up on any gaps ● Patch verification — confirming client machines are up to date and flagging any that aren’t ● Documentation upkeep — keeping client and device records accurate, so what we know about a client’s environment stays current and correct As you build skills and demonstrate ownership, additional technical responsibilities and advancement opportunities become available over time — we’re looking for someone who wants a long-term home, not just a first job. Is this role a fit? This role may be a good fit if you enjoy helping non-technical users, stay calm when a client is frustrated, are comfortable following documented processes, and would rather ask for help than guess. This role may not be a good fit if you dislike phone support, prefer project work over ticket work, struggle with detailed documentation, or aren't comfortable working U.S. business hours. title: Google Ads Manager
description: WE’RE HIRING: GOOGLE ADS SPECIALIST Full-Time | Work From Home | Philippines We’re looking for an absolute Google Ads expert to join our full-time remote team. This is not a junior role and it’s not a role for someone who has simply “managed Google Ads before.” We want someone who knows Google Ads inside out, can look at an account and quickly identify what’s working, what’s wasting money and what needs to change to generate more leads at a better cost. We are a marketing agency working heavily with trade and service businesses, so if you’ve previously managed Google Ads for electricians, plumbers, HVAC, builders, landscapers, pool companies or other home service businesses, that is a BIG bonus. WORK HOURS 7:00 AM – 3:00 PM Manila Time Monday to Friday Full-time, work from home Weekends and public holidays off WE’RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE LONG-TERM We already have a team of 15 employees based in the Philippines, and most of our team members have been with us for a minimum of five years. We’re proud of that. We’re not looking for someone who wants another short-term remote job. We’re looking for someone who wants to become part of the team, master their role and stay with us long-term. THIS MUST BE YOUR FULL-TIME ROLE If you are planning to take this position as a second full-time job, particularly one that overlaps with these working hours, please do not apply. We need someone who is available, focused and committed to our team during the agreed working hours. We have been working with our Philippines team for years, so we understand how remote teams work and what genuine full-time commitment looks like. If we discover during your first 90 days that you have another full-time role that conflicts with this position or that you have misrepresented your availability, your employment with us will be terminated. Please be upfront from the beginning. WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING You’ll be responsible for the performance of Google Ads accounts across our client portfolio. That includes: * Building Google Ads campaigns from scratch * Auditing and restructuring existing accounts * Search campaign management * Performance Max * Display and remarketing * Keyword research and search term management * Negative keyword strategy * Writing and testing ad copy * Conversion tracking and troubleshooting * Budget and bidding strategy * Improving CPL, conversion rates and ROAS * Identifying wasted spend * Analysing landing page performance and recommending improvements * Monitoring campaigns and making proactive optimisations * Producing clear performance reports * Explaining WHY performance has changed, not simply reporting the numbers * Working closely with our marketing, content and development teams YOU MUST HAVE * Strong hands-on Google Ads experience * Google Ads certification * Excellent understanding of conversion tracking * Strong knowledge of GA4 and Google Tag Manager * Experience managing lead-generation campaigns * Strong analytical and problem-solving skills * The ability to confidently audit an account and explain what you would change * Excellent written and spoken English * Experience working remotely with a team * Confidence using Google Docs and reporting tools Microsoft Ads experience is a bonus. Previous experience with trades, home services or local service businesses is a BIG advantage. WHAT YOU WON’T BE DOING You won’t be writing blogs or social media content. You won’t be designing or building landing pages. We already have content, design and development teams. Your job is Google Ads performance. IMPORTANT: PLEASE DO NOT APPLY WITHOUT PROOF OF YOUR WORK We are hiring an expert, so before Stephanie meets anyone for an interview, we need to see evidence that you know what you’re doing. TO APPLY Use the subject line: AdsPro4Stef2026 Please send us: 1. A short video introducing yourself. Tell us who you are, how long you’ve been managing Google Ads and the types of accounts you specialise in. 2. Show us your work. Share your screen in the video and walk us through a Google Ads account or campaign you have worked on. Please remove or hide any confidential client information. Show us things like: * Campaign structure * Spend * Leads/conversions * Cost per lead * Conversion rate * What wasn’t working * What YOU changed * What happened to performance after your changes We don’t just want screenshots of a good ROAS. We want to hear you explain the account and demonstrate that you understand WHY it performed. 3. Tell us about your experience with lead generation. If you’ve managed Google Ads for trade businesses, home services or local service businesses before, please show us those examples. 4. Include your CV/resume and your expected monthly salary in PHP. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT We will review your application and video first. If your experience and results look strong, you’ll move to the next stage where we’ll give you a real Google Ads account to review. We want you to show us what you see, what you would change and why. Only after that stage will shortlisted candidates be invited to interview with Stephanie. No video = no interview. If you’re genuinely excellent at Google Ads, want one full-time role with a stable, long-term team and can prove your skills, we’d love to hear from you. I’ll pay the right candidate the right money to get them into the team. I want a forever hire.

title: Level 3 Network Architect
description: Network Engineer (Level 3) — On-Call / As-Needed Location: Fully Remote (Ph) Schedule: As needed. You will be contacted via WhatsApp when advanced tickets requiring these skills come through. Hours: Availability during US East Coast business hours (EST) when engaged Engagement Type: Ongoing as-needed contractor — this is not a full-time salaried position Compensation: [RATE TO BE INSERTED] About T3 Tech Partners T3 Tech Partners is a US-based company and the team MSPs rely on when challenges exceed Tier 2 or internal expertise. We operate as a Fractional Tier 3 partner, delivering advanced Systems Administration, infrastructure, cloud, network, and security expertise to MSPs supporting diverse client environments. Our engineers are trusted technical partners — leading implementations, resolving complex escalations, and working directly with MSP clients to execute real-world solutions. Role Overview We are seeking a senior-level Network Engineer to serve as an on-call escalation resource for complex networking issues across our MSP partners' client environments. This is an as-needed engagement, not a scheduled full-time role. When an advanced network ticket comes through that requires this skill set, we will reach out to you directly via WhatsApp. You are expected to acknowledge quickly and, when you accept the work, engage during US East Coast business hours until the issue is resolved or handed back. This structure suits someone who already has a primary role or an independent consulting practice and wants additional senior-level work on a flexible basis. It does not suit someone who needs guaranteed weekly hours or predictable income. This role requires strong technical depth, independence, and the ability to step into an unfamiliar network with limited documentation and orient yourself quickly. Key Responsibilities Advanced Network Escalation Support Take ownership of advanced and expert-level network escalations passed up from MSP Tier 1 and Tier 2 teams. Diagnose complex connectivity, performance, latency, and packet loss issues across LAN, WAN, and hybrid environments. Perform root-cause analysis and implement durable fixes rather than temporary workarounds. Work directly with MSP technicians and, where required, end customers to execute resolutions. Document findings, changes made, and recommendations at the close of every engagement. Firewalls & Network Security Configure, troubleshoot, and optimize enterprise firewalls including Fortinet FortiGate, SonicWall, Cisco, Meraki, Palo Alto, and similar platforms. Design and troubleshoot site-to-site IPsec VPNs, SSL VPNs, and remote access solutions. Implement network segmentation, VLAN isolation, and access control policies. Configure and tune IDS/IPS, content filtering, geo-blocking, and threat protection features. Review and remediate firewall rule bases for security and performance. Routing, Switching & Wireless Configure and troubleshoot managed switching including VLANs, trunking, spanning tree, link aggregation, QoS, and PoE. Work with static routing, policy-based routing, and dynamic routing protocols (OSPF, BGP) as environments require. Deploy, tune, and troubleshoot enterprise wireless environments (Meraki, Ubiquiti, Ruckus, Aruba, Cisco). Perform wireless coverage, roaming, interference, and density troubleshooting. Diagnose DNS, DHCP, NAT, and IP addressing issues. WAN, Circuits & Cloud Connectivity Troubleshoot ISP circuits, hand-offs, and carrier issues, and manage escalations with providers. Configure and support SD-WAN deployments, failover, and multi-WAN load balancing. Build and troubleshoot hybrid connectivity into Azure, including virtual networks, VPN gateways, and site-to-site tunnels. Support network requirements for Microsoft 365 workloads, including QoS for Teams voice and video. Assist with network cutovers, ISP migrations, and office relocations. Analysis & Documentation Perform packet captures and protocol analysis (Wireshark or equivalent) to isolate difficult issues. Produce or update network diagrams, IP schemes, and configuration documentation as part of engagement close-out. Provide clear written summaries that an MSP Tier 2 technician can act on and learn from. Recommend standards and long-term improvements to MSP partners where appropriate. Availability & Engagement Expectations You will be contacted via WhatsApp when a qualifying ticket comes in. Acknowledgement is expected within a reasonable window during US East Coast business hours. You are free to decline any individual engagement, but consistent unavailability will end the arrangement. When you accept an engagement, you are expected to work it through to resolution or to a clean hand-off. Some work may fall outside standard hours for maintenance windows, cutovers, or critical outages. These are scheduled in advance where possible. Volume varies. Some weeks will bring multiple escalations, others none. Qualifications Required Experience 5+ years of hands-on network engineering experience, with significant time in an MSP or multi-client environment. Expert-level proficiency with enterprise firewall platforms (Fortinet, SonicWall, Cisco, Meraki, Palo Alto, or comparable). Strong command of routing and switching fundamentals, VLANs, VPN technologies, and network troubleshooting methodology. Demonstrated ability to resolve issues that Tier 2 teams could not. Experience with packet capture and protocol-level analysis. Comfort working in unfamiliar environments with incomplete documentation. Excellent native-level English communication, written and verbal. You will be speaking directly with US-based MSP technicians and client stakeholders, often under pressure during an outage. Reliable high-speed internet, a backup power source, and a quiet workspace suitable for client calls. Proven experience working in MSP environments (required). Preferred Experience Relevant certifications (Fortinet NSE, Cisco CCNP, Meraki CMNA, Palo Alto PCNSE, or similar). Azure networking and hybrid cloud connectivity experience. SD-WAN design and deployment experience. VoIP and unified communications network troubleshooting. Familiarity with Microsoft 365 network requirements and optimization. Scripting or automation experience for network configuration and auditing. HOW TO APPLY Please reply in the job post chat here on OnlineJobs.ph with the following: Your resume or a link to it. A specific example of a network escalation you resolved that another team could not. Describe the symptoms, how you isolated the cause, and what you did to fix it. Two or three paragraphs is enough. This is the part we read most closely. The firewall platforms you have the deepest experience with, and roughly how many deployments you have worked on for each. Your hourly rate in USD. Confirmation that you can be reached via WhatsApp and can engage during US East Coast business hours. Any relevant certifications, with dates. Candidates who move forward will complete a live technical conversation over video. Please be prepared to talk through your troubleshooting approach without notes.

callers -Clear coaching with measurable follow-through -Accurate reporting with no surprises -A disciplined, motivated, and accountable calling floor REQUIREMENTS -At least 3 years of outbound employment Experience with B2B appointment setting, lead generation, predictive or power dialers, and Philippine remote teams is strongly preferred.
